about: Songs pulled from music list posts, by post URL. Written by scripts/weekly.js songs.

songs.title: The Governor's Waltz
songs.note: A standout from LOST WEEKEND that jumps into the top 10 this week; the post also name-checks Elliott Smith's influence.

songs.title: Where Is Gone?
songs.note: Became the big topic in the music meeting; a reviewer called it intense, mature, and heavy-hitting. Taken from DOPAMINE CHAMBER.

songs.artist: Justice (feat. Tame Impala, King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, SZA)
songs.title: Flower In A Hurricane
songs.note: Debuts in Grand Theft Auto VI; some found it disco-y and poppy, with a heavy guitar riff recalling "Money for Nothing."

songs.title: nothing
songs.note: A heartbreak song; a listener described it as reaching for someone who was already over them for years.

songs.title: Swan Song
songs.note: Lead single from a upcoming b-sides collection, described as evocative and finely crafted, with urgency beneath a relaxed rhythm.

songs.title: Memphis
songs.note: A new track with tender emotion and intensity, inspired by a conversation with an ex-convict on a flight.

songs.title: Changelings
songs.note: Brooding, Lynchian single with an accompanying video, dark and eerie in tone.

songs.title: Damp
songs.note: Single about desire for connection, with taut urgency and longing vocals, described as uneasy and mournful.

songs.title: The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald
songs.note: Reverent, single-take cover of the Gordon Lightfoot song, marking its fiftieth anniversary.

songs.title: Please
songs.note: Lead single from the upcoming album Runoff, using samples and field recordings alongside a full band.

songs.title: Came Back Kicking
songs.note: Urgent lead single with Japandroids-esque momentum, offering affirming energy amid turmoil.

songs.title: Rafts
songs.note: Folk single from Songs From the Solent, exploring migratory bird decline with nature reserve samples.

songs.title: The Sound It Made
songs.note: Chaotic, abrasive opener from Two Wheels Move the Soul, with deadpan vocals about a changing world.

songs.title: Don't Be Good to Me
songs.note: Final single in a trilogy, earnest and sensual, exploring being shown kindness despite self-doubt.

songs.title: Vision
songs.note: Hypnotic, mantra-like track with repeated mystical images and a pulsing beat.

songs.title: Breakfast
songs.note: Infectious lo-fi single from the album Clipping, with a camcorder video.

songs.title: Punisher of Love
songs.note: Track on contemporary rat race pressures, with a video of a humanoid rat chasing a couple through Brooklyn.

songs.title: Anonymat
songs.note: Praised for its laid-back shatta groove produced by DJ Jyz, with shifting flows, "Sa ki fèt" chants, and a kompa keyboard outro.

songs.title: Devotion
songs.note: A desert blues-tinged track about compulsive limerence, one of the highlights of this dreamy psychedelic folk record.

songs.title: Everything
songs.note: A motorik psych number that the post says mines a desperation for meaning.

songs.title: Infinity Baby
songs.note: An exotica swing track where the artist confronts a childhood fear of the infinite; the post calls it a standout.

songs.title: Cold Bricks
songs.note: A slow crawl of hushed bass and guitar with the two vocalists reduced to a few spare, distant notes.

songs.title: Fade Thru
songs.note: A restrained, almost jazzy track with a dawdling approach, described as similarly subdued to the opener.

songs.title: King Kong
songs.note: A hyperkinetic jungle workout where the duo's vocals are pulverized beneath a stampede of percussion.

songs.title: Search and Destroy
songs.note: Woozy layered drum machine and keyboards create a dreamlike world, with a pressing electric bassline pulling the listener through. Hypnotic and ambiguous.

songs.title: Foyer
songs.note: New track previewing the Little Brain album, pairing wall-of-sound shoegaze with a more reflective, melancholic mood.

songs.title: Racehorse
songs.note: Emotive opener from the Thank You. No, Thank You EP, placing sincere vocals up front before deepening into something epic. About loss from the departed's perspective.

songs.title: Dark Out
songs.note: Jaunty, cool single with a toe-tapping brightness that masks underlying desperation, continuing the sleek style of recent albums.

songs.title: Peace
songs.note: Fleeting sub two-minute rock song, warm and intimate with bittersweet mystery, full of guitar, rambling percussion and fragmentary lyrics.

songs.title: The Mythical
songs.note: Lead single from the Bright Things I Found In The Dark EP, capturing childhood awakening as fairytale softness falls away.

songs.title: Kyle Hangs Ten
songs.note: B-side twin of Kyle Hangs At Noon with a faster tempo, a surf-style summer track written as swaggy country music.

songs.title: Out in the Rain
songs.note: New single from the upcoming solo album Near Divine or Merely Rhyme, elevating personal experience into something near spiritual.

songs.title: One Too Many Nights (feat. Sam Jr.)
songs.note: Lead single from the Happy Thought School record, a cathartic exploration of the unmooring caused by a relationship ending.

songs.title: Kansas Tornado
songs.note: A gentle folk ballad about surrendering to love, framed as a tornado, recorded around one microphone. Released August 5.

songs.title: Stop The Wedding!
songs.note: A writer praises this retro, ABBA-like song about a bride tempted to flee, especially its reworked final chorus lyrics.

songs.title: Someday
songs.note: An indie rock eruption asking what happens when we save our lives for later, with a Wonder Bread line central to its message.

songs.title: Fishes for the Seabirds
songs.note: A fingerpicked folk prayer from a frightened agnostic, pondering human horrors and what might come next.

songs.title: Since I Started
songs.note: A romantic ode to love with lyrics about laughing at death and a bluer ocean, from The Prince of Birchy Head.

songs.title: say anything
songs.note: A hopeful acoustic ballad from the 4 Songs EP, promising that struggles will pass and better weeks lie ahead.

songs.title: Orange Tree
songs.note: Built on a Japanese eighth-century poem and a Hirajoshi scale, it explores love as both blessing and quiet regret.

songs.title: Out
songs.note: The lead single from the debut EP, trading introspection for restless indie rock urgency about anxiety and avoidance.

songs.title: Into the Light
songs.note: A soulful serenade blending rock, Americana, and jam-band energy, with jazzy horns and smooth vocals.

songs.title: Algún día
songs.note: A dreamy indie folk song about mortality that turns into a call to be present and witness life now.

songs.title: Britney Spears
songs.note: A post-punk track about a singer testing many adult selves before realizing she likes the person she was.

https://stereogum.com/2300309/the-5-best.title: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week

songs.title: Misery
songs.note: A jazz-tinged rap track about the dizzying, almost hallucinatory rush of attraction, with hazy horns and unpredictable snares.

songs.title: Bonnet Of Pins
songs.note: The lead single from Berninger's next solo album, praised for its momentum, vivid backing vocals, and horn section.

songs.title: How Bad Do U Want Me
songs.note: A centerpiece of her album Mayhem, built on an interpolation of Yaz's "Only You" and framed as an ultimatum.

songs.title: Arrowhead
songs.note: A caffeinated, emphatic pop-punk comeback after years of dormancy, picking up where the band left off.

songs.title: This Is Real
songs.note: The Pittsburgh group's return after a hiatus, moving from twinkly indie rock into nu-metal and ricocheting between quiet and loud.

songs.title: Fallen
songs.note: A 2025 track where the Ipswich rapper mixes metal screams, nu-metal riffs and quick-witted rapping, with Jamaican Patois and Lion King references.

songs.title: Mmeeaanniinngg Bbuussiinneessss
songs.note: A highlight from this year's self-titled record, stretched into a 37-minute chamber drone that the post links to Dirty Three fans.

songs.title: White Flag
songs.note: A bassline house track from the duo's second album of this year, described as a wobbling, scruffy electrotrash cut with out-of-tune vocals.

songs.title: The Phone Call
songs.note: A shimmering ballad at the heart of Tjäder's experimental pop album Shelf Life, which began as a short story and became an opera.

songs.title: Stillwater
songs.note: Written by Isaac Eiger, with tumbling piano and weary barroom anthemics that the post compares to Alex G's hangdog beauty.

songs.title: Burls
songs.note: From Kiana Li's album Great Jobs, a muscular techno-skank track that moves through dub bass and drum'n'bass territory.

songs.title: Isn't It Nice (to Be Somebody)
songs.note: The Icelandic producer's comeback track, with regimented bass that flickers and feels playfully suggestive.

songs.title: Ascenda
songs.note: A minimal techno track with strong drama and propulsion, inspired by the Greek goddess Astraea who left corrupted humanity for the stars.

songs.title: Exposure
songs.note: Praised for the athletic saxophone scales that Aaron Shaw plays on this Indigo Garden track.

songs.title: The Blue Zone
songs.note: Described as having warm, metronomic tones and a pastoral feel, set on equal footing with Exposure.

songs.title: City of Fire
songs.note: A track on Indigo Garden that laments the loss of Black homes, with piano from Luca Mendoza.

songs.title: Change
songs.note: The writer singles out a lyric delivered on this Kizzy track as a personal favorite.

songs.title: Opaque Mist
songs.note: Closing track on Bleak Days Ahead that opens with a drum machine loop, piano, and clean vocals before guitars arrive.

songs.title: Bleak Days Ahead Pt. II
songs.note: A long epic on Bleak Days Ahead where monk-like singing and throat singing emerge after about six minutes.

https://stereogum.com/2304737/the-5-best.title: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week

songs.title: Waiting pt 1
songs.note: A house single written while she moved back home to focus on music; contemplative and danceable, a subtle jolt against stagnation.

songs.title: Closer To
songs.note: Lead single from their new album; Elliott Smith-like whispers over psych guitars that fall off into loopy trip-hop.

songs.title: Circles
songs.note: Playful, simple ditty with theatrical vocals and quick rhythm, reminiscent of early Wire; lead single from Musical Chairs.

songs.title: Monsieur Hawkweed
songs.note: Heedless, expressive energy with soaring harmonies and fuzzy guitars that zoom past genre categories.

songs.title: Tell Me I Never Knew That (Feat. Caroline Polachek)
songs.note: Polachek's airy voice blends seamlessly into caroline's textured strums and chimes, a delirious, intuitive pairing.

songs.title: Everything in the Shade
songs.note: Pitchfork's track review calls it a slippery, Laurel Canyon-meets-Copenhagen song from Fine's upcoming album Jazz Dreams, with a shifting root chord.

songs.title: PHX HOT BOY
songs.note: Sounds like a braggadocious trap anthem at first, but its lyrics trace JEFE's move from youthful partying to enlightenment.

songs.title: Get Ya Soul Right
songs.note: Rejects physical confrontation and backbiting in favor of spiritual elevation, and includes a verse the writer particularly likes.

songs.title: Fork/Heart
songs.note: Sophie Harris's expressive delivery here, mournful, menacing, and taunting, is singled out as best showing her range.

songs.title: Dashboard Mary
songs.note: A slow-build ballad that the writer calls an album showcase for Harris's narrative skill.

songs.title: Le couteau par la lame
songs.note: Named as a track that belongs on playlists for listeners curious about extreme metal who want catchy hooks.

songs.title: Volontaire
songs.note: Recommended alongside another track as a strong entry point into the band's extreme metal from Sans Adieu.

songs.title: #Faithful
songs.note: Built on a looped gospel sample that repeats "I need you," with lyrics about faith through desolate times.

songs.title: Without
songs.note: Built on a euphoric gospel sample, it works through difficult relationships and paraphrases 1 Corinthians 13.

songs.title: What Doesn't Serve You
songs.note: Drops to half speed for a headbanging finish in a 50-second song from the EP Coerced.

songs.title: False Pulse
songs.note: Extended textural experimentation that the post says hints at more ideas the band has yet to explore.

songs.title: LUSH
songs.note: Hypnotic minimalism with a repeated 'I see you and me' line, likened to a manifestation spell.

songs.title: LoveCrime
songs.note: Vocal track from Sound Therapy that deals with self-love, according to the post.

songs.title: Change 101
songs.note: Vocal track from Sound Therapy that deals with stability, according to the post.

songs.title: Kill Switch
songs.note: Throbbing techno rhythms that the post compares to pneumatic drills on Mind Abandon.

songs.title: Memory Leak
songs.note: Throbbing techno rhythms burrowing into a thin base layer of sound on Mind Abandon.

songs.title: Misted
songs.note: Thrums and pulses while strong toplines emerge from the fog, per the post.

songs.title: A Hidden Path
songs.note: A music-box-like melody sits above a subterranean groan on Mind Abandon.

songs.title: Gallows
songs.note: Centerpiece blanketed in lush synths, built around a swooping crystalline lead line.

songs.title: Threshold's Tragedy
songs.note: Album closer drenched in church-like organ that overpowers the stampeding guitars.

songs.title: Haderburg
songs.note: Guitar chords slur together into a single heartbreaking ribbon of sound, per the post.

songs.title: Harmless
songs.note: Title track of the upcoming album Harmless, built from a repeated set of questions about helplessness and complicity amid televised genocide and inequality.

songs.title: Lighter Blue
songs.note: Latest single from WATERBODIES, using geological imagery to consider how the will to create can illuminate life's shadowy paths.

songs.title: Bitter End
songs.note: Upbeat single reflecting on a break-up, pairing personal uncertainty with brightness and the tension between regret and letting go.

songs.title: Poppa
songs.note: Follow-up single from Throwing The Game, remembering Corey Laitman's grandfather and how dignity persists through later life and grief.

songs.title: Future Memory
songs.note: Closing track of Memories of the Future, a fatalistic yet clear-eyed reflection on a world in crisis and a failed collective imagination.

songs.title: Pearls
songs.note: New single with a video by William H. Travis showing most of the band gathered together, described as a perfect moment in time.

songs.title: Tough Luck
songs.note: Atmospheric, almost ethereal single about the comedy of circumstance and the mixed feelings of meeting an ex after a breakup.

songs.title: There Is A Way Home
songs.note: Single from part two of a double album wrestling with faith, depression and suicidal ideation while contemplating God amid pain.

songs.title: Howling World
songs.note: Lead single title track inspired by Magritte's painting Young Girl Eating a Bird, blending intimate emotion with an elemental atmosphere.
Album opener and lead single from Hold Time, exploring memory and time in a scrappy, raw way rather than hazy dreaminess.

songs.title: Òran Molaidh
songs.note: Sood weaves in a 1952 recording of his great-uncle, a Highland fiddler, restoring a voice history might have lost.

songs.title: Over In No Time
songs.note: One of the despondent-titled songs on a breakup album whose wistful, smoldering arrangements express the pain quietly.

songs.title: Giving You Up
songs.note: Another despondent-titled track from the breakup-inspired album, with subdued dynamics and quiet-storm R&B rhythms.

songs.title: Young Oldhead
songs.note: Defcee reflects on being a thirtysomething oldhead, waiting for an Uber home after a show.

songs.title: Heat Check
songs.note: Defcee describes himself at a four-way intersection with the other divorcees, over restrained beats from Dove.

songs.title: Alma
songs.note: Defcee writes rhymes in his head on the way to visit his daughter, in a plainspoken, autobiographical track.

songs.title: elmyra
songs.note: Opens with dollops of 1970s analog synth plinking out a robotic melody, shifting shape like a dream.

songs.title: soulless cycle
songs.note: About a minute in, it turns into a bone-rattling hardcore-style breakdown with battering drums and guitar explosions.

songs.title: Thinkingscape
songs.note: Tanpura drones over a plodding bassline from a Moog Grandmother, blending ancient and modern instruments.

songs.title: Astral Echoes
songs.note: The clarinet and JUNO 6 synth share a satisfying tonal similarity on this track.

songs.title: Girls
songs.note: A feminist song that the review says can come off a bit second wave, though the writing still impresses.

songs.title: Foremothers
songs.note: A feminist track whose messaging the review finds a bit second wave, mentioning witch burnings.

songs.title: Headfirst
songs.note: A jangling proto-punk song where Winder-Lind thanks God for all that she feels.

songs.title: You're Not An Angel
songs.note: Winder-Lind revels in being a body on this track from the Brighton singer-songwriter's solo debut.

songs.title: Grandma & Robert de Niro
songs.note: A piano ballad in which Winder-Lind questions your love for Bob Dylan.

songs.artist: Zach Bryan ft. Lana Del Rey
songs.title: Lies
songs.note: A weepy piano-and-strings duet that the reviewer finds sounds too much like Hozier, with a lyric-borrowing and awkward feel; calls it a little sad rather than

songs.title: I Danced With Another Love in My Dreams
songs.note: Track from Irreversible, a dreamstate infidelity tale with springy 80s-style guitar melodies and heart-skipping tempos.

songs.title: Slumber Party
songs.note: Track from Irreversible about depression-induced agoraphobia, set to springy 80s-style guitar and brisk tempos.

songs.title: I Can Take the Sun Right Out of the Sky
songs.note: Track from Irreversible covering apocalyptic melancholy, with heart-skipping tempos and infectious guitar melodies.

songs.title: Tongue
songs.note: Highlight from Crystalpunk, with start-stop, sung-screamed cacophony and snarling alternative rock hooks.

songs.title: IDC
songs.note: Highlight from Crystalpunk, a bottom-heavy electroclash track with industrial grooves.

songs.title: Pain
songs.note: Highlight from Crystalpunk, a bottom-heavy electroclash track with industrial grooves.

songs.title: Skem
songs.note: Highlight from Crystalpunk, a throbbing, paranoid techno track.

songs.title: Parental Advisory
songs.note: Opener from I Guess U Had To Be There that moves from a story about corporal punishment to a broader critique of harsh systems.

songs.title: Lynch
songs.note: Opener from KHAZNA, with springy synths and chugging guitar riffs under Alkhateri's silken, cutting vocals.

songs.title: Loosen Up
songs.note: Track from Mali with a herky-jerk rhythm and bulbous synths bouncing around like a paddleball.

songs.title: Driving On Sand
songs.note: Track from Mali featuring Steve Spacek, a hypnotic, soulful house-leaning song with a joyous backdrop.

https://stereogum.com/2310886/the-5-best.title: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week

songs.title: Getaway Plan
songs.note: Lead single from Jacob Duarte's solo project, a freewheeling, caffeinated rocker meant to feel like rocking out with your inner child.

songs.title: The Big E
songs.note: Title track from Wendy Eisenberg's new album, an anxious rumble about alien visitors and aging, with a piercing vocal melody.

songs.title: Easier Said Than Done
songs.note: First single for label Epitaph, keeping the band's Florida emo sound while hitting a little harder with more direct bittersweet lyrics.

songs.title: Life Signs
songs.note: Lead single from new album It's A Beautiful Place, with a blown-out power-chord riff, gnarly surf guitar, and a jazzy chorus.

songs.title: Fame Is A Gun
songs.note: Track with collaborators ELVIRA and Luka Kloser that evokes Britney Spears circa Blackout, a sticky, perilous take on mass attention.

https://stereogum.com/2502093/the-5-best.title: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week

songs.title: Unfinished Concrete Initials (feat. Hemlock Ernst)
songs.note: Presented as the pilot of the TV series DOOMED!, the album with Kenny Segal; a post-breakup song with soulful singing and rap over a Segal beat.

songs.title: I Can See
songs.note: Title track and gateway to his new album; a flowing, falsetto-led song with a guitar entrance nearly five minutes in.

songs.title: soulless cycle
songs.note: Lead single from forthcoming album fata morgana; an enthralling noise rock blast with polished vocals floating through the chaos.

songs.title: Better Man
songs.note: Starry-eyed shimmy pushed into dreamy territory, with Emily Massey's yearning vocals over spangly guitars and keyboards.

songs.title: Deep Blue
songs.note: Haunting, shredding track of the same ilk as their 2024 album Cool World; vocals swing between drawl and feral screams.

https://stereogum.com/2490571/the-5-best.title: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week

songs.title: I Didn't Mean To Change My Mind
songs.note: A blown-out power-pop ballad with jangly guitars that feel like reassurance, tied to a sense of something ending with rebirth ahead.

songs.title: I Know!
songs.note: Debut single for Winspear that flows naturally, built on a repeated hook and a rush of band sound when the chorus breaks in.

songs.title: i want a beer
songs.note: A sour, unsettling debut single with industrial stammers, eerie vocals, and dark, unrelenting energy beneath its pop surface.

songs.title: Berlin
songs.note: A murky atmospheric confessional about unsettled life, using past mega-pop elements like breakbeats, keyboards, and smooth-jazz sax.

songs.title: Stupid Bitches
songs.note: Latest single from upcoming album Girlfriend, embracing a pop diva persona while shrugging off a romantic rejection with confidence.

https://stereogum.com/2303102/the-5-best.title: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week

songs.title: Dissociation (feat. Chloe Hotline)
songs.note: Montreal rapper-producer gets personal over a grandiose post-rock beat, rapping about sobriety, depression, and loved ones; Chloe Hotline adds harmony on the hook.

songs.title: Potion
songs.note: A sleek '70s Laurel Canyon-style folk-pop track with propulsive finger-picking and jaunty falsetto, from the new Djo album.

songs.title: Aegean blue
songs.note: A hymn-like song with flutes and soft guitars where open space and her gradually building voice carry the track, singing of rivers.

songs.title: East Side Screamer
songs.note: A brooding, power-pop-tinged guitar song describing a supernatural encounter in his Madison hometown, from the upcoming album Timeless World Forever.

songs.title: catch these fists
songs.note: A giddy, silly rock singalong slammer with flinty guitar riffs and sleepy murmured lyrics, continuing the sound of their debut.

songs.title: One One
songs.note: An addictive, pitying dismissal of an ungrateful ex, with menace creeping into minimalist, stumbling percussion.

songs.title: Dead Shark II
songs.note: Eleven years after her debut, Liz Harris (Grouper) revives the dream-pop band; the review calls it as good as the genre gets.

songs.title: 2Late
songs.note: A synthwave-ballad debut for XL, switching from his ultra-emotional rap tracks to singing, restless after a breakup.

songs.title: Eddie's Album
songs.note: The Royal Trux vocalist's side project plays taut disco-funk behind murky lo-fi chillwave production, on supremely fun form.

songs.title: Entre Nous
songs.note: The title track of an ambient and dub techno album, with a subtle dancehall pulse adding a touch of heat.

songs.title: From
songs.note: Lo-fi, blanketed intimacy and layered vocals, from a new release on Phil Elverum's label.

songs.title: One Night Only (Break Loose Break Free!)
songs.note: The first New Radicals song since 1999, with Gregg Alexander's knack for secular affirmations, from a film soundtrack.

songs.title: qué les pasó a mis amigos?
songs.note: Title track where Minus muses on purpose and burnout, singing in Spanish over pulsing synths.

songs.title: lose my cool
songs.note: Atmospheric track about a relationship that has become unrecognizable, amid overwhelm and uncertainty.

songs.title: espiral
songs.note: Hypnotic, synth-driven track that speaks to exploitation in the music industry.

songs.title: seagull theory II
songs.note: Ambient folk piece built from field recordings of birds and waves, tied to ecological grief and transience.

songs.title: from
songs.note: Gentle ambient folk composition that the post says is borne by the truth that everything is changing.

songs.title: The Crowning
songs.note: Thundering guitars shot through with yearning, from the band's third album Verbolgen.

songs.title: In Blood And Earth
songs.note: Seven-minute track moving from a hushed acoustic opening to towering, wave-like chords.

songs.title: The Glow of Dawn
songs.note: Album finale that slows down behind a melancholy, lonesome flute melody.

https://diymag.com/feature/the-neu-bulle.title: The Neu Bulletin (Kiosk, Hank, Big Softy and more!)

songs.title: Troubleshooting
songs.note: A catchy post-hyperpop electronic track with stacked sample loops, a syncopated breakdown, and a playful take on erectile dysfunction.

songs.title: G.V.O.
songs.note: Their first single in three years, an absurdist post-punk track with literary influences and art-rock energy, described as a joy to hear back.

songs.title: Tell The Leaves Not To Turn
songs.note: A guitar-heavy, shoegazey track with soft vocals, using autumn imagery to convey someone slipping away; the band's debut album is due next month.

songs.title: Baby Teeth
songs.note: A dark neo-gothic electronic track with dissonant vocals from Bella Alcock over a trap sequence, described as a dance track for the too-cool-to-dance.

songs.title: Billed Gates
songs.note: Thumping bassline makes it one of the album's ominous, thunderous highlights on Atomic Justice.

songs.title: Lifting Gravity
songs.note: Creeping piano hovers like distant thunderclouds, adding to the album's bleak, overcast mood.

songs.title: Able to Be Kane
songs.note: Pointed lyrics about hateful comments and Christianity, with a sharp closing ad lib.

songs.title: Thrilla Bark
songs.note: Cites Idiocracy, a line the post says sums up the album's theme about America in 2026.

songs.title: Touch Grass
songs.note: Ward's unhurried rhymes sit over a DOOM-esque mix of jazzy guitar and bright keys, with Lord Jah-Monte Ogbon guesting.

songs.title: Table Etiquette
songs.note: Ward moves breezily through relationships over Loman's keyboard eighth notes, like Christmas lights.

songs.title: Blight
songs.note: New single pairing a meditation on a relationship's end with country-fried indie pop and pedal-steel-style lead guitar.

songs.title: Erosion
songs.note: Opens Winter's End with a post-punk lead guitar skipping over a jittery drum machine, leading into a run of banger tracks.

songs.title: Cisne
songs.note: Trance opener on Invierno en la playa, where Lorena Pulgar sings about searching her body for the pleasure of trying.

songs.title: Antes del día
songs.note: Imagines the Sun imploding and burning everything, with a lyric about skin blending that ties into a love theme.

songs.title: Life Ahead
songs.note: Opens as a Peter Gabriel-style ballad before bursting into a heartrending R&B chorus showcasing his higher register.

songs.title: Holy Mountain
songs.note: Skipping highlife with silvery, staccato guitar lines darting behind a fragile falsetto from Obongjayar.

songs.title: Instant Animal
songs.note: A snarling psychedelic track later on Paradise Now, described as one of the record's stylistic detours.

songs.title: Just My Luck
songs.note: A sprightly '80s pop track with blinking keys, placed later in the album.

songs.title: destroy build destroy
songs.note: Punches syllables like percussion amid crashing sound, with focused rapping that guides listeners through a harrowing midsection vocal.

songs.title: what i learned in boating school is...
songs.note: Rapid-fire bars cast out independently of the purposefully erratic, sputtering drums.

songs.title: Cursive
songs.note: A spooky party jam built from a rhythm section beat, with Valentine Caulfield's magnetic vocals over a chaotic, undulating groove.

songs.title: Eulogy
songs.note: Described as a polished, retro synth-rock song that evokes 1980s teen-movie scenes, moving from the band's earlier scrappy synth-punk sound.

songs.title: Apple Pie

songs.title: Tumbleweed
songs.note: A hip-swinging, bold and fun track with expansive snapping guitar and hypnotic, fluttering vocals.

songs.title: Nevermind
songs.note: A sparse, desolate song about ambiguity and unsaid things, built on booming vocals, sparse guitars and persistent reverb.

songs.title: Pale Song

songs.title: I'm Here
songs.note: Latest single exploring fear and its influence on identity; Groth says the song confronts that fear rather than being consumed by it.

songs.title: Reason
songs.note: Debut single from a new New York band with Emily Cabarle, about reconnecting with childlike wonder and escaping adult isolation.

songs.title: Emmeline

songs.title: Leash
songs.note: Standalone single with a sassy, tongue-in-cheek breezy rock sound, celebrating the shadow self and darker impulses.

songs.title: Upstate
songs.note: Partner single to Mirror at Night B-Sides, described as a quiet, otherworldly transmission where memories blur and dreams surface.

songs.title: Wake Dance Romance ft. Lead Into Gold

songs.title: Loved By Me
songs.note: New track from upcoming album Song Room, an expression of unconditional love aimed at tender parts of oneself and others.

songs.title: No Sweat
songs.note: Single from debut EP Wild Mountain Time, a sunny surf-tinged track with a supernatural edge inspired by city commuting.

songs.title: Compliment
songs.note: Synth-driven single from upcoming album Attention, about receiving unexpected attention while already in a relationship.

songs.title: Flourish
songs.note: Earthy, emotive folk single evoking spring and hopefulness, ahead of her third full-length via Bonsound.

songs.title: When To Stop
songs.note: Latest single from debut solo album, offering a compassionate tone shot through with rising tension.

songs.title: Any Other World
songs.note: Krautrock-y track with concentric cycles of musical and lyrical phrases that lose meaning like an intrusive thought.

songs.title: No No Yes Yes
songs.note: Dance-punk track that forgoes traditional song structure for repeating musical and lyrical cycles.

songs.title: Set Me Free
songs.note: Processional keyboard-organ melody and hymn-like harmonies that turn maudlin before the album's darker turn.

songs.title: Purgatory Of Consciousness
songs.note: Cavernous, ghastly ambience that the post highlights as a disarming moment on the record.

songs.title: Matty
songs.note: Opener looking back wistfully at a childhood crush, admitting she is way too old for love now.

songs.title: Barbed Wire
songs.note: Strings devastating phrases about a friendship's end, building to a climactic wall of electrified sound.

songs.title: Heavenly One
songs.note: Acoustic ballad moving from fragile vulnerability to a whirling pool of strings, synths, and a self-made choir.

songs.title: Slit
songs.note: Shows the band's dream pop and shoegaze combination, one of several styles they juggle.

songs.title: You Are The Sun
songs.note: Doomy slowcore track showing the band's range across the record.

songs.title: Joe Modern
songs.note: Jittery post-punk track about a scumbag landlord.

songs.title: Amaranth
songs.note: Album highlight; a deceptively beautiful folk-screamo hybrid with gothic undertones.

songs.title: BLK XMAS
songs.note: Final verse tells the story of evicted neighbors, so meticulously crafted that no single line stands alone.

songs.title: Waterproof Mascara
songs.note: Chilling narrative about the death of woods's father, with whom he had an ambivalent relationship.

songs.title: Lead Paint
songs.note: Uses a dead boy's shoes to create a deliberately discomfiting effect.

songs.title: Ultra Red
songs.note: Study of absence that pulls the album's bottom out with barren tones buried under static and fog.

songs.title: Reeling Mist
songs.note: Dubbier, more obtuse and mysterious track that picks the album back up after the drop.

songs.title: Lagoon
songs.note: Thrumming, almost menacing track that evokes being pursued through dark subterranean tunnels.

songs.artist: Stolen Velour, Floco and Aria SL
songs.title: Caught Myself
songs.note: Lead single from debut album Underlight; bobs between sunken drawls and airy, keening vocals, like a swimmer submerging and reappearing.

songs.title: Still I Love Him
songs.note: The Lankum member's solo debut; a song of devotion where the narrator's lover "knocks me about", with sadness carried through a warm arrangement.

songs.title: The Ground Here
songs.note: Acoustic track with Laurel Canyon influences, channelling Joni Mitchell's open-hearted style with her own rangy energy.

songs.title: The Bridge
songs.note: Aqueous ballad about an overwhelming crush, with PinkPantheress harmonising gorgeously alongside Kelela.

songs.title: Save Me

songs.title: Placeholder

songs.title: Sígueme
songs.note: Spanish-language cover of Amanda Lear's Italo disco classic Follow Me, from the new album Pavor.

songs.title: Not for Nothing

songs.title: Moss Song

songs.title: Australian Summer
songs.note: Hazy, sun-drunk folk-inflected song from a double single, sung by Aine Keogh, evoking long lazy summer days.

songs.title: Simple Delight

songs.title: Lies About The Sky (Shudder to Think cover)

songs.title: Twisters
songs.note: First glimpse of upcoming album Total Dive, a confident, wearily optimistic mid-tempo country rocker.

songs.title: Moreoff More Off Than On
songs.note: Lead single from Sabrina Nickels, charged with adventure and experimentation, made in a more committed, adult-serious way.

songs.title: Brush Me Like A Horse
songs.note: Lead single from Joe Newman's solo project, blending gospel, Motown and blues with a surreal story of a man turning into a horse.

songs.title: Room Tone
songs.note: Ambient live-to-tape improvisation exploring baritone guitar as an environment, named after the filmmaking term for silent room sound.

songs.title: Be Around
songs.note: Lead single from upcoming album Song Room, about the feeling of being too much and hard to love.

songs.title: The Hunt in Edson
songs.note: New Saddle Creek single inspired by two unrelated true events, exploring being under extreme pressure.

songs.title: Pink Skies

songs.title: Black Dog March

songs.title: Swimming Hole

songs.title: Ivory Tower
songs.note: Described as critiquing the grip the top 1% holds over the world's people.

songs.title: Fade Way

songs.title: Something's Different

songs.note: Described as feeling like being dragged through alluvial muck, showing the band's sludgy, disgusting death metal side on Offering of Chaos.

songs.title: Jimmy
songs.note: The album opener on Marten, where Jackie Perez Gratz's cello opens up the band's sonic space from the first notes.

songs.title: That It Was to Say
songs.note: Opening work of Du.0's debut, a nine-minute negotiation between wobbly pitches and wordless vocal shadings that ends in a tart passage.

songs.title: Upon the Wheel
songs.note: Brittle, spiky dissonance and wild swoops give way to a gorgeous chorale-like conclusion, played with delicate sonic choreography.

songs.title: Dead Horse Bay…Thoughts From the Future
songs.note: Nine-movement sonic portrait of a South Brooklyn body of water, veering between dystopian angst and melancholic nostalgia.

songs.title: Lynx
songs.note: Focuses on cellist Mariel Roberts, with Modney's violin and Sam Pluta's live signal processing commenting on and disrupting her playing.

songs.title: Everything Around it Moves
songs.note: Written for string quartet and piano, a jagged piece cleaved by ruptures, ending in a sorrowful lattice of just-intonation lines.

songs.title: Zeitgebers
songs.note: Ten-minute percussion-driven work melding field recordings with the janky, homemade rhythms Hennies is known for.

songs.title: Clock Dies
songs.note: Written for Talea Ensemble with a conductor; slowly morphing themes shift into stuttering piano patterns and halting rhythms evoking a broken clock.

songs.title: Motor Tapes
songs.note: Performed by Dedalus Ensemble, electric guitar passages convey isolated memories that replay like a tape loop, drawing on Rodolfo Llinás's idea.

songs.title: Arpeggio
songs.note: From a solo violin suite, a single pattern builds into a stunning climax over eight explosive minutes, touching on early Philip Glass.

songs.title: Triads
songs.note: A movement evoking the serenity the composer felt looking out her studio window in winter rather than chordal construction.

songs.title: Particle Dust
songs.note: Opening movement of Waves and Particles, based on a fractal called Cantor dust, with cycling string patterns that shift with each repetition.

songs.title: Spectral Waves
songs.note: Clustered tones swell and ebb as the strings seem to shape-shift electronically, with shapes built from sound waves.

songs.title: Mirror Blown Into Pieces, The Immortal III
songs.note: Performed by Yarn/Wire, elliptical piano parts are caressed and pierced by bowed metal, with fluid swells and distortions.

songs.title: An Index of Fictions
songs.note: Tactile percussive dialogue gives way to white noise and synth washes, until an insistent piano note cuts through the din.

songs.title: Pitiless as the Sun
songs.note: Cold bleakness in the first half, with the second half slowly turning dread into a tenuous sense of hope or peace.

songs.title: Curva Triangulus
songs.note: Performed by Ensemble Proton, a patient, glowing piece with a re-tuned Baroque triple harp and a haunting, ancient-futuristic form.

songs.title: RIGHT TURN ON RED
songs.note: Stop-start breakbeat chaos in a caffeinated video game-rave style, with the funk kept in check.

songs.title: GoGoGoGO!
songs.note: Bleep-cascade electro hyper-boogie that the post calls alarming but hugely fun.

songs.title: JUMP START
songs.note: Title track with piledriver drops, described as a fresh twist on UK garage.

songs.title: Void 19
songs.note: UK garage track with shark-eyed menace, singled out for its fresh twist.

songs.title: Dust Dance
songs.note: Beautiful rollage using Central Asian-sounding hand drums and string melodies for a transportive atmosphere.

songs.title: Rattle
songs.note: Subtly martial, dubstep-inflected track weaving Punjabi bhangra into grime.

songs.title: Heart Meter
songs.note: Cascading flutes and carnival atmosphere blended with Punjabi bhangra and grime.

songs.title: Grid
songs.note: Looks back to grime's early eight-bar sound, with gigantic kicks and a spiraling melodic hook.

songs.title: E9cn39c98g4cg4094b

songs.title: Days & Days (Vocal Mix)
songs.note: Listed as a recommended track in the post's roundup of picks.

songs.title: Like Water
songs.note: Extremely zippy techno with dub-tech piano chops and a warm sustained string note.

songs.title: Finding a Way
songs.note: Similar string tone with pizzicato-like notes playing an old-school rave riff for euphoric effect.

songs.title: Calvinist Hospitality
songs.note: Title track with a steppers reggae rhythm that the post likens to African Head Charge.

songs.title: Distant Star

songs.title: I Know Where Ray Cappo Lives
songs.note: A one-off single with snotty SoCal '80s hardcore vibes and barking vocals, reminiscent of Black Flag's "Nervous Breakdown."

songs.title: The Last Days of May

songs.title: Close Quarters

songs.title: fat belly (Ben Bondy and Yves remix)

songs.title: Moon Theater

songs.title: Colibri

songs.title: Pazuzu

songs.title: Nosebleed

songs.title: See You

songs.title: Eleven Eleven

songs.title: Hey Heron

songs.title: Kill Floor

songs.title: Train Wreck

songs.title: Bachelors Theme

songs.title: Bragging Party

songs.title: No Cigarettes

songs.title: Kiss Me

songs.title: L.D.E.

songs.title: Kitty Cats

songs.title: My Fault

songs.title: Sterile Century

songs.title: Access

songs.title: The Web

songs.title: Rock Tune

songs.title: Kyiv

songs.title: El Nahr

songs.title: French Hotel

songs.title: Running Out of Time

songs.title: Into the Dark

songs.title: Night Thoughts

songs.title: Smug

songs.title: Tunnel Vision

songs.title: Breath II

songs.note: From Folio #5, this piece comes strong with volatility, standing apart from the album's more balanced pieces.

songs.title: La vie commence aujourd'hui
songs.note: From Folio #5, this piece swings toward pure serenity, the opposite direction from the volatile tracks.

songs.title: The Inchworm
songs.note: A standout on Tippin', played with the joy of musicians jamming for its own sake.

songs.title: Weeping Willows
songs.note: Swaying track built on dusky blues and soul loops that create a twilight atmosphere.

songs.title: First Too Lose
songs.note: Gently jittering track where Suede raps reflectively about calling home more.

songs.title: Silverhand
songs.note: Experimental track blending dub influences with graveyard percussion, with Suede criticizing wordy MCs.

songs.title: ELDERBERRY
songs.note: Fat Ray delivers boastful verses over spectral strings on this Food From The Gods track.

songs.title: CANE
songs.note: Guest appearance on aggressive funk production from Food From The Gods.

songs.title: Just Say No
songs.note: Danny Brown guests on this Food From The Gods track and waxes nostalgic.

songs.title: Franky Lymon
songs.note: Bruiser Wolf raps about moving powder over a shimmering, piano-spiked beat.

songs.title: Satisfied Soul
songs.note: Title track of the Ant-produced album, where Ali calls himself a poet warrior and issues warnings.

songs.title: Sing Myself Whole
songs.note: Acoustic guitar-driven track where Ali finds solace from tragedy and grief in music.

songs.title: glimpses of god
songs.note: Watson raps surrealist lyrics over a serene, pulsing groove produced by Elaquent.

songs.title: remedy
songs.note: Arrives halfway through the album with cherubic chimes and wispy guitar lines.

songs.title: In Between The Lines
songs.note: Farma G digs into the dynamics of the writing process on his solo debut.

songs.title: Bearskin Coats
songs.note: Farma G asserts his clout on this How To Kill A Butterfly track.

songs.title: The Start And End
songs.note: Naturalistic imagery recalls the style of his Task Force days.

songs.title: Reflections In Smoke
songs.note: Archibald Slim raps straight-talking advice over clipped drums and graceful synths.

songs.title: Sparkling Water
songs.note: EP closer spotlighting Grey's soulful production of aching piano and rattling drums.

songs.title: Catch Your Breath
songs.note: Pink Siifu raps over static and hiss on a dusky, intimate remix track.

songs.title: Focus
songs.note: Crunching Bear-One-produced opener about the importance of self-motivation.

songs.title: Anxiety
songs.note: Nervy synths underpin bars about sleepless nights.

songs.title: Shame
songs.note: Open Mike Eagle brings conceptual skills to this track.

songs.title: Manifest
songs.note: Raucous sparring session with verses from Apathy and Mickey Factz.

songs.title: Ringling Bros
songs.note: Bank$ moves from baked-goods snacking to a grislier state of mind over Wino Willy's beat.

songs.title: Best Days
songs.note: Chemistry between Bank$ and Wino Willy's woozy beat work is in peak form.

songs.title: Sub Zero (Wintro)
songs.note: Guitar-driven opener where Wrekonize raps about freezing and navigating label woes.

songs.title: Fantasy Baseball
songs.note: Comments on hip-hop becoming commodified Moneyball-style, stripping listeners of the thrill of the musical moment.

songs.title: Dork Crystal
songs.note: Described as the peak of Luminous Rubble, evoking a nervy walk through a dusky fantasy forest in a supernatural film.

songs.title: I AM
songs.note: An undulating track where D.R.O. pinpoints his personal shortcomings over pillowy keys and shuffling drums.

songs.title: GOD LIKE FEELING
songs.note: Turns braggadocio into a cry for connection, according to the post.

songs.title: SHAME
songs.note: Closer that pairs a lilting, sun-blissed backdrop with confessions about lost opportunities and pain.

songs.title: 12 Labours Of Hercules
songs.note: Intense bars over hypnotic, horn-smeared production that recalls RZA's work on Ghostface's Ironman.

songs.title: Crocodile Tears
songs.note: Weeping piano-laden closer where the MC mixes boasts and spiritual reflection while holed up in an East African bar.

songs.title: Damaged
songs.note: D Withdrawn reflects on leaving trouble and violence behind over a backdrop lit by Debbie Deitering's vocals.

songs.title: Midnight Madness
songs.note: Napoleon vents about doubters over a crunchy, piano-powered backdrop.

songs.title: The King Walk
songs.note: Angular funk and brawny drums make it the standout among LEGMATIC's instrumental versions.

songs.title: Until The End
songs.note: An emotional track built on an aching, melancholy xylophone riff that conveys tender rumination.

songs.title: Eternally Grateful
songs.note: Closer that wraps a vocal refrain in gentle echo, ending the album on a hopeful, soothing note.

songs.title: Forensics
songs.note: Early high point with mid-tempo production, where Sinatra describes sharpening his mind and scheming.

songs.title: Cut Weight
songs.note: An '80s soul throwback featuring Milc.

songs.title: Memoriam pt. 2
songs.note: Jittery drums and off-kilter sludge funk, with desde featured.

songs.title: Origins
songs.note: Features PremRock and SKECH185, with Sinatra describing reality seen through broken lenses.

songs.title: Struggle Meal
songs.note: A funky track where Fatboi Sharif recalls menus from a more turbulent era.

songs.title: Pancakes!
songs.note: Lays out an array of breakfast choices over the album's jazzier beats.

songs.title: PATH
songs.note: Lungs, OneShotOnce, S!LENCE, and Slim Carrey celebrate the transit system over crunching snares and agitated strings.

songs.title: Contact (Karen Nyame KG Remix)
songs.note: Karen Nyame KG remixes Kelela's alt-R&B track, adding Afro-house rhythms and amapiano log drums beneath layered vocal processing.

songs.title: Night Creatures
songs.note: The title track with Detroit vocalist Blak Tony is an elegant sci-fi electro piece, in the spirit of Juan Atkins.

songs.title: He Isn't Even From Round Here Part 1
songs.note: A British turn from this London producer, with squirming, fidgety drum & bass in the style of late-'90s Squarepusher and an ambient coda.

songs.title: The Don
songs.note: A funky, noisy beat inspired by early-'90s hip-hop and Britcore, with sub bass and a vocal from The Ragga Twins.

songs.title: Daddication Pt. 1
songs.note: Myka 9 shares thoughts on fatherhood over wobbly sci-fi synths and lonesome chimes.

songs.title: Count To Ten
songs.note: Pacewon brings an upbeat presence to a chugging track.

songs.title: Freakin' Beats
songs.note: Sensational flows over a groggy funk backdrop.

songs.title: The Diary
songs.note: Opener with dewy synths and a placid piano riff, evoking a gentle sunrise.

songs.title: Shallow Breaths
songs.note: A deeply meditative outing built on rustling static and pulsing bass tones.

songs.title: Honestly Don't
songs.note: Subtle strings build into a soundtrack for heartbreak.

songs.title: Acapulco
songs.note: A sinewy synth line suits a liquor-fortified mid-afternoon lament on life.

songs.title: Change The Channel
songs.note: A two-minute blitz of frenzied, rave-influenced breaks and bleeps with sharp bars.

songs.title: Ask What Happened
songs.note: Closer tying the album's themes together, questioning a world run by a tech-empowered elite.

songs.title: Welcome To The Future
songs.note: King Kashmere bluntly states the world is messed up over grinding digi-funk.

songs.title: Oblivion 4000
songs.note: Cappo navigates the digital apocalypse over this track.

songs.title: CTHULU
songs.note: Fingathing's Dan Peter Parker brings turntablist work to a humming track.

songs.title: Nekron
songs.note: Bigg Jus conjures end-times visions over demonic bass.

songs.title: Ulmer Scale
songs.note: Matter Ov Fact raps over squelching G-funk production.

songs.title: Cookin' with Gas
songs.note: Album closer with tales of battling a Kraken and doomscrolling on 'shrooms.

songs.title: Untitled (Close Your Eyes)
songs.note: Hooli lays down unhurried confidence over a smoldering bass backdrop.

songs.title: Fresh Air
songs.note: Guest spot on a mid-project outing, sharing a contraband mission anecdote.

songs.title: Track One
songs.note: Pairs a sample about human memory with skewed piano notes.

songs.title: olive
songs.note: Sludgy bass tones set against snippets of woozy keys.

songs.title: the harp one
songs.note: Shuffles into serene climes with honeyed strings and bird sounds.

songs.title: Angel's Share
songs.note: Opener of hazy synths and plaintive piano with ruminative, whiskey-soaked lyrics.

songs.title: Steal Wool
songs.note: Pink Siifu guests on a subtly glistening track.

songs.title: Crueler Walls
songs.note: Nappy Nina closes out the jazzy track.

songs.title: Receipts
songs.note: billy woods contemplates moving on from a life stage over piano-spiked production.

songs.title: Scrying Mirror
songs.note: Sinatra raps over aching sampled vocal snippets balancing positive and negative influences.

songs.title: Beast Mode
songs.note: Standout string-fortified track where Term drinks Hennessy through a straw.

songs.title: Glue Mechanic
songs.note: Lo Fives' new single, a noisy, twangy punk track with big hooks; the post calls it a standout from the two-song EP.

songs.title: New Illiterates
songs.note: Second track on Lo Fives' two-song Glue Mechanic EP; the post lists it with big ear-wormy choruses and hooks.

songs.title: I'll Go Anywhere
songs.note: Post calls this devotional track the sonic apex of the album, blending fingerstyle guitar, hand clapping, and a women's choir singing in Arabic.

songs.title: Imaan
songs.note: Post reads this song's secret relationship as a metaphor for young Muslims balancing Western social life and Islamic values.

songs.title: Libre
songs.note: Post calls this lead single sweetly danceable but colored by icy synths that turn dark by the end.

songs.title: Décembre
songs.note: Post describes this track as nightmarish, one of the album's sonic extremes.

songs.title: Julia
songs.note: Post praises this alt-radio track for its chugging guitar and wry sarcasm in Leigh Nash's delivery.

songs.title: Moonlit Floor
songs.note: Post says LISA incorporated bits of Sixpence None the Richer's "Kiss Me" into this new single.

songs.title: War Flowerz
songs.note: Post calls this album centerpiece a focused, bracing internal struggle with dense, layered wordplay.

songs.title: Changing of the Guard
songs.note: Post says its dreamlike synth backdrop is one of the production highlights of the album.

songs.title: Ronin
songs.note: Post describes this track's anxious chipmunk soul production as a contrast to the album's dreamier moments.

songs.title: Relapse
songs.note: Guitars claw at the song like skeleton fingers, on the band's Faces to Hide, described as a grim, bleak L.A. rock record.

songs.title: Satellite of Love
songs.note: Described as having a panicky urgency that quickens the pulse, with the writer noting it is not the Lou Reed song.

songs.title: Laws of the Land
songs.note: Singled out for its three-note guitar skip-up-the-octave, a detail that makes the production stand out.

songs.title: Eyes & Ears
songs.note: Singled out for a flute that darts mosquito-like across the track without distracting from the rest.

songs.title: Aggravated
songs.note: A moody track where the rapper moves from hazy rainstorm imagery to blunt reflections on mortality.

songs.title: Naration
songs.note: Described as a moment when divergent conversations enter a collective rhythm; a standout rhythmic display on Adrift.

songs.title: Reflections of Rif
songs.note: The post says it lights up like gasoline, a fiery highlight of the Adrift session.

songs.title: Third Bardo
songs.note: Its rousing personality is said to bloom from the previous track, Naturis, like chapters in an epic novel.

songs.title: Babylon Shuffle
songs.note: Named in the post's list of picks; the write-up gives no further detail on this track.

songs.artist: Mindy Meng Wang 王萌, Sui Zhen
songs.title: Origin of You
songs.note: Melbourne duo's spacious, rarefied 'fifth world' record blending traditional and futurist sounds, with a hilarious flex track the post urges DJs to play.

songs.title: It's a Bomb
songs.note: Named in the post's list of picks; the write-up gives no further detail on this track.

songs.title: Enamoradode (DJ Babbatr Rapacious Mix)
songs.note: Wilfully silly Venezuelan hard house with a one-note riff that rewards those who go with it, plus a beatboxed cymbal break.

songs.title: All That We Have
songs.note: From a session bassist's debut EP blending house, disco, post-punk and Afro-Brazilian groove, with a quirky vocal from Sofia Grant.

songs.title: The Good Times
songs.note: Named in the post's list of picks; the write-up gives no further detail on this track.

songs.title: Prophecy b/w Super Sunday
songs.note: Two jungle throwbacks: 'Prophecy' is big and bashy, while 'Super Sunday' revisits early jump-up's stripped-back menace.

songs.title: Ich Sehe Vasen
songs.note: Trilogy Tapes release mixing radiophonic weirdness with clockwork-like outsider house across a sprawling world of its own rules.

songs.title: Reach for the Stars
songs.note: Upbeat single in '90s UK rave and trance style, with Idehen delivering wry motivational musings on the wisdom of age.

songs.title: Body Music
songs.note: Named in the post's list of picks; the write-up gives no further detail on this track.

songs.title: Crude Appraisal
songs.note: Sweat-drenched acid house from a prolific DJ and producer, with some tracks swapping kicks for shuffling breakbeats.

songs.title: Top Shelf Material
songs.note: Laid-back, post-rave electronica from an Anglo-Italian collaboration, with fizzy chords, meandering melodies and giddy breaks.

songs.title: G-OUT
songs.note: Named in the post's list of picks; the write-up gives no further detail on this track.

songs.title: Tune IN
songs.note: Named in the post's list of picks; the write-up gives no further detail on this track.

songs.title: Nanoclusters
songs.note: Sheffield Central Processing Unit release with focused electro and techno, Kraftwerk-style influences and a steady robo-funk groove.

songs.title: Stella Remota
songs.note: Named in the post's list of picks; the write-up gives no further detail on this track.

songs.title: Backie Riddim
songs.note: Off-beat kicks and deep horn stabs build to a dancehall-meets-rave bubbling banger with Surinamese producer Lamsi.

songs.title: Screwball Scramble b/w Double Dutch
songs.note: Two crisp, minimal drum and bass cuts from Manchester's Chimpo, each with playful swooshes and DJ cuts to keep the party going.

songs.title: Resonant Tree I
songs.note: Slow-motion harpsichord and just-intonation chords with viola, flutes, and bass clarinet, with acoustic guitar and 12-string accents.

songs.title: Resonant Tree II
songs.note: Flutes are absent; viola takes a more prominent role and interacts more directly with the harpsichord.

songs.title: Open Symmetry
songs.note: Extended work for three vibraphones and 20 one-bit electronic devices, shifting between meditative, intense, and psychedelic moods.

songs.title: Hypnokaséta
songs.note: Sixteen uninterrupted parts inspired by lockdown dreams, performed by Quatuor Bozzini with Andy Moor and cassette noise.

songs.title: for Toshiko
songs.note: Four-movement piece based on Toshiko Takaezu's bronze bell recordings, arranged for piano, violin, and cello by Longleash.

songs.title: sending messages
songs.note: Performed on clay pots in the first movement and bells and rattles in the second, drawing on Takaezu's sound world.

songs.title: Dodone
songs.note: Piano overtones resembling bowed strings, grazed and slowly decaying before the next gesture enters.

songs.title: Chalkeion
songs.note: Angular, jagged chord stabs struck asymmetrically, leaving dissolving artifacts after each articulation.

songs.title: Omphee
songs.note: Uses bowing with a more metallic bite in the higher register and denser piled-up gestures.

songs.title: Amvracia
songs.note: Mixes conventionally struck low tones with prepared piano, producing rattling and buzzing sounds.

songs.title: Dione
songs.note: Electronically shaped tones that seem played backwards, so decays appear to swell rather than fade.

songs.title: arcing, stilling, bending, gathering
songs.note: Piano and violin float through wavering sonic gauze, drawing on the opening bars of the final movement.

songs.title: Tiding II
songs.note: Pianist, percussionist, saxophonist, and electronics produce patient, unfolding constellations of sound and texture.

songs.title: A through-grown earth
songs.note: Soprano Juliet Fraser sets Gerard Manley Hopkins texts over a hovering, translucent ensemble texture.

songs.title: Our Father
songs.note: Late piece built on a liturgical vocal duet, with Davóne Tines overdubbing both parts over stark orchestral accompaniment.

songs.title: Piano 2
songs.note: Obscure late piece performed by Richard Valitutto, with notation cleaned up by Joseph Kubera.

songs.title: Prelude to the Holy Presence of Joan of Arc
songs.note: Davóne Tines delivers an intense, soulful performance with a stentorian voice; Seth Parker Woods plays all cello parts.

songs.title: String Quartet No. 4
songs.note: Strings and voices slowed to near incomprehensibility, reflecting post-Sandy and Irene rebuilding and climate anxiety.

songs.title: String Quartet No. 2
songs.note: Just-intonation chords rise and fall in overlapping patterns, enhanced by wordless vocal shapes.

songs.title: Pastorale …. para los pobres de la tierra
songs.note: Alice Teyssier moves between voice and flute, with The Rhythm Method's harmony singing, on texts by Machado, Neruda, and Saint Francis.

songs.title: Venutian Wetlands
songs.note: Piercing upper-register clusters, animal-like grunts, and unstable fluctuations that abruptly turn turbulent.

songs.title: CD Players
songs.note: A texture-rich drone toggling between two lone pitches, opening into a wide range of harmony.

songs.title: kvoða
songs.note: A sweet-toned work that still has a nice timbral bite, performed by Viibra.

songs.title: Mundana X
songs.note: Originally for two contrabass clarinets; one line is played by the composer with a low sine tone, and the other is spectrally broken into seven layers.

songs.title: Ms. Ephemeris Abyss
songs.note: Masses seven flutes into a single wriggling organism that suggests a nest of vipers from one source.

songs.title: Raw Shit
songs.note: Named as the most aggressively mind-bending, body-rocking track on Natural Frequencies' 10-track classic Detroit techno compilation.

songs.title: General Principle
songs.note: Described as a complex, elevated track on the Natural Frequencies compilation, sitting between the wilder and more reflective tracks.

songs.title: Mantequilla
songs.note: Opening cyberpunk reggaeton track on the EP, featuring the Spanish dancehall-punk vocals of Clara!.

songs.title: tambien (Regal86 remix)
songs.note: Remix by Monterrey producer Regal86 described as brutally hypnotic techno.

songs.title: A Fog
songs.note: Skittery bossa nova dub track on the surprise-drop album Slay Tracks.

songs.title: Tunnel
songs.note: Gurgling breakbeat acid track on the album Slay Tracks.

songs.title: Mint
songs.note: Misty, bass-heavy techno track on the album Slay Tracks.

songs.title: The Returner
songs.note: Rubbery trip-hop track on the album Slay Tracks.

songs.title: Stay In My Life
songs.note: Lavish timeless deep house track by Pops Roberts, pouring out of speakers like honey.

songs.title: Bad Trip
songs.note: Fizzing Caribbean-inflected funky house single from the Saffron collective, released with a sample pack.

songs.title: I Don't Care Until I Do
songs.note: Subterranean techno dub single from the Saffron collective, released with a sample pack.

songs.title: My Reward
songs.note: A standout banger with huge menacing hooks, likened to a lost No Trend B-side, from their five-track EP.

songs.title: Rental Girlfriend
songs.note: A catchy punk track kept in the tried-and-true style that runs through the Digital Pet LP.

songs.title: W.F.H.
songs.note: A mid-tempo, riff-driven track with a Big Star-esque rock 'n' roll feel, a prime example of the record's experimentation.

songs.title: Scared To Care
songs.note: Called a candidate for song of the year on the sophomore LP A Healthy Alternative.

songs.title: Evil Angels
songs.note: The title track of a two-song 7-inch, praised as a perfect single with a massive chorus hook.

songs.title: Lizard Kingdom
songs.note: The B-side to Evil Angels, described as equally great with a dizzying mid-tempo stomp.

songs.title: Colder Shade Blue
songs.note: An epic shoegaze-tinged punk banger from Oakland's Blue Zero, written by Marbled Eye's Chris Natividad.

songs.title: Chambers of Magic
songs.note: Praised as one of the most memorable vocal hooks on a metal album this year, with a sharp, sneaky lyrical line.

songs.title: Exhumation of the Womb's Splendour
songs.note: Opens the album by quickly showing all the key parts of the band's sound, from churning riffs to buried vocals.

songs.title: Aurora Cruoris
songs.note: Its intro is described as an almost warped, alternate-universe grunge ballad that adds breathing room to the album.

songs.title: Vikozhu Odin Ya Na Dorogu
songs.note: A nearly nine-minute folk reworking that interpolates Van Halen's "Ain't Talkin' 'Bout Love" into its arrangement.

songs.title: La brunante
songs.note: Cited, with "Dusk" as its translation, for an atmosphere that the reviewer says the influences like Foghat and AC/DC never reached.

songs.title: Les enfants de la nuit
songs.note: Named with "Children of the Night" as its translation as another standout example of the album's atmosphere.

songs.title: The Thief's Candle
songs.note: A dimmed-stage, Maiden-style soliloquy that shows frontman Meister Cagliostro's theatrical side.

songs.title: Synodus Horrenda
songs.note: An epic retelling of a macabre moment in Catholic history, the 9th-century posthumous papal trial.

songs.title: Thaw
songs.note: A Nine Inch Nails-inspired deep cut remade for the circle pit, with piano melodies and breakbeats on The Sin of Human Frailty.

songs.title: Twice Devoured Kill
songs.note: Lurching grindcore rhythms, guttural vocals from J.R. Hayes, and a fast, scattershot prog solo.

songs.title: For Anyone And You
songs.note: A dream pop track with a huge reverberating hook and angelic vocals from Gina Modotti; called the band's best yet.

songs.title: Better Off This Way
songs.note: An adrenaline-fueled garage track that the post highlights as a standout from the band's debut.

songs.title: Can I Borrow Your Lighter?
songs.note: Another garage highlight, praised for its adrenaline-fueled energy and economical songwriting.

songs.title: Clashing At the Party
songs.note: A trippy, reggae-infused track that shows the band's dub-tinged side.

songs.title: Blue Suzuki
songs.note: A dreamlike track with pillowy synths and a forward bassline that drifts into the next song on the compilation.

songs.title: Perhaps a State of Being
songs.note: A tranquil drone built from a series of sustained notes held to create calm.

songs.title: Sleepyhead
songs.note: A New Romantic R&B track that leads into a miragelike dubstep song on the compilation.

songs.title: Do Vesny
songs.note: A miragelike dubstep track that follows Violence of the Fauve's Sleepyhead late in the compilation.

songs.title: Human in the Loop
songs.note: A levitational, beat-less track the post says not to miss on her Machine Alliance release.

songs.title: Ode to the D
songs.note: Named as a Detroit-rooted track on Machine Alliance, closer to Robert Hood's minimalism.

songs.title: System & Structure
songs.note: Described as closer to Robert Hood's minimalism, with Kerrie's own personality stamped on it.

songs.title: One Last Dance
songs.note: A subdued Balearic track with sultry, grown-up fairytale feel that the post says is worth staying for.

songs.title: The Seven Line Prayer to Guru Rinpoche 莲师七句祈请文
songs.note: Rapid-fire chanting locked into complementary electronics, singled out as especially mind-warping.

songs.title: Commencement
songs.note: One side of a single, described in the post's list alongside its b-side Mineral Blend.

songs.title: Mineral Blend
songs.note: The b-side of a single, listed alongside Commencement in the post.

songs.title: Silly Girls
songs.note: Listed as the A-side of a single, with chirping, swooping trippy synths and rolling breaks.

songs.title: Ur Luv
songs.note: Listed as the b-side of a single with Silly Girls, in the post's jungle-focused recommendations.

songs.title: páirc béal uisce
songs.note: Cited as an example of the album's Irish folk influence, shown atmospherically through its verdant layering and sloped contours.

songs.title: tor head
songs.note: Named alongside páirc béal uisce as an example of the album's atmospheric nods to Irish folk traditions.

songs.title: Lucky
songs.note: Lead single with skittering d&b drum breaks over an interpolation of Linda Kiraly's 2007 song "Can't Let Go."

songs.title: ooh
songs.note: A sauntering appeal for satisfaction showing her airy, sultry, girlish persona.

songs.title: Ex Girlfriend
songs.note: Features Shygirl over a mellow reggaetón beat with strings and a choir.

songs.title: My Day Off
songs.note: A welcome bitch track with a trap beat and sharp lyrics about being left alone.

songs.title: ice
songs.note: Second single, described as a Timbaland-esque earworm featuring hip-hop duo They Hate Change.

songs.title: Soft Spot
songs.note: Cited as an example of young bedroom producers bringing drum & bass and UK garage into pop.

songs.title: Hawkmoon
songs.note: Segarra recalls a younger self with a buckknife, fake ID, and sleeping bag in the big city.

songs.title: The World Is Dangerous
songs.note: A duet with Conor Oberst that traces a relationship's drift in and out of the singer's life.

songs.title: Iron Mountain
songs.note: Title track with humming guitar and dreamlike, unsettling images above low-lit beauty.

songs.title: Lucile
songs.note: Follows the title track with surreal lyrics about a fisherman met on Lucile.

songs.title: Hush
songs.note: Opens the album with sludgy, blackened cosmonaut metal that moves into a hallucinogenic, focused heavy listen.

songs.title: Torre del serve
songs.note: Named as the album's paranoid, winding closer, ending the record's shifting journey.

songs.title: Venom
songs.note: Cited for its eccentric grooves, especially the hand percussion.

songs.title: BEST FRIEND/SWEET
songs.note: Sashaying funk opener where Holliday's ex fires back, forcing him to admit he sometimes hates himself.

songs.title: Little Yellow Bus
songs.note: Album highlight with warped 4-track acoustic guitar, recalling Cody ChesnuTT, about time travel to stop loving someone.

songs.title: What You're Looking For
songs.note: Disco-soul track that shows the album's eclectic range.

songs.title: Brown Eyes
songs.note: Electro-funk track cited as part of the album's stylistic variety.

songs.title: Ma Chi Sei – Ascoso
songs.note: Kim tiptoes over softly glowing synths, delivering words one tiny syllable at a time.

songs.title: Obsession – Indomita Mente
songs.note: Kim's reversed vocal runs into robotic effects over punchy bass, creating a woozy, elastic moment.

songs.title: She Said She Said
songs.note: Cover of the Beatles song, warped with gritty abrasiveness while respecting its psychedelia.

songs.title: Blue Jay Way
songs.note: Cover of the Beatles song, praised for its wild experimentalism on the covers record.

songs.title: Your Time
songs.note: Singled out as a convincing proof-of-concept blending shoegaze, slowcore, and emo.

songs.title: Stone
songs.note: Singled out as a convincing proof-of-concept that will appeal to Cloakroom or Nothing fans.

songs.title: The Madrigal
songs.note: Spooky girl group harmonizing that opens the album's retro sweetness.

songs.title: Mystic Spiral
songs.note: Bubblegum jangle in the vein of All Over the Place-era Bangles.

songs.title: Clown Song
songs.note: Bubblegum jangle in the vein of All Over the Place-era Bangles.

songs.title: Fell Into a Spell
songs.note: Bluesy and woozy number from the glossy Fantasy Now.

songs.title: Don't Make Sense
songs.note: Bluesy and woozy number from the glossy Fantasy Now.

songs.title: Aunt Maizy
songs.note: Smiley and flowery track from Fantasy Now.

songs.title: On A Cloud
songs.note: Smiley and flowery track from Fantasy Now.

songs.title: Dreads At The Monastery
songs.note: Suede raps about his music history and state surveillance over crunching drums and muted horns and keys.

songs.title: Excessive Celebration
songs.note: A dramatic track on the Reoccurring Characters release, with support from Duncecap.

songs.title: Cold Hue
songs.note: Curly Casto appears on this track from Reoccurring Characters.

songs.title: One Way Ticket
songs.note: Three MCs trade verses over a lurching, piano-laden backdrop with a horror-movie feel.

songs.title: South Beach
songs.note: A string-laden introductory cut on 12 Hour Shift that outlines the project's aims.

songs.title: All Mine
songs.note: A bittersweet relationship snapshot from the 12 Hour Shift collaboration.

songs.title: Feeling Fantastic
songs.note: A subtly upbeat track on 12 Hour Shift featuring three artists.

songs.title: Strange People
songs.note: The album closer, with singers and MCs taking turns over craggy drums and cushiony keys.

songs.title: WHTCHU SAY?
songs.note: The opening track of the album, with a grainy, lo-fi backdrop from GHOWSTE.

songs.title: RITUALS / BROTHERHOOD
songs.note: A mid-project highlight with sludgy bass and whispering keys.

songs.title: BIRDIE
songs.note: Strips the sound down to a plaintive acoustic guitar that sinks into fuzz.

songs.title: PINTO
songs.note: Sounds like a warped Spaghetti Western soundtrack, with the MC pondering time.

songs.title: SHEPHERD
songs.note: Fatboi Sharif joins on this closing chapter over a psych-influenced GHOWSTE production.

songs.title: Grimy Squadron Grow A Garden
songs.note: Investigates consumer-accepted technological surveillance over industrial production.

songs.title: Ghost Story
songs.note: The duo free associate over rumbling demonic bass and ambient distortion.

songs.title: God
songs.note: The closing track weighs how positive and negative ripple through life.

songs.title: Fast Talk Maturity
songs.note: An early highlight where Simpson shows humble pride over a kooky horn-infused funk slab.

songs.title: The Era That Doesn't Know
songs.note: A raucous guitar-spiked track with forceful lyrical assistance on the Escalation album.

songs.title: Stakeouts
songs.note: Quelle Chris guests on this track from Escalation.

songs.title: Chaos Is Merely Order Waiting To Be Deciphered
songs.note: An introspective track where Sue sounds out the soul-searching of the project.

songs.title: Dream Pop On Steroids
songs.note: The closer, where Sue finds a serene space over a dreamy backdrop with live keys.

songs.title: plz don't cut my wings
songs.note: Earl Sweatshirt closes this track with slurry, self-reflective thoughts over orchestral strings.

songs.title: U think Maybe?
songs.note: Liv.e and Venna combine on this track with rich, 80s soul vibes.

songs.title: Golden Hour
songs.note: Larry June brings slick patter to this sleazy jazz-funk track.

songs.title: Box Of Bullets
songs.note: Farris raps about hustling over percussion built from shuffling hi-hats and congas.

songs.title: Samples Of My Soul
songs.note: Farris references the cash-centric Righteous Gemstones over a flickering flute.

songs.title: Splashes Of Tragedy
songs.note: Big Rube blesses the track with philosophical thoughts on navigating one's ultimate fate.

songs.title: Whispers
songs.note: Pianist Kate Ledger plays chords and single notes, shadowed by her own halting vocal sounds, with a live electronic element.

songs.title: All English Music Is
songs.note: Written for Howard Skempton; amplified accordion sounds make sponges bounce across drawn staves, forcing real-time adjustment.

songs.title: Primo Libro
songs.note: James Weeks's opening work of 16 brief madrigals using a 31-tone scale, performed with meticulous precision.

songs.title: this is but an oration of loss
songs.note: Hannah Kendall's piece based on an M. NourbeSe Philip poem about enslaved Africans drowned in 1783, blending harmonica and vocal utterances.

songs.title: Moths
songs.note: A trio performance where slowly shifting gestures and microtonal wobbles create a kaleidoscopic, hypnotic effect.

songs.title: Pas
songs.note: A brief, elliptical opening piece surrounding slowly decaying notes with extended silence, serving as a prelude to Labyrinthine.

songs.title: Biliana
songs.note: Violin and wordless voice from Biliana Voutchkova form a resonant, glacial stream of closely tuned sustained lines.

songs.title: They bury their dead with great ululations
songs.note: A sorrowful work named for funeral wailing, performed by Ensemble Dal Niente with sensitivity and grace.

songs.title: Pillars
songs.note: A piano and alto saxophone duo with Geoffrey Landman that seeks to embody Netzer's core compositional principles.

songs.title: I AM SO FUCKING ZEN
songs.note: A deliciously microtonal work performed with precision by the saxophone quartet ~Nois.

songs.title: All Life Long
songs.note: A meditative, downward-drifting organ piece toggling through microscopic harmonic adjustments, with a choral version also discussed.

songs.title: Dust/Light
songs.note: An assemblage of intermittent small sounds that the post calls stunning and says reaches deep into the listener's mind.

songs.title: To Live is Inherently Succumb to Chaos
songs.note: A track with dark electronic pulses and noisescapes that the post finds surprisingly calm and nearly orderly.

songs.title: Friend Boat
songs.note: A broke-machine ballad that squiggles and curls skyward, singled out as the writer's favorite patient, meditative side.

songs.title: Frog Lift
songs.note: A yearning track that turns string strains and pipe-organ-style breaths into something like a sonic prayer ritual.

songs.title: I Saw The Cure in '94
songs.note: The final track, a slightly more upbeat jaunt that adds some humor to an otherwise dark, eerie album.

songs.title: Interwhining
songs.note: A rollicking track praised for rocking with the force of a metal band unleashed from its genre chains.

songs.title: Echolocation
songs.note: The title piece, a rollicking jam that the post says rocks hard with a fiery approach suited to now.

songs.title: III
songs.note: A 13-minute piece that escalates and soars toward the sun while gathering wind and rain along the way.

songs.title: Fifteen Minute Drills…
songs.note: Melancholy soul track on THUG ZINE 003 with warnings about precious metals and celebrating freedom from vendettas.

songs.title: Patron Saint (for Ka)
songs.note: Closes THUG ZINE 003 by setting archived interviews with the departed poet Ka over a solemn backdrop.

songs.title: PLUG ONE
songs.note: Opener of IN SPACE… bopping over stripped-down drums and jaunty keys, with lyrics on pyramids and Aretha Franklin.

songs.title: EVERY MORNING…
songs.note: Eight-minute beat-shifting standout from IN SPACE… that showcases the chemistry between Bryson and Blu.

songs.title: Sofa King Grim
songs.note: Title track of the album, with swarming bass tones under braggadocio, gallows humor, and reflections.

songs.title: False Prophets
songs.note: Bluesy street rap parable with '80s horror-flick bass, pained guitar, and sampled televangelist voices.

songs.title: Saba
songs.note: Sun-kissed soul track from The Weight Of The World, with serene synths and cozy static, described as a winter head-bop.

songs.title: Spellcasted Television
songs.note: Jagged, gnarly guitar beat from Genuine Dexterity, featuring guest verses from billy woods and ELUCID.

songs.title: Sangria
songs.note: Jeff Markey-produced track from ceci n'est pas un portrait with a grinding backdrop and gruff raps.

songs.title: zugzwang
songs.note: Wobbly funk track that the post calls the peak of ceci n'est pas un portrait.

songs.title: the book of job part ii
songs.note: Roper Williams production of tiptoeing piano and gliding strings on ceci n'est pas un portrait.

songs.title: dismiss the fear of being you
songs.note: Foule Monk beat of murky kicks and snares on ceci n'est pas un portrait.

songs.title: the pollyanna principle
songs.note: Markey's nervy, clandestine-terror closer to ceci n'est pas un portrait.

songs.title: Peachfuzz
songs.note: Instrumental reinterpretation of MF DOOM's work with harder, clattering drums giving a bleaker outlook.

songs.title: Doomsday
songs.note: Instrumental reinterpretation with sinewy guitar lines and plucked guitar replacing the original scratches.

songs.title: One Beer
songs.note: Instrumental reinterpretation of the original kooky bop, turned into a graceful mystical workout.

songs.title: The Gas Face
songs.note: Curiously brooding instrumental take on 3rd Bass's track, included as a nod to DOOM's debut.

songs.title: Fire Country
songs.note: Opening track on COUNTRY; its folk-country and art-pop blend feels self-assured and immediately absorbing to the writer.

songs.title: Mother's Daughter
songs.note: Another opening track on COUNTRY, praised for its unselfconscious blend and the dreamy summer atmosphere it creates.

songs.title: Atoll
songs.note: A strummy, cruising track that poetically critiques U.S. imperialism in the Pacific, referencing the 1954 Bravo nuclear test.

songs.title: Exmilitary
songs.note: Guitar-heavy track where a sampled loop gets trampled by power chords, and it includes a confession about the cost of tweeting.

songs.title: New Black History
songs.note: Praised for its 1970s synth minimalism, one of the record's most striking production moments.

songs.title: Don't Put Anything On the Bible
songs.note: Described as haunting, centered on a gorgeous, ghostly vocal from Buzzy Lee.

songs.title: JPEGULTRA!
songs.note: Contains a punchline the writer found especially funny, and it's one of the record's standout jokes.

songs.title: Jihad Joe
songs.note: Exposes the rapper's internal conflict about internet fame, with lines about self-respect and being terminally online.

songs.title: Sunday Robe
songs.note: Named among songs on Golden Pear, with fluttering effects and bright melodic beams that the post calls New Age-y yet earnest.

songs.title: Plant Shop
songs.note: Named among songs on Golden Pear, which the post describes as easygoing and verdant with twinkly, bright melodies.

songs.title: Wild Marionberries
songs.note: Named among songs on Golden Pear, which the post describes as easygoing and verdant with twinkly, bright melodies.

songs.title: In the Crosshairs
songs.note: Named among cuts that filter steel pan through disco, funk, and soul into multi-faceted grooves.

songs.title: Hazy Memories
