songs.note: Cited as one of the tracks building dynamic, multi-layered grooves from steel pan fusion.

songs.title: Treasure Quest
songs.note: Highlighted alongside other cuts for capitalizing on the band's instrumental proficiency.

songs.title: Harlequin
songs.note: Singled out as a peppy highlight where the band's new in-the-room sound makes retro pop songs work.

songs.title: Temple of the Mind
songs.note: Called a breezy highlight, showing the band turning retro pop vibes into proper songs.

songs.title: Diamonds, Rhinestones, and Hard Rain
songs.note: The album's sole exception to its instrumentals: a measured '60s psych-pop title track with a flanged, sing-song chorus.

songs.title: Eyes like Dead Stars
songs.note: A shape-shifting, kraut-leaning instrumental from the album that stretches well past seven minutes.

songs.title: Catamaran
songs.note: A long, hallucinatory instrumental from the album that the writer cites as an example of its far-out journey.

songs.title: GLE450
songs.note: Praised for the spy-theme guitar Kyo Itachi lays through the track on this odds-and-ends compilation.

songs.title: Akbar Pray Day
songs.note: Singled out for the creepy, horror-movie-style piano score D-Styles places beneath the track.

songs.title: My Kind
songs.note: Its scattered intro collapses into lockstep formation, cited as an example of Middleman's nebulous songcraft.

songs.title: Rewind
songs.note: Highlighted for the whooshes of white noise burbling behind it on Bite Down.

songs.title: May It Be On Offer
songs.note: Described as a heavenly prayer, cited as one of the album's most striking moments.

songs.title: Dragonfruit
songs.note: Named as an example of the maximalist, feel-good arrangements on the band's ambitious third album.

songs.title: Wisteria
songs.note: Named as an example of the radiant digital textures on Fruit Galaxy, music meant for dancing and dreaming.

songs.title: Right Back to It
songs.note: Quoted for its warm, comforting take on devotion, showing the album's homier, more conversational scope.

songs.title: Crowbar
songs.note: Its guitar line is said to resemble something lifted from R.E.M.'s Out of Time, showing the album's countryfied sound.

songs.title: Grain
songs.note: Drum rattles morph into a heavy, guitar-like drone on this snare drum piece that uses mics and amps for feedback.

songs.title: Hold
songs.note: Drumming recedes into near-silence before returning as grinding noise, in a track built from snare drum soundscapes.

songs.title: The Loss
songs.note: Opener launching with rough cello scrapings and short saxophone puffs that intensify until they sound ready to explode.

songs.title: Attempted Recreation
songs.note: A see-saw of racket that reaches cacophony even faster, following the opener on this duo's release.

songs.title: This One is For You
songs.note: Heavily distorted viola notes balanced with moments of reflection and pause, from a live performance recording.

songs.title: Arcus
songs.note: A quiet opening of sparse chords that grows into a denser, heated web, live at Sonic Acts.

songs.title: You must have quite a little big problem
songs.note: The yelping closer of this vocal and trumpet duo's album, described as serious fun with a bubbling mix.

songs.title: Where Do You Come From?
songs.note: Nostalgic opener recalling childhood baseball cards, Tone Loc and Young MC, and shoplifting cassettes.

songs.title: L.A. Underground
songs.note: Celebrates the rapper's home city and invites Will.i.am to revisit his pre-pop roots.

songs.title: KMD Mr. Hood Vibes
songs.note: Carefree track nodding to Zev Love X, Subroc, and Onyx's early 90s debut.

songs.title: Champion
songs.note: Reggae-tinged track featuring Mickey Factz flowing over the beat.

songs.title: Seckle
songs.note: Stripped-down cut with KRS-One bringing his booming voice and boom-bap manifesto.

songs.title: B-Ville Pioneers
songs.note: Lurching call to arms with General Steele and Lil Fame.

songs.title: My Year
songs.note: Late-project cut with a posthumous verse from Trugoy of De La Soul, recalling their early opening-act days.

songs.title: Sniper Tower
songs.note: Crucial cut with a chugging backdrop and cascading guitar, full of scams and violent threats.

songs.title: WE ALL
songs.note: Cherubic boom-bap track produced by Kaelin-Ellis, with Thomas sounding relaxed on the beat.

songs.title: GOTTA GET UP
songs.note: Sweeping motivational call-to-action delivered with Thomas's nimble flow.

songs.title: CRASHING DOWN
songs.note: Penultimate track with Blu3 Boy and Chris Patrick rallying against fake authenticity marketing.

songs.title: Poets, Politricks & Propaganda (10" Mix)
songs.note: Album standout where Myka-9 scorns oppressive structures and nods to Fela Kuti.

songs.title: art of war
songs.note: Broody bass-driven track of subway wandering that ends in a soul-searching vignette.

songs.title: Redbone Blues
songs.note: Rags on judging success by digital metrics, with a guest verse from Slug.

songs.title: Wicked
songs.note: Tone Spliff and Bobby J From Rockaway trade verses over the track.

songs.title: Put It Inna Book
songs.note: Haunting sax riff and jagged drums under Muja's litany of societal ills and peeves.

songs.title: Had To Improve
songs.note: Motivational mantra cushioned by jazz-fusion synth lines.

songs.title: Give Way
songs.note: Optimistic track bringing in rock and spoken word.

songs.title: World On Fire
songs.note: Empathetic state-of-the-world reportage with an extended jazz coda.

songs.title: Thankful For
songs.note: Driven by a tricky Moroccan-influenced drum pattern that Oddisee rides with confidence.

songs.title: Showbiz
songs.note: Woozy Child Actor-crafted opener with the trio introducing themselves and nodding to Digital Underground.

songs.artist: Open Mike Eagle, Video Dave & STILL RIFT
songs.title: Pliers
songs.note: Lurching psych-funk track with Eagle reflecting on time-hopping and personal memories.

songs.title: Steel Pan Labyrinth
songs.note: Guest MC Lungs worships hidden deities in a church basement over murmuring production.

songs.title: Nutkracker Blues
songs.note: Breezly Brewin slinks over moonlight bass while questioning how to keep innocence.

songs.title: Illusions Of P
songs.note: PremRock codifies the ShrapKnel credo over murky low-end tones.

songs.title: Star Frog Dilla
songs.note: Trio's previously released track that opens West Mineral's LP; ost's remix release collects reworkings of it, from shoegaze to deconstructed pop.

songs.title: Cash, Mere Dreams
songs.note: Opener from Blacc Kanzou, with luxurious food boasts over a graceful backdrop from producer Malek Winter.

songs.artist: Da Flyy Hooligan & Knowledge The Pirate
songs.title: Supreme Kush
songs.note: Knowledge The Pirate joins the MC over a gently humming, elegiac-synth backdrop for streetwise philosophies.

songs.title: BLACK FLAG FREESTYLE
songs.note: Early track from King Of The Mischievous South Vol. 2 featuring Texas rapper That Mexican OT over bass-heavy production.

songs.title: SKED
songs.note: Project Pat guest verse over a bass-swamped beat on this Southern rap-inspired mixtape.

songs.title: G'Z UP
songs.note: Features 2 Chainz bringing a mainstream presence to this Southern-leaning mixtape track.

songs.title: Dot vs Dilla
songs.note: Asserts New York credentials and salutes Deric D-Dot Angelettie; an extended standalone version also exists.

songs.title: The Letter P!
songs.note: Alliteration-heavy rhymes over production repurposed from Capital Steez and MF DOOM on The Y.O.U Tape.

songs.title: Fetus
songs.note: Opener balancing anguished lines about crooked cops and atomic bombs over a sorrowful, swaying piano.

songs.title: The Hours
songs.note: Guest SKECH185 delivers a lament about life being b-roll over distorted radio and ambient noise.

songs.title: Psychedelics Wrote The Bible
songs.note: Title track using a recurring nervy chime as a metronomic device, with references to A Tribe Called Quest and Miles Davis.

songs.title: Alligator Skin
songs.note: Loon raps about lobster tails and Gucci sandals while Watson adds a verse over a creeping, bass-heavy backdrop.

songs.title: Pink 50s
songs.note: Whispering menace from Swamp Water with a guest verse from Wizz Havvinn.

songs.title: I Don't Rave
songs.note: Father glides over doleful piano and backwards tape loops on this Swamp Water track.

songs.title: Send A Box
songs.note: Lil Scumbag brings an agitated presence and Mike Jones references to this Swamp Water track.

songs.title: ERANU/UVAVU
songs.note: Lapgan's remix gives a hypnotic charm to Acne's boasts about being a rhyme Dionysus.

songs.title: EAT RIGHT
songs.note: Pitch 92 adds a digi-funk swagger to this HAUNTED CODEX remix.

songs.title: HEALTHY NORMALZ
songs.note: Tom Caruna's flip is built around a cascading celestial synth line.

songs.title: Megaloblast
songs.note: Soothing strings underpin Sonnyjim alternating English and Punjabi, followed by a tribute to Sidhu Moose Wala.

songs.title: Bappi Lahiri
songs.note: Simmering, staticky track with jabs at the UK Independent Party and a guest tirade from MONGO.

songs.title: Rehab
songs.note: Opener from Wayward Skies exploring donning psychological masks to navigate society over live guitar and drums.

songs.title: Sunny Water
songs.note: Champions taking small steps forward to create better days ahead, on stripped-down acoustic instrumentation.

songs.title: A Way Back In
songs.note: Raw Poetic considers his creative longevity and claims to master hip-hop for the older intellectual.

songs.title: Take Your Mind Someplace Else
songs.note: Political commentary and a bleak economic prophecy over fuzzy bass and rolling drums on Honest.

songs.title: Frieze the Week
songs.note: Quelle Chris and Buddy Peace appear on this Basquiat-referencing track.

songs.title: Heaven Can Wait
songs.note: NAHreally navigates the buzzsaw bass of this Honest track.

songs.title: Candid
songs.note: Mike Ladd attacks the electro-tinged track with criticisms of late capitalism.

songs.title: Peace GOD
songs.note: Muted brass lines support Fev's rhymes about life lessons and feeling out of touch on Strapped.

songs.title: OA
songs.note: Written in 2018; unfolds slowly with layered instruments, silences, feedback swells, and a Fender Rhodes that shifts the mood.

songs.title: FG
songs.note: Written five years later for the same ensemble; slow pace, more stripped down, with acoustic colors radiating from arcing feedback.

songs.title: Pitch and Whine
songs.note: Juke/booty bass track with pinging 808s and a hip-wiggle groove, per the post.

songs.title: Stop (Call Mi Phone)
songs.note: Straight-up bashment riddim with vocals from Lateena, giving it a low-key swagger.

songs.title: Fear Me
songs.note: Spiky, percussive track blending early grime, Polygon Window-era Aphex Twin and Chicago house.

songs.title: Quicksand
songs.note: Detuned, liquid-feeling track with querulous vocals and kickdrums that later hit like thrown rocks.

songs.title: L'Oseille
songs.note: Jamz Supernova and Sam Interface remix mixing Diwali riddim clap-alongs with CSS-like indie-electro vibes.

songs.title: Força
songs.note: Dwells remix that turns the track into a flying-dream trance rush.

songs.title: La Mano
songs.note: Denzel Himself remix twisting it into an episodic hip-hop piece that recalls Tricky.

songs.title: The Other
songs.note: Scratcha DVA remix dissolving it into a nightmarish soup of bass, reverb and snare crashes, keeping its song structure.

songs.title: I Can't Sleep
songs.note: First new tracks in years from the label's Slaughter Mob project; dark, paranoid and shuffling.

songs.title: All in My Head
songs.note: Another new Slaughter Mob track, described as dark and swerving with paranoid titling.

songs.title: Valentine
songs.note: One of the EP's last two tracks, described as absolutely heartbroken.

songs.title: Core Memories
songs.note: Closing track that the post says finds stillness amid the most furious movement and noise.

songs.title: Into the Dark
songs.note: Opening track, an improvisatory exploration of texture and extended technique that begins forming a fractured vocal melody in its final 90 seconds.

songs.title: Love III
songs.note: Gathers the anticipatory fragments from earlier tracks and turns them into a gorgeous tune showcasing Ratkje's full-throated lyrical singing.

songs.artist: Eric Wubbels, Josh Modney, Mariel Roberts
songs.title: endings
songs.note: Opening movement of an eight-movement work, with Wubbels's oblique chord set against sustained just-intonation double stops from the strings.

songs.artist: Eric Wubbels, Josh Modney, Mariel Roberts
songs.title: tombeau
songs.note: Second movement that moves the piano to the focal point, with the strings grinding against glassy arpeggios and flickering runs.

songs.title: stutter-step the concept
songs.note: Opening piece, a contrapuntal work of jagged stops and starts, written in 2016 for Ensemble Dal Niente and performed with precision and energy.

songs.title: Vapours
songs.note: Written for Quartetto Maurice, an ensemble work of fluctuating string lines that Bertucci named after a historical diagnosis of hysteria in women.

songs.title: Flax
songs.note: Epic solo piano work performed by Kerry Yong, with tonalities that stop wiggling about halfway through and settle into a more restricted terrain.

songs.artist: Cassandra Miller, Linda Catlin Smith, Laurence Crane
songs.title: The City, Full of People
songs.note: Miller's choral piece, with singers scattered around the audience in six clusters, setting melodies sung along to Tallis's Lamentations.

songs.title: Folio
songs.note: Choral work using Emily Dickinson's poetry, with a gracefully changing landscape that feels more modern and deftly mirrors a sense of detachment.

songs.title: String Quartet No. 2
songs.note: Slow-moving quartet with stark voicings, performed leisurely by the Esposito Quartet, deconstructing timeless string quartet cadences into something modern.

songs.title: Seagrass
songs.note: Title piece by Adrianne Munden-Dixon, transposed for viola by Frey, with shifting complexions held together by an agile, elegant navigation.

songs.title: Zastrugi
songs.note: Written by Adrianne Munden-Dixon for the violist, described as a beautifully skittering piece.

songs.title: No Reading/if this were ever sounded
songs.note: Adapted from an ensemble version with fixed media into a solo piece using just intonation, with dense, thorny zig-zags and molasses-thick harmony.

songs.title: Choros
songs.note: By Maria Kaoutzani, toggling between dark serenity and jacked-up intensity while imagining a series of disparate rooms the violist moves through.

songs.title: Inhabit Inhibition Space #1
songs.note: Ensemble Mosaik performs this abstract piece, where feedback is tamed and woven into acoustic instruments.

songs.title: inhabit_inhibit
songs.note: EnsembleKollektiv Berlin performs this spatialized work, with feedback soloists interacting with acoustic quartets.

songs.title: under_current
songs.note: Electric guitar slashes and riffs against the BBC Scottish Symphony Orchestra, conducted by Ilan Volkov.

songs.title: An Atlas of Deep Time
songs.note: A slow, rumbling orchestral work spanning planetary history, performed by the South Dakota Symphony Orchestra.

songs.title: Distances Bending
songs.note: Synthesizer, quarter-tone flutes, violin and cello shift slowly through harmonic series tones across six movements.

songs.title: Rewild
songs.note: Ghost Ensemble's long, slowly unfolding piece about repairing damaged ecosystems, which bends the listener's sense of time.

songs.title: ghost geography
songs.note: Wesley Shen plays a solo piano work over a persistent electronic drone, inspired by the North Saskatchewan River.

songs.title: pale forms in uncommon light
songs.note: Luciane Cardassi performs this five-movement piano work, where the drone rises and falls against the piano notes.

songs.title: Mountainweeps
songs.note: A brief triptych for cello, written for Arlen Hlusko, reflecting alpine environments degraded by climate change.

songs.title: Sparks an empty pool
songs.note: A piece from a nine-year project mixing live instruments and field recordings, pierced by a blast of Thai pop.

songs.title: Blackwing
songs.note: A sparse solo bass clarinet piece with patient, swooping lines, played by Heather Roche.

songs.title: Lamento
songs.note: A violin duo by Mira Benjamin and Chihiro Ono, described as an elegant close-harmony dance.

songs.title: String Quartet #6
songs.note: A substantial quartet favoring sonic ambiguity and dense polyphonic thickets over formal perfection.

songs.title: Allégorie
songs.note: Clara Levy plays this piece of delicate overtones, sparkling vibrato and pizzicato plucks, which feels light but hits hard.

songs.title: Listening Into Silence
songs.note: A lengthy piece filled with rests whose lengths the performer chooses, drawing the listener into the silences.

songs.title: Wha Happen
songs.note: Dubstep, grime and trap cuts flow together; Trim's threats sound oddly joyous. Instrumental version and a grime-electro mix by K-65 also noted.

songs.title: Plenty
songs.note: A dub-reggae-influenced dubstep creeper with MC Logan Olm moving between reggae proclamation and grime rhyming.

songs.title: Freak in the Streets
songs.note: Listed among the post's recommended club tracks this month.

songs.title: Fractures
songs.note: Techno-based record themed around the Europa Clipper mission, pairing cosmic textures with dancefloor propulsion.

songs.title: Back
songs.note: Five tracks made with an unnamed new tool, with shifting tempos and sounds gliding into one another.

songs.title: The Drowned City
songs.note: Jungle micro-edits alongside ambient and Burial-like two-step tracks, released via Ilian Tape.

songs.title: Cano 6 Your Code is Your Code
songs.note: Detroit EP that the post lists among its weighty, genre-bending selections this month.

songs.title: WFO
songs.note: Listed among the roundup's picks, from a comeback collection of old and new tunes.

songs.title: Those Kinds of Friends
songs.note: Listed among the post's recommended tracks this month, with no further detail given.

songs.title: Crooked Transmissions
songs.note: Listed among the post's recommended tracks this month, with no further detail given.

songs.title: Unity
songs.note: Three manic breakcore tracks from a Ukrainian producer, with melancholic introspection beneath the high-velocity sound.

songs.title: Trumpets
songs.note: Afro-house hybrid blending South African gqom space with driving trance arpeggios for a peak-time track.

songs.title: Life Is
songs.note: Opening track of Here in the Pitch; its 60s-pop sound gives way to a darker, surreal atmosphere than it first suggests.

songs.title: I Don't Love You
songs.note: A glitchy piano ballad on Cyan Blue that also offers olive branches alongside its scorn.

songs.title: Canopy
songs.note: A throwback diss track on Cyan Blue with scathing lines, ending on an uneasy question about sameness.

songs.title: Fiqexpert
songs.note: Fearsome bass drone pressure with electro-house synth swoops and traditional plucked instruments.

songs.title: VUGUVUGUU
songs.note: High-drama sweaty techno, singled out as a standout cut from the Blacksea Não Maya crew member.

songs.title: BATESTE
songs.note: Described as sounding like a rusty robot carnival.

songs.title: Shaman
songs.note: An epic finale that threatens to lift whole dancefloors into other realms.

songs.title: Rhythm of Love
songs.note: Blissed-out, sun-kissed Balearic bumper with rippling pianos, string parts, and a Latin syncopation hint; features Cata Mansikka-aho.

songs.title: Maybe Neggst Time
songs.note: Trip-hop built from goofy old horror and spy movie samples, with an English egg-pun title.

songs.title: Groove Eggspert
songs.note: Another egg-pun trip-hop track that mixes retro samples with fresh-sounding Ninja Tune and Ghost Box echoes.

songs.title: Juggernaut
songs.note: A reboot of his classic purple sound, with half-step grime patterns and P-Funk synths squirming through.

songs.title: S-Wave
songs.note: Grimier than before, with swooping bleeping square-wave synths and orchestral stabs jabbing in.

songs.title: Sweet Powder White
songs.note: A narcotic loping dub funk track with heavy early Andrew Weatherall hints.

songs.title: Re/fractions
songs.note: Closing work commissioned by Mystery Sonata's duo; described as a ravishing piece that closes the Aequora album.

songs.title: Notre Dame
songs.note: Two-movement meditation adapted for violin and piano from its harp-and-violin original, with thick overtones.

songs.title: Reminiscence
songs.note: Austere solo piano work that threads dark melody through bold extended techniques, performed by Gajić.

songs.title: Ballade.Rauschen
songs.note: Extended monophonic piano centerpiece, played by Yumi Suehiro, that accelerates and decelerates over about 22 minutes.

songs.title: Das Summen Meiner Teile
songs.note: Centerpiece of Summen, built from notes he wrote at age seven, with a string quartet and his drumming.

songs.title: Two Instances
songs.note: Opening duo with cellist Matthias Lorenz, a game of anticipation built on pizzicato melodies.

songs.title: Eight Notes
songs.note: Newest and longest duo piece with Beinhauer and Lorenz, a mesmerizing improvised back-and-forth.

songs.title: Rhythm, Presence, Voice
songs.note: Fully notated work for string quartet and piano, with Reinier van Houdt's sharp piano stabs.

songs.title: Trees
songs.note: Minimalist opener of the clarinet quartet album, with stately unison patterns that feel like a liturgical work.

songs.title: For 4 Clarinets
songs.note: Meticulously fluttering study of acoustic beating and shimmering long tones abraded by upper-register dissonance.

songs.title: Olim
songs.note: Reed quartet piece that draws outside the compositional lines with sly contrapuntal ticks, trills, and accents.

songs.title: Ubique
songs.note: Quartet work from Density 21.5's 10th cycle, with electronics, moving from ethereal grace to turbulent tension.

songs.title: TERRARIUM
songs.note: Sound map of the Irish Midlands performed by the 10-member Crash Ensemble, with wild dynamic shifts.

songs.title: Drishti
songs.note: Ten-movement violin work braiding Western classical and Hindustani music, performed by Simone Porter.

songs.title: Lachen Verlernt
songs.note: Chaconne for violin with slashing intensity and a midway crescendo, performed by Simone Porter.

songs.title: Improvisation on O Virtus Sapientiae
songs.note: Gorgeous swirling but measured piece based on Hildegard von Bingen's 12th-century antiphon.

songs.title: passage: time (copy)
songs.note: Opening violin piece performed by Miranda Cuckson that borrows and transforms quotations from earlier composers.

songs.title: Chorale (those driven out will come)
songs.note: String quartet with extended techniques and spiked harmonies, drawing on Beethoven's Op. 132, played by Quartet121.

songs.title: Banishing the Iris of Sempiternal Tenebrosity
songs.note: Lord Kaiju flips between vocal styles to recreate the Gamera 3 final battle; the post calls it invigorating.

songs.title: The Plight of a Sorcerer
songs.note: A diary of a failed Merlin figure whose ignominious path ends with ogres sucking marrow from bone.

songs.title: Rose Arbor
songs.note: An enigmatic parable about a superstitious king and a miraculous rosebush.

songs.title: Chapter for Not Being Hung Upside Down on a Stake in the Underworld and Made to Eat Feces by the Four Apes
songs.note: A fast, brutal track the post singles out; it leads straight into the sub-two-minute "To Strike with Secret Fang."

songs.title: To Strike with Secret Fang
songs.note: A sub-two-minute blast that follows "Four Apes" and evokes a circle pit.

songs.title: Fucked with a Broken Bottle
songs.note: Cited as one of the confrontationally brutal tracks on Duck Face Killings.

songs.title: Human Scalp Collection
songs.note: Cited alongside the album's brutal material as a confrontational highlight.

songs.title: Aristocratic Suicidal Black Metal
songs.note: Described as a future live staple with a tectonic groove, comparable to a prior song's status.

songs.title: Less and Less Human, O Savage Spirit
songs.note: A highlight for drummer Illusory, who finds a pocket even at ungodly tempos.

songs.title: A Coin Upon the Tongue
songs.note: Has a couple of guitar solos said to sound like they fell off Judas Priest's private plane.

songs.title: Top of the Sky
songs.note: A kaleidoscopic ballad where the band rises to meet vocalist Elin Larsson.

songs.title: Somebody Better
songs.note: A sultry track where the band rises to meet Elin Larsson's powerhouse vocals.

songs.title: Goodbye, Hotel Arkada
songs.note: Six-track album for Ghostly with guest features from The Cure and Slowdive members; a snapshot of her accessible formula.

songs.title: Dissolution Grip
songs.note: Three lengthy compositions warping found-sound samples into melodic waveforms; first release for his label OFNOT.

songs.title: Fake Sleep
songs.note: Unsettling, uncanny ambient record for Stroom pairing three new tracks with 13 previously released ones.

songs.title: Personal Problems
songs.note: Six tracks of blunt vocals over whimsical piano and string playing; tender, tear-jerking and slightly eerie.

songs.title: Klima
songs.note: Ten pieces built on piano, bass flute and field recordings, written for a Portuguese UNESCO site and recorded later.

songs.title: small circle
songs.note: Serrated white noise and lush pads form one disorienting movement, a departure from his gentler past work.

songs.title: Foreign Smokes
songs.note: Four sprawling tracks running raga, blues and space rock through an airy filter, with Bill Mackay.

songs.title: Pathways
songs.note: Six tracks blending dub techno, downtempo and spacey lounge into weightless, wooly, floaty worlds.

songs.title: Hot Plate Only
songs.note: Nine tracks merging pastel electronics and jazzy acoustic playing, with chipper recorders, clarinets and accordions.

songs.title: Hot Fruit
songs.note: Improvisational record of rambling, organic tones tying left-field instrumental music to American folk.

songs.title: Didion
songs.note: Fourth track on Liberated Gesture, described as a transformative moment where the album's winding paths come into focus.

songs.title: Supernatural
songs.note: Post praises its high-arcing, almost post-rock build and a scorching chorus that hit the writer hard.

songs.title: Silver Dollars
songs.note: Post describes Christmas sneering and yelling over an avalanche of drums and guitar with forceful intensity.

songs.title: It Means What It Means
songs.note: Post highlights its lyric "Don't miss the healing/ in search of the cure" as a summary of the album's outlook.

songs.title: Indigo
songs.note: Post cites Spencer Ouellette lobbing wailing synths into the abyss on this track as a standout performance.

songs.title: Soft Prey
songs.note: Post says Ouellette applies metal solo techniques to saxophone and lap steel on this track.

songs.title: Descent of Sinuous Corrdiros
songs.note: Post notes gothic piano arpeggios on this track as an example of unexpected arrangements.

songs.title: Ring
songs.note: Post says it features haunting Anna Holmer vocals and sounds like Dead Can Dance with Burial in a steel mausoleum.

songs.title: Manges La Pomme
songs.note: Post says it smears a wobbly vocal line across menacing tones.

songs.title: Olive Green
songs.note: Post says this track plunges industrial music into an acid bath.

songs.title: The Beaten Path Made Flesh
songs.note: Named as an example of how extended blast beat sections whip songs into swells of dark fury on Affection & Vengeance.

songs.title: Purple Curtains
songs.note: Cited alongside the opener as a song where blast beat sections build into dark, furious swells.

songs.title: Tomb Corpse Haruspex
songs.note: The 15-minute closing track of From the Visceral Abyss, praised for blending death, black metal, and noise with grace.

songs.title: My Rocket Crashed in Uranus
songs.note: A Steel Beast song whose absurd title the writer uses to explain why the earnest, lo-fi speed metal is worth hearing.

songs.title: Scions of Teal Plumage
songs.note: Named the winner of the Four Sorrows split, standing out among four atmospheric black metal acts.

songs.title: city17
songs.note: A collaboration paying homage to turn-of-the-century New Age, built on sherbet-soft pads, floaty leads, and Japan field recordings.

songs.title: superbath (2024 remaster)
songs.note: The gentlest end of Special Guest DJ, stretching a misty drone and elusive melodies over 24 minutes.

songs.title: Quarter Tone Sub
songs.note: Choppy bass and broken-beat drums recall 2010s trap, with a glassy, icy quality under dramatic compression.

songs.title: Sirendaze / July 2020
songs.note: An 11-minute two-movement composition built on manipulated field recordings and shoegaze-y distortion, searing and ruminative.

songs.title: Insecure
songs.note: A mournful violin line rises about a minute and a half in, floating over the song's insistent rhythm.

songs.title: Get Up
songs.note: Despite its anthemic title, it's a squelching, wormy track sporadically hit by rat-a-tat snares.

songs.title: Handcuff Escape
songs.note: Uses the handcuff escape as a metaphor for Moses breaking free of material temptations and those who would block his rise.

songs.title: I Thought You Knew
songs.note: The album's most wrenching track, recounting Moses's homelessness at 16 and his recovery from a metaphorical death.

songs.title: Golden Hour
songs.note: Shows a strong Southern California influence, evoking cruising in a car at sunset.

songs.title: That's Life
songs.note: Features call-and-response group harmonies and has an inklings of a Beach Boys-style '60s pop song.

songs.title: I Would Let You
songs.note: A fabulous piano ballad that flies into a fuzzed-out guitar solo.

songs.title: Bon Voyage
songs.note: The closing track, showing off the psych rock influences Li brought to her debut.

songs.title: Nightshift
songs.note: One of the heavier, more grunge-inflected songs on the band's debut EP.

songs.title: Gas Station
songs.note: One of the heavier, more grunge-inflected songs on the band's debut EP.

songs.title: Manic Pixie Dream Girl
songs.note: An indie-ish track that balances the heavier songs on the seven-track EP.

songs.title: Slaves of Myth
songs.note: An excoriating track from Infected by Myth that pushes back against Botswana's hostility toward death metal.

songs.title: Silenced Voice of Holy
songs.note: Another excoriating song from Infected by Myth, confronting the culture that suppresses death metal in Botswana.

songs.title: Overthrust Deathmental
songs.note: A self-mythologizing anthem the post compares to Iron Maiden's "Iron Maiden," easy to imagine sparking a wild mosh pit.

songs.title: Scorched Vision
songs.note: An 11-minute track, the most convoluted on The Promise of Rain, yet it follows a coherent, twisted internal logic.

songs.title: Motormentor
songs.note: A track where the band's tongue-in-cheek attitude shows, though the post says it is not musical unseriousness.

songs.title: Traumatized in Traffic Jam Ejection
songs.note: A playfully irreverent track from From Gravel to Grave that the post cites alongside "Motormentor" as showing the band's humor.

songs.title: Duality
songs.note: A 16-minute album-closing title track the post calls a haunted labyrinth and a jaw-dropping expression of the band's ambition.

songs.title: Canícula
songs.note: An epic ballad duet with bossa nova singer Isadora Melo, switching from English to Portuguese, called the record's most exciting track.

songs.title: The Timeless All and Nothing
songs.note: Singled out as the stellar exception on The Dark Path to the Light, led by Misþyrming frontman Dagur Gíslason.

songs.title: Lost Civilizations
songs.note: The neo-folk-tinged intro to The Dark Path to the Light, said to build a rich world in about three minutes.

songs.title: Sigil Strider
songs.note: A stomping, mid-paced rocker that the post cites as an example of the album's old-school heavy metal homage.

songs.title: The Prophecy
songs.note: A moodier track on Time Immortal Wept, cited alongside the album's stomping rockers as a highlight.

songs.title: Time Immortal Wept
songs.note: The nearly 12-minute title track of the album, cited as a highlight of the band's primordial heavy metal.

songs.title: I Ride Alone
songs.note: The epic opening track of Further in Evil, which the post says would get Fenriz's blood pumping.

songs.title: Victimized
songs.note: A vamping track from Further in Evil that the post says would also appeal to Fenriz of Darkthrone.

songs.title: A Thick Event
songs.note: Opener on Pitch Dark and Trembling; heavy sonic undertow on tromba marina with effects pedals, pulling and spitting the listener.

songs.title: Trembling
songs.note: Adds a metallic rhythm that evokes an encroaching army or a lumbering herd.

songs.title: París no se acaba nunca
songs.note: Opens with an underwater-sounding dance beat from Birgé's keyboard and electronics, from the improvised Titres.

songs.title: Etel
songs.note: Opener on Prayer in Dub, starting with Greg Fox's penetrating drum rolls before the guitars and bass join.

songs.title: Deborah
songs.note: Twisty guitar chaos that the post highlights from Prayer in Dub.

songs.title: Scout
songs.note: Described as having a Dirty Three-esque ascendance on Prayer in Dub.

songs.title: First Time
songs.note: A 34-minute, dense noise and drone piece the post calls the most compelling of her four releases.

songs.artist: Mackenzie Kourie, Luke Rovinsky & Caleb Duval
songs.title: Duroc
songs.note: Opener of Beautiful Pigs, launching with guttural rumbles and grinding squeaks that mimic animals.

songs.artist: Mackenzie Kourie, Luke Rovinsky & Caleb Duval
songs.title: Mangalista
songs.note: Starts with static and glitches that feel like a machine breaking down on Beautiful Pigs.

songs.title: Amathounta
songs.note: An oscillating track from Hav that hypnotizes almost instantly.

songs.title: Death in Trafo (or, The Crater)
songs.note: From Stena; its opening dissonance melts into a two-chord sway that drifts back and forth.

songs.title: Power of Solidarity
songs.note: Modular synth track named to suggest hope in dark times, with buoyant, rebellious energy.

songs.title: Confidence Comes from Taking Action
songs.note: Modular synth track whose name suggests hope in dark times; the post links it to change through eagerness rather than anger.

songs.title: Believing in Possibilities Beyond Yourself
songs.note: Modular synth track whose title suggests hope in dark times, part of an album of defiantly optimistic pieces.

songs.title: My Ideal Is Windy
songs.note: Three-track suite of glitchy cello repetitions that become hypnotic, with the music flitting like a hummingbird.

songs.title: strings one
songs.note: Side A piece that starts in near-silence before launching into whirrs, whines, and crashes, built from guitar.

songs.title: strings two
songs.note: Side B piece that is crackly and disruptive, with crunchy sounds banging around, less a meditation than a disturbance.

songs.title: Illinois
songs.note: Flute improvisation the post calls a throat-burner, with huffing, spitting, and blowing that feels relentless.

songs.title: a hummming, thrumiiiing circle spunnn / Holy Shimmer
songs.note: Twenty-minute closer that the post says sounds like a ceremonial ritual stretched to fill a day.

songs.title: Changing Landscapes (Dim)
songs.note: Ground-shaking rumble during which the air seems to disappear, according to the post.

songs.title: Temporary Structures
songs.note: Heavy bass tones that the post says evoke echoes in an abandoned industrial park.

songs.title: Fever Dream
songs.note: Cycling drones cover strings buried below, creating a dreamlike zither and cello piece.

songs.title: Train Ride Home
songs.note: Zither-centered piece that the post says glistens like a passing landscape and is among the most transfixing tracks.

songs.artist: Sarah Belle Reid and Vinny Goila
songs.title: Autumn Bog Fowl
songs.note: Improvisation that the post says sounds like distant signals of an ancient city as well as natural noises.

songs.title: Yui Horie "DEAR FUTURE (cuxrixous remix)_unfinished"
songs.note: Flips a classic anime theme into a reworking that the post says redefines "future garage" with two-step beats and shimmering synths.

songs.title: "Never" (Osunlade & Waajeed Remixes)
songs.note: Post praises Osunlade's bubble-bath-like remix and Waajeed's reworking with thumb pianos and metallic pings.

songs.artist: Karen Nyame KG with Gina Jeanz
songs.title: "Sovereign Groove"
songs.note: Post says it traces South African amapiano back to '80s Italo disco roots, linking it to Wes Lee's "Gates".

songs.title: "Manigua's Groove"
songs.note: An amapiano-derived groove the post calls cinematic, with nighttime thrills and menace.

songs.artist: Karen Nyame KG with Griffit Vigo
songs.title: "Saturn"
songs.note: Post says it adds dreamlike subtlety to gqom's spaciousness, with special clap patterns and vocal drones.

songs.title: "Hold of Me"
songs.note: The post's best pick from the collaborations, with UK singer TYSON riding levitational bass and shakers.

songs.title: "Femme Fatale"
songs.note: A narcotic chug referencing electropop, synth disco and euphoric rave, with "money… danger… sex" refrains adding sleaze.

songs.title: "Secondary Loop"
songs.note: Post says it packs familiar early '90s hardcore rave samples into a production that still sounds futuristic.

songs.title: "Good Boys Say Yes Sir"
songs.note: Ultra-queer, sleazy rap track the post calls a banger, with an instrumental that is also sweaty and sleazy.

songs.title: "Overnight Looking Down"
songs.note: An eight-and-a-half minute ambient, dreampop and shoegaze piece over a steady kick, described as heart-stoppingly beautiful.

songs.title: "Macumba"
songs.note: Post calls it an anthem in the making, with robot voices, deep funk history and half-step sections.

songs.title: "Want More?"
songs.note: Listed in the post's closing roundup of recommended tracks, with no further description given.

songs.title: Seagull Shapes
songs.note: A meditative piece the post calls excellent, with saxophonist Sami Pekkola adding shruti box, from the Finnish quartet's album.

songs.title: Shifting Sands (Mainline)
songs.note: Khadijatou Doyneh's spoken word contribution is singled out for its enchanting power, on Dawson's Afro-jazz and Brazilian-influenced album.

songs.title: Microdōt
songs.note: Named as a standout on the Romanian-born, UK-based producer's EP, described as lean, mean and hyper-speed, and superbly disturbing.

songs.title: Gyallis Spira
songs.note: A single paired with "TNTC" on the list; the post gives no further detail about the track.

songs.title: Lying to Myself
songs.note: Listed as a recommended track; the post gives no further detail about it.

songs.title: Python & Prophecy
songs.note: Named among the tracks on the EP, which moves from coldwave and EBM hints into a rhythmic mesmerism.

songs.title: A Path Appears
songs.note: Named among the tracks on the EP, which moves from coldwave and EBM hints into a rhythmic mesmerism.

songs.title: Gentle Samurai
songs.note: Farmer Dave Scher's galactic ode to friends who are now gone, cited as evidence of the band's optimism.

songs.title: Gem
songs.note: Chris Gunst's gentle song about his daughter, which includes the lyric the album's title comes from.

songs.title: Torn in Two
songs.note: A genuinely affecting ballad about broken dreams, with a lingering promise to not let the heart turn to stone.

songs.title: Everyman
songs.note: A poetic scene-setter that opens the record as dusty outlaw country before it turns experimental.

songs.title: Dream Wine
songs.note: A moody instrumental passage that stretches the record beyond the usual boundaries of genre.

songs.title: Zeibright Road
songs.note: A psych-folk exploration that the post highlights as part of the album's adventurous approach.

songs.title: Collapse (Zack)
songs.note: Featuring Kadesh Flow and Dizzy Eight, it salutes Cloud's idol Zack Fair over drill-y bass and OST string samples.

songs.title: EGO (Edging God Out)
songs.note: Featuring Quelle Chris, it frames the Cloud and Sephiroth duel as a universal us-versus-them story.

songs.title: Ciudad Ruidosa
songs.note: The title track squelches and groans, with throbbing bass broken up by ghostly, mechanized wailing.

songs.title: Sunset for Breakfast
songs.note: Opens the EP with an electronic melody line that wriggles like a stabbed worm.

songs.title: After A Shower (Itzel Remix)
songs.note: Itzel's remix strips out the melody for buzzing electronics above mechanized scrapes and shrieks.

songs.title: Manifestation Manifesto
songs.note: Shimmering 1980s synths on the otherwise eclectic STARFACE album.

songs.title: STARFACE's Descent
songs.note: Atmospheric strings that feature on the sci-fi concept album STARFACE.

songs.title: FLUORESCENT / Beyond Space
songs.note: West London rap, one of the many genres the STARFACE album moves through.

songs.title: Shell of You
songs.note: Alt-rock guitar shredding on STARFACE, a concept album about a genderfluid space alien.

songs.title: Second Hand Sadness
songs.note: Injects drum and bass into the cosmic funk of STARFACE.

songs.title: Humanity
songs.note: An achingly pretty track that grounds the album's fantastical themes in personal lyricism.

songs.title: I-90
songs.note: A Midwest emo-inflected quarter-life crisis song about being back home in Ohio.

songs.title: SHL
songs.note: A regret-filled song with soft violin and bright fingerpicking, built around a cutting lyric about being hurt.

songs.title: Nothing Nothing
songs.note: Conjures feelings of suburban malaise on the pared-back EP Dying in the Wool.

songs.title: Dying in the Wool
songs.note: The closing track builds to an emotional climax of electric guitar feedback, pounding drums, and a repeated lyric.

songs.title: Messages in Money
songs.note: Over a galumphing bassline and tense strings, it highlights the dark side of cash and its hold on the rapper.

songs.title: Monopoly
songs.note: Outlines the rapper's winding path through life, warning that there is no get-out-of-jail-free card.

songs.artist: Gull Grey Eyes x Kev Metta
songs.title: Cyyano
songs.note: A nearly 13-minute flying-dream track with subtle bass and sweeping strings, likened to a Studio Ghibli sequence. The post also mentions a 16-minute ambient mix.

songs.title: Île Flottante
songs.note: Balearic-inspired work for International Feel that blends street soul, kosmische and electropop to capture bittersweet Balearic bliss.

songs.title: Italo Disco Banger
songs.note: A surprisingly fresh follow-up to his 2016 track, more balanced, with warm interlocking melodies and riffs; the B-side "Hotline" is funkier.

songs.title: Original Vibes
songs.note: Italian producer Nicola Altieri's deep house with relentless beats and detailed hi-hats and chimes, designed for a big, crisp system.

songs.title: Axis
songs.note: Belgian minimalist drum & bass in the Doc Scott 31 Recordings style, with precise parts that orbit each other without touching.

songs.title: Restoration
songs.note: Matt Lyne's solo work of wistful, detailed miniature soundscapes built from instruments, electronics and field recordings.

songs.title: Ruthers & Jupiter
songs.note: Four tracks and a remix of psychedelic disco-rock gallops; the strings of "Andromeda" are singled out as the most spectacular.

songs.title: kontra gobbledygook
songs.note: Greek rave music with a 1992–93 energy, with Amen breaks over sped-up organ house and deep subs, using modern production.

songs.title: Remixes (Hardway Bros & Tigerbalm)
songs.note: Trippy disco and acid house remixes of "Wanna Pop With You" with dub effects, plus Tigerbalm's cover of Fox's "S-S-Single Bed."

songs.title: Just A Lil Bit Of Sweat
songs.note: Footwork-jungle hybrid on a Moveltraxx EP, praised for its saucy vocal sample and singing pitched snares.

songs.title: Closing the Loop
songs.note: Newcastle DJ's uncategorizable dance track, described as euphoric and clearly on a roll.

songs.title: Smitten
songs.note: Meditative house banger with club warmth, noted for its intensity on an album of personal expression.

songs.title: Unidentified
songs.note: Zippy track that reworks recent Black U.S. club music with raw, sophisticated textures and funk.

songs.title: Cycle
songs.note: Slower, more martial track that keeps the producer's technical complexity and funk.

songs.title: Saturn is a Supercomputer
songs.note: Sci-fi techno from the Hanover-born, Lisbon-based producer, blending ambient, electro and industrial hip-hop beats.

songs.title: High Voltage Dubs
songs.note: Dub reggae tribute built on clattering Nyabinghi-rooted percussion, exploring many tempos and textures.

songs.title: Disig
songs.note: Stumbling techno-dub track that the post likens to discovering the heartbeat of a giant creature underground.

songs.title: Marka
songs.note: Track the post compares to a fever dream of being caught in an asteroid field.

songs.title: Gunshot!
songs.note: Pure classic Northern English bassline from Huddersfield, with a live grime MC demanding a gunshot riddim.

songs.title: Jump Up (Get Beat Down)
songs.note: Distilled inner-city rave at 130 BPM with funk samples, rave stabs and immense kicks.

songs.title: Four Tusks
songs.note: Hypnotic meditation with huge synth chords and ritualistic, acoustic-sounding drums, described as very powerful.

songs.title: Elastic Band
songs.note: Bristol producer's bouncy funk-synth track with squawking, stretching lead synths; a DJ ADHD techno remix keeps its personality.

songs.title: Small Room
songs.note: Just as bouncy, with swelling emotional chords rising and falling through an odd, stop-start skipping rhythm.

songs.title: Lamp
songs.note: Four Tet-ish thumb piano trip-hop with something off-beam that feels better the more you immerse yourself.

songs.title: E-sprint
songs.note: High-speed bongo rave that seems wrong at first but grows more satisfying with repeated listening.

songs.title: Espektra 4
songs.note: Multidimensional breakcore that shifts into the next track's sci-fi theme, showing a maverick at work.

songs.title: Espektra 5
songs.note: A beautiful but slightly off-kilter sci-fi movie theme that the post calls a fantastic psychic rug-pull after Espektra 4.

songs.title: Celebrate
songs.note: A triumphant late track on Daylight, one of the final tracks the post says hit with great impact.

songs.title: The Show
songs.note: A triumphant final track on Daylight that the post says will take your breath away on a dedicated listen.

songs.title: Wetdisk
songs.note: A dose of pure Chicago acid that doesn't try anything new, and the post says it's all the better for it.

songs.title: On Edge
songs.note: Aussie punk 7-inch track with a caveman groove the reviewer compares to early Hank Wood and the Hammerheads.

songs.title: On The Loose
songs.note: Closer to classic '80s Black Flag-style punk, with a touch of psychedelic guitar edge at moments.

songs.title: Breaking Point
songs.note: Erick the Architect calls it the album's heart, saying it gives him the most emotional reaction; he has cried playing it multiple times.

songs.title: Ezekiel's Wheel
songs.note: George Clinton plays a hookah-smoking caterpillar alongside RÜDE CÅT's chorus, echoing the Biblical metaphor in the title.

songs.title: Mandevillain
songs.note: A villainous alter ego emerges as the rapper mines his personal growth after leaving NYC for Los Angeles.

songs.title: Rock 2000
songs.note: A surging track sonically indebted to the '80s, despite its Y2K-referencing title.

songs.title: Héros Nationally
songs.note: Showcases the raps alongside Afrobeat-inflected grooves, one of two prime examples of the album's hits.

songs.title: Calling You Out
songs.note: Lead single from Forever, described as having the stomp and sparkle of peak Shania Twain, with a gigantic chorus.

songs.title: Ruby
songs.note: Praised for Jay's braggadocio and JUNE!'s hushed closing bars over a ghostly soul backdrop produced by Reggie the Father.

songs.title: Mood to Make Love
songs.note: Sultry lead single from Lover, Other, built on a piano phrase and woodblock knock with a tense, restrained feel.
Big, clangy lead single that evokes the group's noisy early efforts, though the album proves more melodic.

songs.title: YZ80
songs.note: Heartbreaking song about teenage motorcycle rides with the singer's late father, paired with a lovely melody.
Backward-looking song opening with an iconic lead guitar line and the lyric about feeling most alive in 1995.

songs.title: Grief in Phantasia
songs.note: The band's longest track, starting at full strength and never letting up; the post calls it a fitting picture of dogged grief.

songs.title: Fleas
songs.note: Straightforward proto-punk with a deliciously crunchy guitar sound, described as short, sweet garage punk.

songs.title: Square
songs.note: Closing track with girl-group vocal styling; the post calls it undeniably catchy and recalls The Rondelles.

songs.title: God's Hammer
songs.note: Lo-fi title track full of hooks, with bright guitars, subdued vocals, and singer Samuelito Cruz slipping into falsetto.

songs.title: Old Heads
songs.note: A banger with a bigger sound and upbeat melody, paired with a depressed message about daily sameness.

songs.title: Let's Kill Punk
songs.note: Fast, aggressive title track about a protagonist miserable with punk and miserable without it.

songs.title: Buzzz
songs.note: Described as a lightning flash, showcasing the band's outlandish guitar noise.

songs.title: Al Otro Lado
songs.note: Title track of the latest album, with lyrics on how easy it is to screw over and obey without thinking.

songs.title: Túnel de plástico
songs.note: An urgent, poppy track about migrant workers harvesting produce in substandard conditions; called a standout.

songs.title: Working Class Drama
songs.note: Bright guitar lines give a melodic air to this emotive song from the Barcelona boot boys' Oi!-meets-post-punk sound.

songs.title: Citat Vella
songs.note: The most upbeat moment the trio gets on this record.

songs.title: Fills de La Nit
songs.note: Described as the best track here, with sharp instrumentation and an infectious beat.

songs.title: Mindful Solutionism
songs.note: Traces human misuse of new technology back to caveman days, opening a conceptual run through tainted tech.

songs.title: Infinity Fill Goose Down
songs.note: Described as an Animal Farm-esque highlight of the Integrated Tech Solutions concept journey.

songs.title: Forward Compatibility Engine
songs.note: Features Rob Sonic on a guitar-strewn, EPMD-referencing track.

songs.title: By The River
songs.note: A calming, naturalistic track suggesting nature may win out against ITS's agenda.

songs.title: AAU Tournaments
songs.note: billy woods raps over dusky flute lines and downy keys about America and spirituality.

songs.title: Pink Lemonade
songs.note: RXK Nephew passes through the honeyed production.

songs.title: Sad Vampire
songs.note: Brian Ennals searches for salvation amid a tumultuous world.

songs.title: Hater Porn
songs.note: Casual and Breezly Brewin trade taut bars over rumbling guitar.

songs.title: Now That's What I Call A Posse Cut Vol. 56
songs.note: Closing cut with Bruiser Wolf, Danny Brown, billy woods, and Despot as a posse cut.

songs.title: Ignorance Is Bliss
songs.note: Alaska explores divide-and-conquer tactics over somber piano and noir-tinged production.

songs.title: SP 12 Jump Off
songs.note: Climactic closer described as Schoolly D-level.

songs.title: Down Wit It
songs.note: Paul White brings ’80s synth sadness to the track.

songs.title: Jenn's Terrific Vacation
songs.note: Kassa Overall gives the track a jazzy gusto.

songs.title: Ain't My Concern
songs.note: Quelle Chris and Chris Keys craft a warped, spacey backdrop for Brown's self-reflection.

songs.title: Bass Jam
songs.note: Album send-off recalling songs that bring tears before the chorus.

songs.title: Small Victories
songs.note: Guest Dom Chronicles raps over cherubic keys and pitter-patter percussion.

songs.title: Spirit Of Richard Right
songs.note: Skyzoo pays tribute to author Richard Wright.

songs.title: Away
songs.note: Chester Watson delivers abstractions over levitating keys.

songs.title: Lobster Spaghetti
songs.note: Brainorchestra embraces bass-propelled deep funk.

songs.title: I Made You A Song
songs.note: Album closer with a quiet hopefulness and soothing melodic charm.

songs.title: Shadow Self
songs.note: A two-steppy track exploring self and duality with synth-centric production.

songs.title: Glass Ceiling
songs.note: Semiratruth praises self-reliance on this defiant track.

songs.title: Down Down Bb
songs.note: Quelle Chris flows over bubbling bass and metallic hi-hats on the penultimate track.

songs.title: The Garden
songs.note: Opener with spiritually inclined soul-searching over crunching kicks and a tranquil keys loop.

songs.title: Dragons
songs.note: Closing cut contemplating the meaning of victory, inspired by the manga Vagabond.

songs.title: B.Q.E
songs.note: Opening track with a static-swaddled vocal sample and two MCs moving through time.

songs.title: 3Pack
songs.note: Elric blesses the kooky boom-bap of the track.

songs.title: Sad Eyes
songs.note: DOOF closes out the weeping soul of the track.

songs.title: You Played Me
songs.note: The album's sole vocal cut with ’80s club pomp.

songs.title: Fleeting Youth (An Audible Life)
songs.note: Discards drums for delicate piano, ending with a lost radio broadcast.

songs.title: Monday's Generation
songs.note: Upbeat track with a taut drum pattern, children's playground choir voices, and KPM samples.

songs.title: Bamboo
songs.note: Built from fragments of Oswald d'Andréa's music.

songs.title: Dream Factory
songs.note: Closer that unearths the easy-listening work of Syd Dale.

songs.title: Sly
songs.note: Opening track of Flukin'; Joe-Armon Jones's keyboards add a modern cosmic jazz quality to what the post calls a dance club tune.

songs.title: Catch the Drum
songs.note: Praised for its kung-fu flutes, dry bass-and-snare crack, and Tibetan monk chant loop, which won the writer over despite initial disappointment.

songs.title: Hypocrite
songs.note: Described as a phenomenally menacing stomp draped in stomach-churning strings, showcasing the rhythm-driven backbone of The Severed Ear.

songs.title: Imagine That
songs.note: Its bright, rolling drum pattern carries a song that lyrically feels like a belated sequel to Jadakiss's "Why."

songs.title: Misery
songs.note: Highlighted for its wailing saxophone, one of several unlikely instruments Doza uses to carry the melodic hook.

songs.title: Four of Clovers
songs.note: Cited as an example of the 90s Britpop influence woven into Fool's Parade's loose, winding Paisley-style sound.

songs.title: When The Clouds Run In
songs.note: Named as a stopping point drawing on 70s piano rock within the band's extended, multilayered psychedelic album.

songs.title: Hazel Eyes
songs.note: Cited as a 60s country-tinged stopping point on Fool's Parade, adding to its multi-timeline approach.

songs.title: Virus
songs.note: Opens Unprecedented Sh!t with a jarring, distorted sound that the editor found startling and compelling.

songs.title: Unprecedented Sh!t
songs.note: The title track lurches and chomps, with weird whistling noises around clawing, distorted chords.

songs.title: Baby Roe
songs.note: A subdued, eerie track where sudden arrhythmic vocal samples throw the backdrop off balance.

songs.title: You Forgot to Speak
songs.note: A subdued moment with eerie tone and scattered arrhythmic vocal samples across the backdrop.

songs.title: All Amusement/So Close to Tears
songs.note: Incorporates digital blips and crackle, branching out from the band's earlier sound.

songs.title: Okleigh Woods/The Ghosts At Night
songs.note: Features disarmingly still ambience, showing the band's more confident and assured side.

songs.title: Prowler
songs.note: The lead single from the six-track EP, piling on wubs and focused on hooks and beats.

songs.title: Worm
songs.note: Slathers '70s motorik drums in sleazy '00s electroclash synths for a mind-blowing mix.

songs.title: Sugar Kingdom
songs.note: Contrasts crisp hand-percussion hip-hop beats with ghostly dub vocals.

songs.title: I Am a River
songs.note: A sparkling, Sundays-channeling number with chiming guitars and delicate, angelic vocals.

songs.title: Nightmare Temptation
songs.note: Wreathed in fuzz, showing the band's broadened and brighter sound on Raw Colours.

songs.title: It Must Be Burning
songs.note: Shares the spookiness of the best UK psych-folk, retaining the ghostliness of the earlier record.

songs.title: Something More
songs.note: A jangly album closer with a Southern Gothic feeling, likened to a Flannery O'Connor story.

songs.title: AmmA
songs.note: A feminist anthem with Algerian and Tunisian influences, singled out as the standout track on the album Swaken.

songs.title: Karma
songs.note: A scorching, Cream-esque track described as self-explanatory, from the album Swaken.

songs.title: Play It Cool
songs.note: Praised as one of Will Moloney's best songs, with absurdist lyrics and a mind-melting verse sequence.

songs.title: Cakewalk
songs.note: A new standalone single of spooky garage pop with layered three-part harmonies and twangy guitars.

songs.title: Coral Mimic
songs.note: A banger with distended synths, part of the waterlogged club music on Tidal Memory Exo.

songs.title: Pulse Angel
songs.note: A banger with distended synths, part of the waterlogged club music on Tidal Memory Exo.

songs.title: New Species
songs.note: Features short-circuiting samples in nasty, immersive club music from Tidal Memory Exo.

songs.title: Germ Chrism
songs.note: Features short-circuiting samples in nasty, immersive club music from Tidal Memory Exo.

songs.title: DESTEJER
songs.note: Pretty, balmy melodies from the psychedelic avant-jazz debut album MESTIZX.

songs.title: TURBULÊNCIA
songs.note: Whips up a storm of psychedelic energies on the duo's debut album MESTIZX.

songs.title: WRITING WITH KNOTS
songs.note: Emits battle cries for ecological justice on the duo's debut album MESTIZX.

songs.title: Degree Decree
songs.note: Standout track from debut album A DOG A DEER A SEAL, tackling climate change with sarcastic, funny imagery and a brutal Tesla roast.
Lead single from the 4×4 EP, praised as the uncontested champion of a dance-pop, EDM-leaning release out on NLV Records.

songs.title: Empty Bottle Boogie
songs.note: Up-tempo stoner metal with charismatic, debauched vocals; named among the tracks that leave particularly strong first impressions.

songs.title: Big Bad Bodega Cat
songs.note: Party-minded stoner metal from the band's Graveside Grin; named among the tracks that leave particularly strong first impressions.

songs.title: Spit in the Casket
songs.note: Lead single with groove, melody, and chugging riffs; named among the tracks that leave particularly strong first impressions.

songs.artist: MC Juice, All Natural, Georgia Anne Muldrow
songs.title: Run It Back
songs.note: Album high point driven by chomping electric guitar, with MCs echoing classic hip-hop cadences over new lyrics.

songs.artist: MC Juice, All Natural, Georgia Anne Muldrow
songs.title: Dreams Deferred
songs.note: Album closer with a bright, jazzy arrangement that masks lyrical darkness.

songs.artist: MC Juice, All Natural, Georgia Anne Muldrow
songs.title: Paper Thick
songs.note: Rapid-fire microphone one-upsmanship featuring guest appearances from E-40, Casual, and Del the Funky Homosapien.

songs.title: The Reflecting Pool
songs.note: Pianist Ben Smith plays patient, elegant arpeggios whose sustain is haloed by electronic accents, making the piece feel almost motionless.

songs.title: Camouflage
songs.note: Shifts endlessly in phrasing and accents while keeping the same harmonic contour, like light on a calm sea.

songs.title: Map of the World
songs.note: A string quartet that sustains a single chord for about ten minutes, with variation coming from bow pressure and speed.

songs.title: De La Salle (Violins)
songs.note: Uses a similar approach with more aggression and volume, with bows in constant motion and terse single-line variants.

songs.title: Gorges Gard
songs.note: A 48-minute piece where the ensemble shapes its form collectively in real time, shifting between sections and outlier voices.

songs.title: microchimerisms
songs.note: Played by flutist Sara Constant, a terse, texture-driven abstraction that opens the album and sets its tone.

songs.title: threads
songs.note: A bruising series of swelling gestures played by the string trio Chartreuse, with microtonal bursts and slashing noise.

songs.title: Caduceus
songs.note: Moves from down-tuned cello figures into lush upper-register gestures enhanced by sizzling electronics.

songs.title: Tsiyr
songs.note: Microtonal piano patterns give way to jittery arco lines from Quatuor Bozzini and darting flute and clarinet.

songs.title: Affine
songs.note: A constellation of staccato sounds gradually absorbed into acrid brass and reed harmonies.

songs.title: Simulacra
songs.note: Features a fierce cello solo from Jeffrey Ziegler amid swelling orchestral writing by Symphony Nova Scotia.

songs.title: Lysis
songs.note: The title piece, played by Bozzini, rises from whispery shadows to hell-bent microtonality, leaving the listener off-balance.

songs.title: Tall Grass
songs.note: Michael Gordon's piece starts in post-Glass minimalism, then breaks the ensemble into fast sections with harmonic effects that sound almost electronic.

songs.title: Antenna Studies
songs.note: Paula Matthusen's work moves toward abstraction, weaving aerated traces of radio broadcasts into meticulously placed sonic strata.

songs.title: The Broken Mirrors of Time
songs.note: A large ensemble piece by the Argento Ensemble, using spectralist harmonies to add adroit tension to memorable motifs.

songs.title: Tracing Hollow Traces
songs.note: A solo clarinet piece played by Carol McGonnell that compresses elegant form and visceral sonic effects into about four and a half minutes.

songs.title: Cantantes Metalles
songs.note: A fierce trio in which cellist Jay Campbell, Conor Hanick, and Mike Truesdell all contribute clangorous metallic percussion.

songs.title: I have loved a stream and a shadow
songs.note: A solo piano piece played by Conrad Tao, moving through glassy introspection and lurching turbulence in three parts.

songs.title: Faerie Rhythm
songs.note: Features the composer's wordless folk-like singing and whistling alongside Quatuor Bozzini, feeling deliciously alien.

songs.title: to carry dust & breaks through the body
songs.note: A trippy piece where strings slowly pitch down against a steady piano, making the keyboard seem to lose its tuning.

songs.title: Nebula
songs.note: A barrage of staccato sax notes that melts into cacophony, then shifts to high-pitched whirr.

songs.title: Air
songs.note: A minimalist abstraction that seems made only of breath.
Moves through long, sine wave-style tones to build atmosphere.

songs.title: Center
songs.note: Opens with small noises and static in patient intervals, then becomes a more continuous, unpredictable stream.

songs.title: Nanhari
songs.note: Starts as a wall of noise, then turns minimal, doling out sounds that create tension and release.

songs.title: Joy 2
songs.note: Rattling gulps that reveal more structure the deeper you listen.

songs.title: Joy 5
songs.note: A springy rhythm highlighted as one of the album's standout sketches.

songs.title: Joy 7
songs.note: Ghost tones that help make the album feel personal.

songs.title: Where Do We Go Now?
songs.note: A loop of metal chiming generates clouds of solace.

songs.title: Apricity
songs.note: Reverberant sounds approach gradually, fully decaying before the next arrives.

songs.title: One Last Look Beyond the Rift
songs.note: A dense, grinding mass that feels like staring into an abyss.

songs.title: S*fe Word
songs.note: A male and female voice discuss safe words over echoing tones, unclear whether they are serious.

songs.title: Swipe Left
songs.note: A confused voice is quickly chopped up and consumed by drilling noise.

songs.title: Pumpkin Spice
songs.note: Slow-grooving post-punk with angular instrumentation and electrifying vocals from lead Sandra Yau; teased ahead of a full-length.

songs.title: Sundae with Peanut
songs.note: Funky track with spoken word over a strong bassline and an unconventional storyline instead of verse-chorus structure.

songs.title: En La Oscuridad
songs.note: Debut LP track with bouncy drums and cutting guitar lines using a heavy, '80s phaser sound.

songs.title: Ser Una Más
songs.note: A hard standout with a dramatic guitar solo.

songs.title: Viejas Trampas
songs.note: Energetic track with captivating reverberating vocals and metallic riffs.

songs.title: Silent Morality
songs.note: Two minutes of lightning-fast hardcore with largely unintelligible yelling, distorted guitar, and a strong bassline.

songs.title: P.B.S
songs.note: Bass-led dirge with ferocious drumming and harsh howls, ending in a building swirl of distortion.

songs.title: H.U.M.A.N.I.T.Y
songs.note: Guitar-driven track with high and low riffs playing off each other, creating heady tension.

songs.title: SICK
songs.note: Fast, straightforward jam that breaks into maniacal laughter and then a feedback-filled bass breakdown.

songs.title: El camino así es.
songs.note: Demonic dual vocals dominate this track from a marginally more refined full-length.

songs.title: La noche de la bestia.
songs.note: Guitar harmonics and noise fill this track.

songs.title: Visu.
songs.note: Brief, fast and particularly brutal track.

songs.title: República Popular Democrática de Korea.
songs.note: Grunt-filled, evil-sounding track with crunchy guitar and a tight rhythm section.

songs.title: Duality
songs.note: Trippy psych-leaning post-punk with organ-like keys and '70s rock licks.

songs.title: L.O.N.E.
songs.note: Delves into country and western with twee group melodies.

songs.title: The Babble
songs.note: English folk influence on the band's melodic psych-post-punk sound.

songs.title: Placeholder
songs.note: Features nonsense Latin lyrics and a strange, unexpected charm.

songs.title: Never Met You
songs.note: Mecca Normal-esque no wave track with a simple guitar riff, layers of noise, and a spare vocal line.

songs.title: Melting Into the Sidewalk
songs.note: The quietest track, with a creeping, water-like rhythm and Beat-poetry-style lyrics.

songs.title: Contempt
songs.note: Heavy title track from the anarcho-punk quartet's fifth full-length, with lyrics urging hope and resistance.

songs.title: Arrigoni Bridge
songs.note: Late work from 2019 with its first recorded premiere, built on the design of a Portland–Middletown bridge and scored for three lap steel guitarists and acoustic

songs.title: Flips
songs.note: A 2020 late work, more stripped-down, with bowed guitars colliding with string and glockenspiel lines; also getting its recorded premiere.

songs.title: Strange Waves
songs.note: Six-movement cello work by Ed Bennett, inspired by the Irish Sea, with field recordings of the coastline beneath the slow-moving strings.

songs.title: In the Cage
songs.note: A 2022 string quartet with objects, described as wildly dynamic, shifting from extreme volume to nearly inaudible sustained vocal tones.

songs.title: Insects & Machines
songs.note: Vivian Fung's fourth quartet, which takes its sounds from insects heard in a Cambodian jungle and stretches them into urban-life noise.

songs.title: Clamor
songs.note: A string sextet work about women finding ways around obstacles, with a bassoon concerto-like middle section and movements named after Korean and feminist references.

songs.title: Threes
songs.note: A 39-minute piece built on a shimmering drone that layers, multiplies, and gradually turns into static while still rising to the surface.

songs.title: (lamentations) for éliane
songs.note: A 32-minute side-A piece for prepared euphonium, inspired by Éliane Radigue, with smooth curves and gritty inner textures.

songs.title: paper blown between the spaces in my ribs
songs.note: A 30-minute title track that builds dense tones into an evolving aural universe, described as completing a series about longing for home.

songs.title: up
songs.note: A 15-minute side-two piece of pulsing, patient guitar and drum sound that the post calls like a therapeutic massage.

songs.title: Good News Blues
songs.note: The 12-minute opener that launches the duo album with momentum the post says lasts across its 65 minutes.

songs.title: Snapping Turtle
songs.note: A groove the pair finds that the post says never snaps under the weight of their quick spurts.

songs.title: Apura II
songs.note: An all-out energy track that Evangelista deftly steers amid high-level playing by the group.

songs.title: Apura III
songs.note: A track where Evangelista precisely traces patterns, described as a high point of In the Fullness of Time.

songs.title: Until
songs.note: The 15-minute album-ending track that rises to a fever pitch and works like a hypnotic drug, per the post.

songs.title: Seven Pieces for Three Percussionists
songs.note: A shorter piece on disc one where percussion patterns overlap, evolve, and coagulate, as performed by Sarah Hennies and others.

songs.title: stamps from childhood I
songs.note: An energizing, rapid sax barrage with close-miked clicks and keys, described as approaching avant-garde dance music.

songs.title: in flux ä
songs.note: A frantic, corrosive sax track of short rapid fires that the post names as one of the album's energizing barrages.

songs.title: Profundity Unveiled
songs.note: A spacious track where oddly repetitive sounds create rhythm while whirrs and clacks feel random.

songs.title: Andersabo
songs.note: Four-movement work using a fixed half-valved position, with shifting long tones moving between full chords and staggered pitches.

songs.title: unfoldings
songs.note: Closing piece where Saviet's bowed lines float over piano drones made with e-bows, creating shifting harmonies; the writer's favorite on the album.

songs.title: Pièges de neige
songs.note: Five-movement piece by Mikel Urquiza that uses extended techniques to replicate snow, ending as if shaking off moisture.

songs.title: flowers endlessly open
songs.note: Daniela Terranova's more introspective piece, with pinpoint interplay under a sustained outer layer of sound.

songs.title: Pod vodom raskršća snova
songs.note: Milica Djordjević's work with Adámek, described by the composer as molten rock pushing up from deep within the earth.

songs.title: A Song for Two Mothers
songs.note: Latest Sonami work for her spring spyre instrument, moving through gestures and slow-motion development with squelchy, percussive patterns.

songs.title: Navazi
songs.note: Four-movement piece by Kian Ravaei inspired by the Persian kemenche, with structured improvisations on Dastgah-e Nava.

songs.title: Breathing Sunlight
songs.note: Expresses simple pleasures of time spent with others, with buoyant rhythms and meditative swells.

songs.title: Shapes in Collective Space
songs.note: Title composition that braids shifting moods, melodies, and gestures, reflecting the composer's idea of holding multiple realities at once.

songs.title: silhouette, mirror
songs.note: Closer adapted from a string orchestra piece, rippling with exquisite tension and striated textures.

songs.title: Roulette
songs.note: Opening duet for guitar and piano driven by roulette-wheel video score, mixing meditative and dystopian moods with electronic tones.

songs.title: Cloud Symmetries
songs.note: Work for four violins that moves between peaceful harmony and passages of restrained darkness; the writer's favorite piece.

songs.title: Possente Spirto
songs.note: Mellotron, synthesizer, and tape delay create an immersive drone, with trombone and viola tracing a slow harmonic progression.

songs.title: Hold On
songs.note: Joy sings the line 'the true gift of love is letting you be you' with bittersweet, palpable humanity on this track from The Making of Silk.

songs.title: Stay
songs.note: Joy says she wrote this song in one evening, part of the instinctive writing process behind The Making of Silk.

songs.title: 4EVA23
songs.note: A heartbreaking song about the death of Loe's brother, where his voice audibly cracks about a minute and a half in.

songs.title: Sinful
songs.note: A buoyant number with twinkling marimba and freewheeling, rapid-fire flow, described as a lighter song on The Ballad of Loesperado.

songs.title: BIRDMANHANDRUB
songs.note: A sex jam Loe murmurs through as if sharing a secret, on The Ballad of Loesperado.

songs.title: Nasty
songs.note: Abyssal bass grooves built for bump-and-grind, from the collaborative album Estrada.

songs.title: Rapido
songs.note: Syncopated, pornographic moans that the writer says will draw confused stares if played in public.

songs.title: Sicilia
songs.note: An icy, orchestral-infused cut that offers a more subdued, atmospheric moment on Estradas.

songs.title: Estradas
songs.note: A lush, marimba-led track that balances the record's steamier club moments.

songs.title: Strange Pains
songs.note: A scorched-earth hard rock track described as an insidiously catchy ripper from Exhaust.

songs.title: Stress Fractures
songs.note: A wry, muscular hardcore song that the writer says torches Converge's Petitioning the Empty Sky era.

songs.artist: t e l e p a t h
songs.title: あなたとの短い瞬間
songs.note: A tranquil track with a melody the writer compares to Terry Taylor's 'Capture Me', calling it an apparent unintentional resemblance.

songs.title: My Method Actor
songs.note: The titular single, with a skittering drum beat and sudden dirges of reverb-heavy guitar, using method acting as a songwriting metaphor.

songs.title: Like I Say (I Run Away)
songs.note: A song about decision paralysis in relationships, driven by knocking percussion and a fuzzed-out chorus recalling The Breeders.

songs.title: Ready for Sun (touch)
songs.note: A pretty acoustic ballad sung to her own shadow, ending in a swell of strings and guitar distortion.

songs.title: Maybelline
songs.note: A standout from Grog, described as lo-fi charm built on high-density hooks and cozy DIY arrangements.

songs.title: New Ro
songs.note: Named as a standout from Grog, delivering straightforward ear candy with a supremely cozy DIY feel.

songs.title: 2085 Blacksea
songs.note: A drumless track from Reflection whose liquid sound matches its title, creating foamlike textures.

songs.title: Round Ritmo
songs.note: A drum and bass-leaning banger on Reflection that the writer calls a high point.

songs.title: Jah True
songs.note: Despite its dub-suggesting title, it arranges sheets of synth in a prism-like formation rather than direct melodies.

songs.title: Output Reflection
songs.note: A squirmy, coldwave-leaning track that gradually opens into early trip-hop before folding back in on itself.

songs.title: The Transparency of Evil
songs.note: Opens Subalternity Interlude as a 17-minute track, distant and echoey, like a horror soundtrack slowed and faded away.

songs.title: Pataphysical Climax
songs.note: The quietest piece on the album, singled out as particularly menacing, with a sense that something will jump out but never does.

songs.title: CAT CUP
songs.note: Highlighted from LAUGHINGFISH as Nine Inch Nails-style industrial pop, one of the duo's chromed-out bubblegum tracks.

songs.title: PURE REALITY
songs.note: Named from LAUGHINGFISH as a brassy noise rock track, showing the album's range.

songs.title: GOOD THINGS HAPPEN
songs.note: Named from LAUGHINGFISH as trip-hop-tinged screamo, one of the album's varied moments.

songs.title: Mutty
songs.note: Stove God Cooks feature on Slant Face Killah, praised as a tour de force that clowns a Jay-Z line.

songs.title: Dandelions
songs.note: Album highlight from News of the Universe, praised for its striking lyric about dandelions turning into moons.

songs.title: Good Luck With Your Secret
songs.note: Haunting track from News of the Universe, cited for its purposefully cryptic lyrics.

songs.title: Fairytale Town
songs.note: Crow Country soundtrack piece praised for '90s nostalgia and unsettling, playful ambient atmosphere.

songs.title: Ocean Kingdom
songs.note: Crow Country soundtrack piece mixing vintage sound fonts with dynamic fluidity to reinforce tension.

songs.title: Pacing the Cage
songs.note: Bruce Cockburn tribute track on Imaginational Anthem vol. XIII, notable for its marimba playing.

songs.title: All the Diamonds
songs.note: Bruce Cockburn tribute cover on Imaginational Anthem vol. XIII, featuring heartbreaking pedal steel by Luke Schneider.

songs.title: Fall
songs.note: Bruce Cockburn tribute version on Imaginational Anthem vol. XIII, highlighted for Matthew Rolin's vocals.

songs.title: The Ash
songs.note: A sludgy track where Christmas seems to teeter on madness before settling into a hypnotic, repeated melody in its final minute.

songs.title: Silver Dollars
songs.note: Wordless breathwork gives way to strangled cries, then Christmas delivers some of the most technically demanding singing on the record.

songs.title: Thin Skin
songs.note: A nü-ish, straightforward song whose aggression is animated by Christmas's unexpected vocal choices.

songs.title: Blast
songs.note: A more aggressive, straightforward song made striking by Christmas's unexpected vocal approach.

songs.title: The Lighthouse
songs.note: A post-metal standout whose simple but striking refrain stands out to the reviewer.

songs.title: Oh, My Baby 666
songs.note: A Venom-inspired proto-thrash track on the final album, with a title the reviewer finds amusing as a non-Sabbat-sounding name.

songs.title: Black Metal Tornado
songs.note: A song mixing first-wave black metal influence with a NWOBHM gallop.

songs.title: Witches' Mountain
songs.note: A song mixing first-wave black metal influence with a NWOBHM gallop.

songs.title: Kanashibari the Dwelling
songs.note: A bugged-out, labyrinthine closing track that the band handles equally comfortably.

songs.title: Passionate Pretender
songs.note: A direct nod to Judas Priest's Dissident Aggressor, per the reviewer's spot-the-influence comparison.

songs.title: Scrying Orb
songs.note: A lush ballad on The Stygian Rose.

songs.title: Thunder (Perfect Mind)
songs.note: A stomping, radio-ready song on The Stygian Rose.

songs.title: The Stygian Rose
songs.note: An 11-minute snaking title track that pushes the band's doom sound past its guardrails.

songs.title: L'Envol
songs.note: An epic-feeling song on Les Chants de l'Aurore, delivered with a delicate touch.

songs.title: Améthyste
songs.note: An epic-feeling song on Les Chants de l'Aurore, delivered with a delicate touch.

songs.title: To Flow Through Ashen Hearts
songs.note: A highlight from Cutting the Throat of God that requires patient immersion to appreciate its depths.

songs.title: To See Death Just Once
songs.note: A highlight from Cutting the Throat of God that rewards close listening with dense polyrhythms and alien noise.

songs.title: First to Finish Last
