songs.note: Tucson punks CLASS return with a Total Punk Records 7-inch; the reviewer calls both songs catchy with wonky, wild '77-style riffage.

songs.title: Just A Worm
songs.note: Second song on CLASS's Total Punk Records 7-inch; the post says it is catchy and riff-driven in '77 punk style.

songs.title: the boy who drew cats
songs.note: A seat-of-the-pants cartoon soundtrack that feels both serious and surreal, the post's standout track from the live set.

songs.title: Glass Eye
songs.note: Voices cut in and out of bombastic noise and meditative echoes, described as a stunning piece from Toxic Colour.

songs.title: Limtruuna 03.02.1972
songs.note: Dead C-like guitar static that the post highlights among the ten short sonic essays on 1972.

songs.title: Sokerucar 21.09.1972
songs.note: A skipping-needle loop that the post singles out as one of the album's interesting ideas.

songs.title: Naroranssiranja 31.12.1972
songs.note: A track of growing noise that the post names as one of the highlights of 1972.

songs.title: 7 Runs (in arc mental styling)
songs.note: The opening title track, built from constant movement, with minimalist chimes and pulses mixing motion and stasis.

songs.title: Below a Layer Bend Aside
songs.note: A rising, reverent drone built from pipe organ and modular synth, which the post calls one of the most transfixing you'll hear.

songs.title: All That's Left Already Here
songs.note: A gently soaring piece that the post describes as a bookend companion to the opening epic.

songs.title: Abide in the Clear Light
songs.note: A 38-minute single-track tribute to Bob Blaize, high-toned and hymnal, that the post says plays more like a celebration.

songs.title: Get In
songs.note: Named as the single from their three-song release, described as a bright, lo-fi pop track with deep hooks, shimmering organ, and jangly guitars.

songs.title: Driving a Piece of Shit
songs.note: Cited as a song by this Minneapolis trio, described as fast, dumb-seeming but subversive raw punk from their EP.

songs.title: Morphers
songs.note: Collaborative neurostep/footwork track, the first time Flore Morfin and Kush Arora teamed up, finding a throughline between their approaches.

songs.title: Cut & Run
songs.note: A version of this Philly/Jersey club-influenced track, one of two versions the duo made.

songs.title: It's OK to Cry
songs.note: Closing track of a five-track set of mid-tempo bassline warpers; sounds kitsch at first, then turns unexpectedly tearjerking.

songs.title: Hello My Friends
songs.note: A roughly 15-minute slow house epic that the post says commands you to close your eyes and sway.

songs.title: Saigon
songs.note: An '80s Euro-flavored track of about eight minutes, described as having a certain perviness.

songs.title: Functions for Machines
songs.note: A gloopy, slow techno track of about eight minutes.
A goth-Balearic, Cocteau Twins-style cover of the Smashing Pumpkins song, under five minutes long.

songs.title: XT
songs.note: A stripped-back UK drum & bass cut with crisp linear drums, brushed cymbals, bongos and bass modulations.
A breakbeat tune hinting at the least fidgety parts of Syro-era Aphex Twin, with melancholy melodies.

songs.title: Such a Night
songs.note: A zippy, electropop-inspired track with melancholy melodies, expanding the producer's rhythmic profile.

songs.title: Feel
songs.note: Featured track recommended in the post; the post gives no further detail about it.

songs.title: Ma fin est mon commencement
songs.note: Post says Miroslav Beinhauer's solo piano version is utterly convincing, a unique work related to the earlier trio version.

songs.title: Stromsänger
songs.note: Post describes a three-section work built from tram recordings, sung tones, and voices, resulting in a trippy sonic journey.

songs.title: Colla Voce
songs.note: Post calls it an Afro-Surrealist anti-opera blending JACK Quartet, vocal improvisers, and electronics into a dazzling, razor-sharp suite.

songs.title: No More Darkness, No More Night
songs.note: Post says Clay's pedal steel and Friction Quartet writing make ambient music of unusual depth and detail.

songs.title: Intimes exubérances
songs.note: Post describes a thorny four-part piano epic that moves between hazy introspection and muscular energy, delivered by Duvall.

songs.title: Traces II
songs.note: Post says this geomungo piece, played by Shin Ji-Hee, has a recurring rhythmic passage recalling a rock groove.

songs.title: Early Riser
songs.note: Post describes this unaccompanied Sasha Elina performance as an idiosyncratic five-minute portrait of painter L.S. Lowry.

songs.title: Living in a World Where Things Are Much Too Big for Me
songs.note: Slow harp strums that flirt with New Age dreaminess while staying grounded, from the four-track long dreams of hope.

songs.title: Go Somewhere and Stay Nowhere
songs.note: Closer with trebly bells that the writer says could have turned treacly but instead feels substantial.

songs.title: I Looked in the Mirror, Again
songs.note: A busy, all-out clatter moment that the writer names as one of the trio's highlights.

songs.title: Popeye vs Bluto
songs.note: A jangly grind that the writer cites among the record's highlights when the trio crests into climaxes.

songs.title: Weaving a Blanket to Warm Your Dreams
songs.note: A rising track where frictive textures melt into waves, described as hymn-like.

songs.title: Ritual of Ruin
songs.note: A moaning piece that blends frictive textures into waves, as the writer hears drones gathering debris.

songs.title: Rebirthday
songs.note: A more abstract piece where less tangible sounds build their own harmonics.

songs.title: Spectre Halo
songs.note: A more abstract piece that relies on less tangible sounds to create its harmonics.

songs.title: The Angels in These Fields
songs.note: A three-part, 20-minute title epic that the writer says shows the many moods the artist can evoke.

songs.title: Cave 12, Geneva
songs.note: A 30-minute opening loop-based track of whirrs and blasts built from trumpet and electronics.

songs.title: Umbo, Zurich
songs.note: A 22-minute track of cutting bursts that the writer says sound like a struggling fire detector.

songs.title: Airport Fridge, Self Checkout
songs.note: Impressionistic piece with faint refrigerator hum woven with chimes, percussion, and synth patterns.

songs.title: Car Horns
songs.note: Mixes sweeping strings with Patrick Shiroishi's saxophone strains.

songs.title: Car Alarm, Turn Signal
songs.note: Makes full use of Ka Baird's flute playing.

songs.title: Cinco de 12 de Mayo v. 2
songs.note: Uses strings and metal objects to create a ghostly jazz atmosphere from sparse sounds.

songs.title: Dec 2023 Toy Turntables
songs.note: Builds atmosphere from clicks and static, as if machines have replaced humans.

songs.title: Résonance du bourgeon de ferrite
songs.note: Dark, subliminal echoes that feel like faded images projected onto a shadowy wall.

songs.title: Pétales Cuivrés
songs.note: A 17-minute cascade of wide, large metal crashes that the writer finds hard to believe was captured.

songs.title: I'm Getting Very Frustrated
songs.note: Opens with a theremin-like whine and leads into a bass-heavy mantra with dichotomous vocals.

songs.title: Circles
songs.note: Closer that moves from early video game sounds through space transmissions to static cacophony.

songs.title: Brandish the Blade
songs.note: Praised for anthemic, head-rush energy, likened to Kill-era Cannibal Corpse.

songs.title: Bounty Hunter
songs.note: Reviewer says it balances between stupid and clever, and quotes its opening lyric about holding a gun.

songs.title: More Insane
songs.note: Title track that also walks the line between stupid and clever, opening with a line about becoming more insane.

songs.title: Disattachment of a Prophylactic in the Brain
songs.note: The reviewer's favorite track, described as bizarre, borderline nonsensical, and stuck in their head often.

songs.title: Shattered and Broken at the Base of Time
songs.note: A three-part, 26-minute centerpiece showing the band's mastery of song construction and dynamics.

songs.title: Primordial Sky
songs.note: Opening 13-minute title track that moves from a sludge dirge into a burst of lead guitar two-thirds in.

songs.title: One Pitch Birds for Distortion and Mouth Synthesizers
songs.note: Named as one of the featured singers' contributions on Christopher Trapani's Noise Uprising, which reworks 1920s and early-1930s recordings.

songs.title: Déjà vu
songs.note: Opening piece of L'ombre du pont, composed in isolation during the pandemic and revisiting vintage techniques.

songs.title: Diálogo con Ana
songs.note: Direct collaboration with pianist Ana Foutel, built through back-and-forth improvisation mixing prepared piano with electronics.

songs.title: Doorways 09
songs.note: Maps a forest location's sounds into electronic gestures, with Black Page Orchestra playing from a graphic score.

songs.title: Blende 01
songs.note: Explores transformation of materials, drawing on the Daphne myth and set in another forest, with abstract churning sounds.

songs.title: natural:neutral
songs.note: Judith Berkson's piece, an elegantly lumbering work where unexpected harmonies reshape the cello, clarinet, and flute timbres.

songs.title: breath in order to be completed
songs.note: Christine Tavolacci's piece built on a Hildegard von Bingen quote, with Berkson singing the words near the end.

songs.title: 18 Flowers in a Row
songs.note: Katie Porter's graphic-score piece of notes, gestures, and flower drawings, mutable and different in every performance.

songs.title: inside seconds
songs.note: Laura Cetilia's closing piece using the minor and major second to create a tricky, frictive drone with much movement.

songs.title: Spur
songs.note: Title piece of the double CD, a quintet with pianist Claudia Chan, drawing on detective-story structures with rigorous construction.

songs.title: intorno al bianco
songs.note: Quintet for clarinet and string quartet performed with clarinetist Thorsten Johanns, included on the new Furrer release.

songs.title: Comet of End Times
songs.note: Named among the sharpest, catchiest songs Mateo Tervonen has written, on the band's melodic death-thrash album Swarming Angels & Flies.

songs.title: The Deep Ends
songs.note: Called one of the sharpest and catchiest songs on Swarming Angels & Flies, alongside "Comet of End Times."

songs.title: Where the Void Begins
songs.note: An acoustic-laced track that brings the efficiency of Swarming Angels & Flies to a grander scale.

songs.title: Inadequate
songs.note: Bassist Cole Daniels's extended bass solo becomes the song's underpinning riff, showing his role on Painted Paradise.

songs.title: The Chains of Hell
songs.note: Opens Sign of the Storm with reverb-soaked echoes, showing the band's classic Swedish heavy metal style.

songs.title: Sacrifice
songs.note: Praised for its smoldering main riffs on Sign of the Storm, which pays loving homage to classic metal.

songs.title: Necromancer
songs.note: Praised for its smoldering main riffs on Sign of the Storm, which pays loving homage to classic metal.

songs.title: Nefarious, Scorned Deities I Am Devoted To
songs.note: A two-minute ripper of Autopsy-style barfed vocals and pounding drums, with a memorable title.

songs.title: Brushed by the Storm
songs.note: A ritualistic opener of synthesizer, percussion, and voice that builds as the storm gathers on Summer Ends.

songs.title: Good Grief
songs.note: A under-two-minute track of chugging riffs, skittering drums, and electronics that captures the band's essence.

songs.title: Dissonance
songs.note: A nine-minute dirge with slow-burning dark melody and ambient elements, the band's most ambitious track so far.

songs.title: I Met Kerri Colby
songs.note: An eight-minute black metal track that mixes dissonant blitz with mangled acoustic guitar, creaking samples, and spoken word.

songs.title: Hermaphroditic Image
songs.note: A noisy synth workout that the post presents as a standout from the album's experimental black metal.

songs.title: The Lament (I Am Calling You)
songs.note: A haunting opener in which guest singer Sarah McQuillan's mournful voice leads into the death metal album.

songs.title: She Is Calling Me
songs.note: A three-part closing song where McQuillan returns, keening as the band builds to the album's end.

songs.title: Sliced in the Chamber
songs.note: Its opening riff is described as scanning as black metal at one angle and nü metal at another.

songs.title: Holy Lance
songs.note: A slow-building minimalist piece with a pulsing synth line, Felicia Chen's voice, sampled strings, and a bird call.

songs.title: Sun Destroyer
songs.note: A bleak, slow epic that the post expects will appeal to fans who missed Mouth of the Architect.

songs.title: Ladder of Self Destruction
songs.note: A bleak epic singled out as a likely draw for listeners who missed Mouth of the Architect.

songs.title: Drawing a Circle
songs.note: One of the experimental tracks the post finds as exciting as the album's heavier songs.

songs.title: Temple
songs.note: Named alongside Drawing a Circle as an experimental track the post finds every bit as exciting.

songs.title: Two Worlds
songs.note: Artful study in doppelgangery with distorted, multi-layered operatic vocals reminiscent of David Bowie's Blackstar.

songs.title: Unstoppable Voice
songs.note: Violent delirium with bleary synths, taunts of "Push Me!", and erratic, scratchy percussion.

songs.title: Danger Zone
songs.note: An album high point, opening on a Gang Starr sample and built from icy xylophones with steely bars from Nivek and Squeegie Oblong.

songs.title: Slow Burn
songs.note: Gorgeous track with a haunting soprano vocal above hard-knocking beats and Nivek's muscular flow.

songs.title: Thump
songs.note: Moody track summoning a Wu-Tang Forever outtake, turning eerie after a gurgling vocal sample enters.

songs.title: Pose
songs.note: Wild hallucinogenic house number with lightning-like synth flashes over a hissing beat.

songs.title: cp
songs.note: Steel-drum-like pads pogo between a samba-like rhythm track.

songs.title: É COMO?
songs.note: Opener whose melody sounds like a sly inversion of the synth riff from Usher's "Yeah!".

songs.title: Mindjeres
songs.note: A masterpiece with a giddy flute melody spiraling over a steady synth pattern and slipping drums.

songs.title: The Radiant Edge
songs.note: The record's longest song, nebulously hooky and submerged-sounding, and also its most memorable.

songs.title: House Music
songs.note: Marsalis sings of isolation and longing with alien-pitched vocals over acoustic guitar and piano.

songs.title: The Strange Beyond
songs.note: Haunted by violence, with industrial crackling samples and corroded mechanical clanks melting into roaring engines.

songs.title: Comparing The Properties Of Stone, Brick And Concrete
songs.note: Pierces the veil with warm, New Age-like light that is unsettling yet serene.

songs.title: Rotundity
songs.note: A rumbling, subterranean piece where Bertel's trombone sounds like it is drilling into the earth.

songs.title: Intangible
songs.note: Part of a fiery, dissonant run of trombone attacks, paired with the next track, "Nettle Sting."

songs.title: Nettle Sting
songs.note: Follows "Intangible" and tears at the sound spectrum with distorted trombone, compared to guitar detonations by Hendrix and Haino.

songs.title: JJ's Blues
songs.note: A jazz/metal improvisation the writer calls a nuclear-waste-like blast, linking many extreme styles into a messy whole.

songs.title: Or Something That Hasn't Happened Yet
songs.note: A nearly-choral track with echoes of Daphne X's voice, sitting within her wash-and-wave textures.

songs.title: For Marian Zazeela
songs.note: A 40-minute single-track tribute looping held saxophone tones into an endless hum, tribute to the late multimedia artist.

songs.title: Intermission
songs.note: A textural drone built from simple repeating sounds that develop and evolve without melodic arcs.

songs.title: Counting Clockwise
songs.note: An industrial-style stomp made from basic, repeated sounds, showing complexity through simple process.

songs.title: Broken Piano Folded For Eardrummatic Effect (Parts 1-4)
songs.note: Feels dramatic when taken seriously and hilarious when heard on a sunny day, per the writer.

songs.artist: Manja Ristić, Joana Guerra, & Verónica Cerrotta
songs.title: O vento retoma o seu lugar inicial
songs.note: Shifting motion and texture across the trio's sounds; the title means "The wind returns to its original place."

songs.title: Authority Control
songs.note: Album opener with simple structure and repetitive lyrics; called the album's most gripping track, with a sharp take on the legal assault on reproductive freedom.

songs.title: Potential Automation
songs.note: Noisy, Huggy Bear-esque track that veers into brash, straightforward punk.

songs.title: Obliterated by Flowers
songs.note: Loud, high-tension track that moves toward more straightforward punk.

songs.title: Burning Cash
songs.note: Harder-edged song where the band members trade vocal duties.

songs.title: Just Another Number
songs.note: Harder-edged song where the band members trade vocal duties.

songs.title: Grid Stress
songs.note: Rollicking, laid-back jam with undeniably catchy riffs.

songs.title: Fast Fashion Activism
songs.note: Urgent track named as one of the album's strongest cuts.

songs.title: The Joke
songs.note: Named as one of the strongest cuts, featuring a sick breakdown.

songs.title: Wine Moms
songs.note: Brutal takedown of liberals who think beating Republicans will fix America's democracy crisis; the writer loves it.

songs.title: Hairless
songs.note: Opening track where the vocalists trade lines in a way recalling Sleater-Kinney.

songs.title: Weather, I Surrender
songs.note: Urgent track with noodly guitar lines that echo Sleater-Kinney.

songs.title: Later
songs.note: Swirling, dark standout with echoey, Siouxsie-style vocals over dirgey guitar.

songs.title: Una Guerra in TV
songs.note: Prescient opening track on the experience of watching far-away wars on television, with a howled critique of human stupidity.

songs.title: Ogni Giorno Malattia
songs.note: Hardest offering, building from feedback and a pick slide into a heavy breakdown with pummeling drums.

songs.title: Bamako
songs.note: The post highlights Connelly's debut recording, which includes a rendition of Roswell Rudd's "Bamako", and says such renditions should be more frequent.

songs.title: To Bem Loko
songs.note: A skeletal accordion line wheezes down the octave a half-step at a time while the drums are repeatedly pulled away.

songs.title: Mortal Kombat
songs.note: A head-spinning deconstructed electronic track with a spectral flute melody and bass, piano, and drums appearing and disappearing at random.

songs.title: Staring At the Moon
songs.note: The closest thing on Guetto Star to a straight-ahead dance track, with a mournful take on Mexican corrido.

songs.title: Zombilly Rave (till someone call police!)
songs.note: A punky guitar pop track with a spooky title that evokes B-movie tropes but is wholesome rather than scary.

songs.title: The Dracula Bop
songs.note: A track from Hazy Horror Party with a spooky-kooky title, delivered as friendly, chiming indie pop.

songs.title: Billy's Dream
songs.note: The editors' pick from Mother Engine, a lurid, skulking nightprowler that blends industrial breakbeats, gothic romanticism, and buzzsaw blues guitar.

songs.title: The Husk
songs.note: From Chimera, a track whose dynamic, rhythmic fluidity makes its ’60s and ’70s-inspired sound feel both nostalgic and fresh.

songs.title: Lies and Games
songs.note: From Chimera, featuring guest Terin Ector, whose smoky tenor guides the song.

songs.title: Running Low
songs.note: From Chimera, with a guest vocal from Jamie Allensworth that the post singles out for praise.

songs.title: Zum Zum
songs.note: From Chimera, one of two Mermans Masengo tracks the post calls particularly excellent, threading Afrobeat, soul, and disco.

songs.title: Tula Muisi (Dance Like Them)
songs.note: From Chimera, a Masengo track with spirited, tremolo-heavy vocals that adds hard rock to its Afrobeat, soul, and disco mix.

songs.title: Ciao Bella
songs.note: From Remy's Revenge, where The Mellos back Datkidbravo's delivery with a tense, shivering-violin backdrop.

songs.title: Chrome
songs.note: From Remy's Revenge, with Korza's oozing, hallucinogenic production and an appearance by al.divino.

songs.title: Peaches & Herb
songs.note: Opener on The Color Chocolate Vol. 1, with street-savvy, spiritual lines over a bittersweet soul backdrop; Ransom guests.

songs.title: Greek Scholar
songs.note: Features ICECOLDBISHOP, who brings an agitated presence to its '80s synth attack.

songs.title: Junior High
songs.note: Evidence and Your Old Droog get nostalgic about school days on this standout.

songs.title: TRAUMA BONDS
songs.note: Explores resentment and distrust that low self-esteem brings to a relationship, over clipped snares and piano.

songs.title: I NEED YOU HERE NOW
songs.note: A motivational track on the album, per the post.

songs.title: 50 CENT VS JARULE (RAP BEEF)
songs.note: Wistful track with wordplay inspired by revisiting a classic early-'00s hip-hop beef.

songs.title: El León
songs.note: Title track with a bluesy piano loop recalling Kool G Rap's "Ill Street Blues".

songs.title: Camino Solitario
songs.note: The MC peers into the mirror to make sense of the demons that have consumed him.

songs.title: Bulevar
songs.note: Plaintive guitar carries the MC back to his hardscrabble days growing up in squalor.

songs.title: Don't Mention It
songs.note: Rousing, brass-heavy track with Sadat X bringing gravitas as a guest.

songs.title: Thanksgiving
songs.note: Introspective, humorous take on New York dating apps and doom-scrolling over woozy synths.

songs.title: Am I Cool Yet?
songs.note: Hangover-tinged track with charmingly scattershot quick-fire couplets.

songs.title: Ambitious
songs.note: Murmuring digi-funk track from the duo of Curly Castro and PremRock (aka ShrapKnel).

songs.title: Boundaries
songs.note: Album closer set over a mélange of kooky cartoon loops.

songs.title: Bloodstained Suede II
songs.note: Title track opening the sequel, with wailing electric guitar and brawny, charged-up flow.

songs.title: Must Go On
songs.note: Cautionary narrative built on a heart-rending '70s soul sample.

songs.title: Mind Control
songs.note: Brooding opener with drums, smoggy keys, and sampled vocals sketching a shadowy agenda.

songs.title: Delusional
songs.note: Kemastry sets out to storm Scotland Yard while dodging forked-tongued characters.

songs.title: Apocalyptic Flows
songs.note: Kemastry revels in shouting over ambient music while the world ends, over slow piano.

songs.title: Stay Grounded
songs.note: Mellow closer, included as an instrumental take as well, per the post.

songs.title: Snake Charmer
songs.note: Gentle pitter-patter of percussion with soothing effect.

songs.title: Spin And Step
songs.note: Zesty '80s R&B synth work.

songs.title: Made
songs.note: Airy future-soul dose underscored by purring bass.

songs.title: Miracle Maker
songs.note: Organic drum & bass rhythms mingle with strings, recalling 4hero's late-'90s work.

songs.title: Synergistic
songs.note: Final cut blending mellow Tropicália guitar and broken-beat percussion.

songs.title: Running
songs.note: Pink Siifu lights up this early track over staticky loops.

songs.title: The Last Of Us
songs.note: Quelle Chris slinks through the dusky atmosphere of this track.

songs.title: Peace
songs.note: YUNGMORPHEUS offers ruminations on how fate can impact a life.

songs.title: Eulogy
songs.note: Album opener over hushed organ and bluesy guitar about veering from a dream.

songs.title: Fences
songs.note: Raw, harrowing commentary on growing up with a physically abusive parent.

songs.title: In Dreams
songs.note: Explores religion, superstition and self-motivation.

songs.title: Tangerine
songs.note: Fuses metaphysics with MC braggadocio.

songs.title: All Be Over
songs.note: Late-album cut on the tension between an artist's ego and dwindling inspiration.

songs.title: (r)evolution
songs.note: Morikawa takes shots at corporate globalization and monarchies, signing off with steely determination.

songs.title: The Forest Church
songs.note: Opens a one-two punch with "Mountain Throne" that shows the band's much stronger songwriting and vocalist Tom Templar's hooks.

songs.title: Mountain Throne
songs.note: Paired with "The Forest Church" as the album's opening punch, showing a band that has leveled up its songwriting.

songs.title: One for Sorrow
songs.note: Named as a crushingly heavy moment where guitarist and organist interplay stands out.

songs.title: Song of the Stones
songs.note: Cited as one of the mellower moments on the album, contrasting with the heavier tracks.

songs.title: Descendants
songs.note: A hellish track where founding guitarist Terrance Hobbs sounds reinvigorated alongside new vocalist Ricky Myers.

songs.title: Embrace the Suffering
songs.note: Another hellish track where Hobbs sounds reinvigorated, with Myers handling the brutal vocals.

songs.title: Overtures of Uprising
songs.note: The title track is stretched to epic length, showing the band's doom-encrusted black metal at its most expansive.

songs.title: Dawning
songs.note: Stretched to epic length, with Andrea Morgan's violin leading amid the roar of guitars and drums.

songs.title: Of Nature & Hatred
songs.note: Whittled down into a more surgical, compact form of the band's doom-encrusted black metal.

songs.title: A Movement in Silence
songs.note: A more surgical, compact track that shows the band's shorter side on the album.

songs.title: Garden of Fire
songs.note: One of three concise, three-minute jackhammering tracks the writer names as likely playlist keepers.

songs.title: Afterglow
songs.note: Named among the three-minute tracks the writer expects to be long-term playlist keepers.

songs.title: Kill the Machine
songs.note: Named among the concise three-minute tracks the writer expects to be long-term playlist keepers.

songs.title: THE WORLD IS DOG
songs.note: Opening track of REVELATOR, with drum & bass-influenced production and a fierce, intense delivery.

songs.title: INSTANT TRANSFER
songs.note: Wavering synths give it a sci-fi paranoia feel, peaking the project's industrial sheen.

songs.title: ZIGZAGZIG
songs.note: Pounding closer that confronts the bloodshed in Palestine, ending on lines about living to tell the story.

songs.artist: Fat Tony & Fatboi Sharif & steel tipped dove
songs.title: Sweet Song of Sade
songs.note: Opens with Sharif's ghostly, psychological imagery before Tony rides dungeon funk production about a warehouse party.

songs.title: No Love
songs.note: Soothing strings back Jabee's call for honesty in rap and his critique of rappers who invent lifestyles.

songs.title: Sacrificial Lamb
songs.note: Woozy track with the release's only guest verse, from Quelle Chris.

songs.title: Overthehill
songs.note: Lays down a template of skewed loops and keys paired with soft, textured drums.

songs.title: suggamamma
songs.note: A shifting slurry of sludge funk that the post names as a peak of the release.

songs.title: look around
songs.note: Dub-style low-end attack highlighted as a standout on Portrait Of Beyond.

songs.title: Cranston
songs.note: Brings nostalgic visions to the listener.

songs.title: Cculprits
songs.note: Throwback '80s street soul with a globe-trotting story involving an airport mix-up with a G-Unit rapper.

songs.title: Push Pressure Points
songs.note: A funk-forward flip built around a scuzzy riff, with NAHreally boasting about his record-pressing history.

songs.title: Sports
songs.note: NAHreally examines modern spectator sports fandom and his loyalty to his home team.

songs.title: Livet bie så riktig
songs.note: Beat that sounds sculpted from a cover of Carole King's It's Too Late, drawn from 1950s Norwegian label samples.

songs.title: Regnet på ruta
songs.note: Closer pairing a lonesome piano refrain with muted brass that slides in and out of the mix.

songs.title: Imposter Syndrome
songs.note: Opener confronting escapism, in a bluesy late-fall mood.

songs.title: New & Unused
songs.note: Gently pulsing track where spot processing gives PremRock's voice an otherworldly aura.

songs.title: Call Abandonment Rate
songs.note: Creeping, goth-tinged track with Curly Castro and Defcee on missed connections caused by technology.

songs.title: Pink Cloud
songs.note: Closer with a question that the post suggests could summarize the record.

songs.title: The Return Of IP
songs.note: Opener over a classic-breakbeat backdrop, with Ipcus rapping about still having the itch after a quarter century.

songs.title: Mic Check
songs.note: Late album cut with Superbad Solace joining a bragging session over slinky piano production.

songs.title: The Look Of Love
songs.note: Marc Mac reinterprets the Slum Village/J-88 song with added strings and a relaxed jazz-soul feel.

songs.title: GENESIS!
songs.note: Energized, conversational delivery over crusty kicks and an elegiac fanfare, touching on betrayal and religion.

songs.title: Silicon Witch
songs.note: A dancefloor-ready, eyeliner-clad goth anthem that opens new avenues for the band's sound.

songs.title: s.p.i.d.e.r.g.o.d.
songs.note: Described as a fanatical hymn of black 'n' roll devotion.

songs.title: The Killing Room
songs.note: A 10-and-a-half-minute title track, a lush epic with haunted synths and melodic riffs that may be the band's finest song.

songs.title: Cold Hard Rain
songs.note: The album's darkest moment, yet still full of animating fire.

songs.title: Long Road
songs.note: The album's most reflective moment, still full of animating fire.

songs.title: Master Tongue
songs.note: A tightly wound ripper showcasing the interplay between Agnete's voice and B.P.'s snaking riffs.

songs.title: Coming from the Dark
songs.note: A tightly wound ripper showcasing the interplay between Agnete's voice and B.P.'s twitchy riffs.

songs.title: Fortune and Glory
songs.note: A supercharged anthem about Indiana Jones himself, with frequent name-checks, that opens the album Showdown.

songs.title: Dancing on the Cross
songs.note: Includes a cheeky Judas Priest riff-check within the band's crushing metallic hardcore.

songs.title: Candela
songs.note: The nearly 12-minute closing title track, described as the best song the band has released so far.

songs.title: Meat Magnet
songs.note: Features Napalm Death's Barney Greenway, and the vocalist holds her own alongside him.

songs.title: Within Reason
songs.note: Opener on Permanent, with rattling percussion that the post likens to Deee-Lite's "Groove is in the Heart."

songs.title: Sweat
songs.note: A manic, almost hyperpop track with constantly beeping keys, described as spectacularly weird.

songs.title: Substance Sustenance
songs.note: A grooving, industrial track that expands the band's jerky, Devo-style sound.

songs.title: Condition Report
songs.note: A throbbing, synth-soaked instrumental mentioned as part of the band's expanded sound.

songs.title: Mind Lapse
songs.note: The longest track, described as masterful dark punk with New Wave catchiness and a coherent composition.

songs.title: Politics
songs.note: Matter-of-fact post-punk with simple verses and clever lyrics.

songs.title: Je Te Crache Dessus
songs.note: A catchy, urgent track whose French title means "I spit on you."

songs.title: Midnight Cowboy
songs.note: A sweet-natured departure with simple distorted guitar.

songs.title: Disco Party
songs.note: A rangy, exasperated track that veers between fast and slow.

songs.title: Guitar
songs.note: A painfully funny track whose yells at the end recall Bikini Kill's Tobi Vail.

songs.title: Bulldozer
songs.note: Aggressive shouts that devolve into rapid-fire bursts of preverbal nonsense at the end.

songs.title: Traumatizer
songs.note: Builds slowly with blasting synths over an ominous low tone until a wall of instrumentation hits.

songs.title: Eyeballer
songs.note: The title track has an urgent, eerie organ giving it an almost horror punk vibe.

songs.title: Counterstrike
songs.note: A short, fast track with a powerful guitar solo.

songs.title: False Societal Order
songs.note: Features machine-like claps from Matthew J.X. Doyle's layered percussion.

songs.title: Abstract General Entity
songs.note: Features clanging electronic maracas sounds in the percussion layers.

songs.title: Cleansed
songs.note: Features snappy drums among the EP's layered percussion.

songs.title: Sovereign Without a Throne
songs.note: A dirgey track featuring Alexandria Sloate's moody alto saxophone.

songs.title: Locked Out Of Life
songs.note: A brief, heavy track with the only spoken-word vocals on the EP.

songs.title: Extract Wealth and Die
songs.note: Named among the album's tracks, with breathlessly shouted anti-state-violence vocals.

songs.title: Apathy is Violence
songs.note: Named among the album's tracks, urging listeners to fight internal apathy.

songs.title: This is the Future
songs.note: Particularly strong, with a dirty bassline and thrashy anarcho-punk rhythm.

songs.title: Spiritual Debts
songs.note: A melodic track with a rousing drum intro and pained howls.

songs.title: Devastacion
songs.note: Phaser-heavy guitar gives a metallic echoing effect, with sharp riffs slicing through the song.

songs.title: Presidio
songs.note: Especially sick, with a heavy intro that gives way to an onslaught of reverberating sound.

songs.title: the Section sign §
songs.note: Closing track of their debut collaboration, with kinetic guitar and bass interplay that peaks and hints at even more to come.

songs.title: Saravah Soul
songs.note: A dizzying two-minute burst of fuzzed-out, fast digital noise that the writer compares to printers escaping a fire.

songs.title: Over
songs.note: A simple, thick, fiery loop pounded out in stereo, described as hard to resist and hypnotic.

songs.title: The Wise Man
songs.note: A sparkling minimalist electronic track that nods to early Space Age work like Raymond Scott's.

songs.title: IRL
songs.note: The album's longest track, blending ambience, noise, and industrial rhythms into a vast, seemingly endless space.

songs.title: Geometry Problems
songs.note: Part of a Canadian anthology; a mechanistic beat that feels like abstract dance music.

songs.title: Time to Go Outside
songs.note: Part of a Canadian anthology; ripples like an unidentified outer space transmission.

songs.title: An Ending Given Human Form
songs.note: Part of a Canadian anthology; evokes the distant sounds of an ancient ritual.

songs.title: Before I Die
songs.note: Lead single from MG Ultra, described as cyberpunk thrills.

songs.title: Cicadas
songs.note: Gabber-infused bubblegum track from MG Ultra, named among the album's standouts.

songs.title: Psychic Attack
songs.note: Mutant drum and bass track from MG Ultra, named among the album's highlights.

songs.title: Hours
songs.note: Heartrending, self-referential track from Grammarye that the post highlights.

songs.title: Eylvue
songs.note: Hard-driving techno track from Grammarye that the post highlights.

songs.title: Dawn
songs.note: Trance balladry track from Grammarye that the post highlights.

songs.title: Bombastic Girl
songs.note: Queasy, churning track with a groaning bassline and icepick-like synth lead; called an album peak.

songs.title: Meditative Milkshake
songs.note: Shadowy track with a wiry guitar line over a throbbing bass and De Groot's calm vocal.

songs.title: Dopamine Dreams
songs.note: Closing title track, elegiac and mournful, with a quavering De Groot vocal.

songs.title: Ode To Jimbo
songs.note: A ripper inspired by a Bushwick dive bar, on the band's fourth album recorded with Ben Greenberg.

songs.title: Bullion Cube
songs.note: Estee Nack's track, where Royale enters at the one-minute mark with breathless, dazzling interlocking rhyme patterns.

songs.title: Szechuan
songs.note: Mika Dough's production is a foreign spy movie backdrop that could stand as a track on its own.

songs.title: Remains Remain Nameless
songs.note: Che Noir sketches her life in sharp strokes over Ronesh's production, rapping about survival and what remains.

songs.title: Psychological Warfare
songs.note: Decay the Llama sounds a wise, hard-won note here, pledging allegiance to the streets that raised him.

songs.title: La Mamá
songs.note: Addresses neo-colonialism through spiritual tourists, wrapped in the album's sunny, political Latin indie pop.

songs.title: Mestizaje
songs.note: Addresses colorism in Latin America within the album's warm, soothing Latin indie pop.

songs.title: Cartagena
songs.note: Sunny grooves and sparkling melodies make this track, from the debut LP Malegría, absolutely infectious.

songs.title: Conocerla
songs.note: Sunny grooves and sparkling melodies make this track, from the debut LP Malegría, absolutely infectious.

songs.title: Ultramarine
songs.note: An original video game track on the GIANTS compilation, a dreamy collaboration between Takashi Tateishi, Harumi Fujita, and Tee Lopes.

songs.title: Octavia
songs.note: A 21-minute piece recorded at GRM, built on piano and electronics with cello and guitar. Austere and baroque-leaning, loosely inspired by Italo Calvino's Invisible Cities.

songs.title: You Are My Universe
songs.note: Named as a standout on Infinite Connections, a piece built around traditional Korean rhythms, with Ambrose Akinmusire featured on a couple of tracks.

songs.title: A Colossus, an Elephant, a Winged Horse; the Dragon Rendezvous
songs.note: Nearly 12-minute centerpiece where Mellotron and sax feel more natural than the chugging riffs and howled vocals.

songs.title: But Fear Not
songs.note: Features the tsampouna, a Greek bagpipe, prominently among the album's experiments.

songs.title: Our Father Rode Again His Ride
songs.note: Also prominently features the tsampouna, a Greek bagpipe, as an experimental touch.

songs.title: The Fog
songs.note: Part of the album's closing diptych, stretching past seven minutes with apocalyptic atmosphere.

songs.title: The Plague
songs.note: Closes the album as the second half of a diptych, past seven minutes with apocalyptic atmosphere.

songs.title: The Pounding of Hooves
songs.note: Features a guitar solo from King Diamond guitarist Andy LaRocque, treated as more than a guest spot.

songs.title: Turibulum
songs.note: Features another guitar solo from Andy LaRocque, described as a co-sign rather than a hired gun.

songs.title: Victim
songs.note: Singled out as a highlight of the album's unapologetically cheesy symphonic power metal.

songs.title: Dawnbreaker
songs.note: Singled out with "Victim" as a highlight of the album's over-the-top symphonic power metal.

songs.title: Jürg Frey: String Quartet No 4
songs.note: A five-movement, hushed and intimate quartet that refines Frey's earlier sound, with a sudden burst of intensity in the third movement.

songs.title: Feedback Studies for Percussion
songs.note: A slow-moving work where crawling piano arpeggios and ringing tuned percussion intensify and drift beneath a hammering din.

songs.title: Acoustic Sourings
songs.note: Battery-driven speaker devices produce sudden bursts of static-laden noise, damped by objects and interrupted by piano-string vibrations.

songs.title: Ocean Into Wire
songs.note: A dance between tinkling and bowed percussion, electronic tones, white noise, and resonant piano chords.

songs.title: An Cúigiú Cúige
songs.note: A stark, poetic work on the idea of a central heart, blending three singers, accordion, field recordings, and abstract electronics.

songs.title: Without Persistent Environments
songs.note: Trombonist Riley Leitch plays long tones layered over recordings of Chicago locales, including a cathedral and Lake Michigan shoreline.

songs.title: Rotations Placement Providence Everywhere
songs.note: A 57-minute piece using live looping of just-intonation long tones, with thick overtone clouds that dissolve any sense of time.

songs.title: Mind Like Water
songs.note: The title work, performed by the Lydian String Quartet, embraces frenetic uncertainty and brief crystallizations while remaining structured and gripping.

songs.title: In Thin Air
songs.note: A three-movement piece for piano, violin, and percussion that moves from hyper-kinetic scampering to slower, keening textures.

songs.title: Germinate
songs.note: Performed by the Composers Conference Ensemble, a terse gestural exchange that gradually stretches into extended themes.

songs.title: 1C+1D+1E
songs.note: Blow Up Percussion section with tender tintinnabulation that feeds into ominous electronic scapes resembling a suspense film.

songs.title: Semi-Occluded Vocal Tract (SOVT)
songs.note: Prepared-piano work from 2017, performed by Richard Valitutto; the post describes it as built on stubborn minimalism and awkward rhythms.

songs.title: When the Night
songs.note: Wiancko's multipartite countermelody piece, inspired by the Ben E. King hit "Stand By Me".

songs.title: Ricercar
songs.note: Adaptation of a piece originally by the folk duo Trollstilt, with a uncanny simulation of Hardanger fiddle overtones.

songs.title: Dans le silence
songs.note: Opening work built from overlapping long tones that shift into a striated mass, per the post.

songs.title: Sucker
songs.note: Slithering PJ Harvey-esque art-song from the Gashlycrumb-based 26 Little Deaths, which the post highlights.

songs.title: Pica
songs.note: Stuttering percussive suspense piece the post singles out from 26 Little Deaths.

songs.title: Material
songs.note: Companion piece to "The Sea", built on multi-layering with Mundy's overdubbed voices.

songs.title: Listening Time
songs.note: A 43-minute just-intonation work co-credited to the ensemble, unfolding through thick, churning harmonies.

songs.title: Sapporo
songs.note: Performance of Toshi Ichiyanagi's 1963 work of glissandi and long rests, which the post calls overlooked.

songs.title: sur Incises
songs.note: Piece for three pianists, three harpists and three percussionists, described as dense with rhythm and glittering harmony.

songs.title: Christmas Alley
songs.note: The 15-minute track chops static into pieces that linger in pauses and gaps, and is singled out as a favorite.

songs.title: She Knows How To Reach Us
songs.note: A 19-minute noise-opera piece that opens with a bomb, then keeps expanding and contracting.

songs.title: TNT Chorus
songs.note: Described as landing between horror movie soundtrack and ominous dance-floor banger, with a clear beat.

songs.title: Bird Beat
songs.note: Also highlighted for its prominent beat, sitting somewhere between horror soundtrack and dance-floor bangers.

songs.title: Point
songs.note: A lively piece of aural calisthenics where each player darts around like a baton-passing sprinter.

songs.title: Nest
songs.note: Feels like a conventional but fascinating solo piano exploration, following the woozy track Crimson.

songs.title: Crimson
songs.note: A woozy, weird track whose random rattles and warped tones create a cloudy dreamlike feel.

songs.title: Sighs from Heaven
songs.note: Bernardot's first posthumous release, a 21-minute piece inspired by someone on Earth seeking heavenly bliss, described as a bittersweet capstone.

songs.artist: New Jazz Underground ft. Axel Tosca & Gina D'Soto
songs.title: Fulani in Love
songs.note: Opening track of the New Jazz Underground album; the post likens it to a window thrown open in mid-winter.

songs.title: Sam From Brooklyn
songs.note: Track from Reggie Quinerly's album where the quartet settles into a melody, with rhythmic dialogue still resonant at a lighter touch.

songs.title: Nocturnal Fire
songs.note: A dazzling guitar solo from M. of Lamp of Murmuur, described as his finest since Submission and Slavery.

songs.title: Ereptor Verae Fidei
songs.note: Vocalist Arnhwald Rattenfänger delivers an entire verse in a stately death growl over church organ and Gregorian choir.

songs.title: If She Floats
songs.note: A stunning track that pushes the speed nearly into power metal territory.

songs.title: The Serpent's Here
songs.note: Title track where stomping riff-rock gives way to a wild jazz breakdown in place of a guitar solo.

songs.title: He Just Disappeared
songs.note: Built around woozy free improvisation and spoken word.

songs.title: Waves of Deafening Soliloquy
songs.note: A highlight track featuring a guest spot from Drugoth, showing the album's diversity in texture.

songs.title: Scarlet Moon Enchantment I & II
songs.note: A highlight track featuring a killer guest spot from Zofie Siege.

songs.title: Rave Angels
songs.note: Named among the latest Longform Editions uploads, a lengthy composition from Jules Reidy featured in the label's new batch.

songs.title: Garrawang Biderap (Black Field Cricket Mating Song)
songs.note: Included in the new Longform Editions batch; the post lists it as worth a spin without much further detail.

songs.title: Clean Floor
songs.note: The writer's favorite from the Longform batch: trebly acoustic strums under murmuring effects, with Gunn's folk tendencies stretching out over 20 minutes.

songs.title: Bundanon
songs.note: A collaboration featured in Longform Editions' latest uploads, listed among the label's new lengthy compositions.

songs.title: Night Terror
songs.note: Picks up where Black Clouds & Silver Linings left off, with muscular riffing and pummeling, hyper-technical rhythms from Portnoy's return.

songs.title: Midnight Messiah
songs.note: Continues the thrilling, controlled-chaos sound of the band's comeback, though frontman LaBrie's self-referential name-dropping is cringe-prone.

songs.title: Bend the Clock
songs.note: A classic Dream Theater semi-ballad in the mold of 'Surrounded' and 'The Spirit Carries On.'

songs.title: The Shadow Man Incident
songs.note: A nearly 20-minute epic described as a natural companion to the band's goofy yet epic 'The Count of Tuscany.'

songs.title: Alone
songs.note: Praised for Tung Barrysmith's career-best vocal performance, especially the climactic coda where she sings the title repeatedly.

songs.title: A Forsaken Lover's Plea
songs.note: Title track of the album, which compares a failed romance with an artist's relationship to hip-hop.

songs.title: Polish Jazz
songs.note: Sultry, psych-y track featuring Joey Bada$$ on guest verse.

songs.title: Flatbush N*****
songs.note: Piano-draped track where Erick The Architect revives the Beast Coast mentality.

songs.title: The Most Deliciousest
songs.note: Combines thumping boom-bap drums with faint melodic infusions.

songs.title: Toiler On The Creek
songs.note: Ventures into electronic film soundtrack territory with synth blips and burps.

songs.title: Bug Copped Village Gini
songs.note: Explores negative production space, inspired by a search for monastery-stored Armenian wine.

songs.title: Dark Alley AzzWhippinz
