songs.note: Droney, abrasive psychedelia that the review highlights as a sharp turn within Variable Happiness.

songs.title: Her Wind Horse
songs.note: Described as a liltingly eerie folk piece that moves the album into a new mood.

songs.title: Singular Grace
songs.note: Elegant, confident majesty that closes out the stretch of tracks the review describes.

songs.title: Castle of Doubt
songs.note: Hypnotic clatter and grating metallic synth that the review imagines coming from a haunted factory.

songs.title: TPOTT
songs.note: The closest the Opinions EP gets to a dancefloor, breaking into ominous whispering mid-track.

songs.title: Carved In Stone
songs.note: Leaden, chugging rhythms and blackened thrash solos show the band's sludgy power on Seeing Through Fire.

songs.title: No Solace, No Quarter, No Mercy
songs.note: Praised as a track proving the band still delivers infernal, sludgy heaviness with real consistency.

songs.title: Unavoidable Truth
songs.note: A standout showcasing vocalist James Bulloch's animated, demonic growls.

songs.title: Oversized Sweater
songs.note: Opens Homo Anxietatem with warm, comfortable late-90s and early-2000s pop, touching on endings and transitions.

songs.title: Our Song
songs.note: Tackles lingering heartbreak on the album Homo Anxietatem.

songs.title: Without You
songs.note: Addresses climate anxiety on the album Homo Anxietatem.

songs.title: Crime
songs.note: One of the writer's favorites, detailing life with depression on Homo Anxietatem.

songs.title: A Day in Zanzibar
songs.note: Opener on Ali's latest album, described as a jazzy, lush musical journey.

songs.title: Please Keep Me Near, Forever
songs.note: A smooth track featuring Ali on trumpet, following the opener.

songs.title: Rise Up
songs.note: Named as an upbeat favorite from the album.

songs.title: Word to Miles
songs.note: Named as a favorite from the album, described as appropriately titled.

songs.title: Deicidal Tendencies
songs.note: A ripper from the debut album, showing kickass riffs and ultra-technical, sludgy grindy energy.

songs.title: Blood Faucet
songs.note: A ripper from the debut album that shows the band's strengths in riffs and dynamics.

songs.title: River Keep Runnin'
songs.note: The album standout, a powerful anthemic soul tune that brings to mind Mavis Staples.

songs.title: It's Gonna Be Alright
songs.note: A slower, uplifting song where Lang reminds listeners that times are gonna change.

songs.title: Ride This Train
songs.note: Closes the album with hopeful lyrics and a New Orleans brass band reprise.

songs.title: Do You Need A Veterinarian?
songs.note: A standout from the Mutant Mayhem score that the writer says slaps, bound to enthrall NIN fans.

songs.title: I Just Met You and You Almost Killed Me
songs.note: Highlighted as a slapping track from the Mutant Mayhem score alongside the lead pick.

songs.title: Attack On a Titan
songs.note: A standout driven by minimal, NES-styled synths that the writer says will appeal to chiptune heads.

songs.title: Landlines
songs.note: Opens We Buy Diabetic Test Strips with backwards tape loops and glitchy flecks, then adds live instrumentation.

songs.title: Woke Up And Asked Siri How I'm Gonna Die
songs.note: Key cut where billy woods raps on personal and worldly wounds, with a head-spinning lyrical style.

songs.title: we should have made otherground a thing
songs.note: Tropicalia-leaning track where Mike recalls underground memories, including P.E.A.C.E. from Freestyle Fellowship.

songs.title: i bled on stage at first ave
songs.note: Opener on another triumph of ghetto engineering, with humming funk production by Quelle Chris.

songs.title: BET's rap city
songs.note: Illingsworth's warm sepia-toned production backs throwback rap lyrics from Mike and Young Zee.

songs.title: WFLD32
songs.note: Lolling, static-embossed track with production by Kenny Segal.

songs.title: Star Struck
songs.note: Cornerstone track of No Traffic, mixing heavy bass, synths and hi-hats with a mantra-like statement of intent.

songs.title: Boom Bap
songs.note: Low-end growling track on No Traffic featuring Frank Nitt.

songs.title: Psycho Mantis
songs.note: Early Hair Of The Dog track pairing squelching bass with infectious hand claps.

songs.title: Donte Slip
songs.note: Described as a star-gazing hip-hop lullaby from Hair Of The Dog.

songs.title: Palazzo de Hachazo
songs.note: Penultimate Hair Of The Dog moment with syncopated percussion and a head-nodding bounce.

songs.title: Messages
songs.note: Tender track on Hand Painted Model Trains with wistful synths and metronomic woodblocks.

songs.title: Mirage
songs.note: Closer on Hand Painted Model Trains, described as a frantic stream-of-consciousness eulogy.

songs.title: Sunrise Rituals
songs.note: Opener on the Family EP with a blissful flute-infused groove and guest SALIMATA.

songs.title: Lemonade
songs.note: Piano-led track on the Family EP where lojii recalls rapping over bootleg tapes.

songs.title: Both Sides
songs.note: Described as the standout on Family EP, with Pink Siifu teaming up with SALIMATA.

songs.title: When It's Fast
songs.note: Early track on Libra with a frantic guitar riff and a tempo nodding to Britcore.

songs.title: Everyday Hustle
songs.note: Melodic, swaggering track on Libra about balancing creativity with nine-to-five and family life.

songs.title: The Deep
songs.note: Apocalyptic posse cut on Libra featuring Junior Disprol, Chrome and Specifik.

songs.title: Flames
songs.note: Brooding track on Libra where Farma G brings worldly smarts.

songs.title: Lucky Number
songs.note: Subtly forbidding Libra track where Lewis Parker interpolates classic BDP for the hook.

songs.title: Belly
songs.note: Early Stacking Chips moment over wormy bass, with Zilla referencing KMD, Big Pun and Soul II Soul.

songs.title: Love Is DOOMed
songs.note: Album's conceptual centerpiece, a relationship rap where Zilla skips a date to watch an MF Doom lecture.

songs.title: Blind (Fred Everything Remixes)
songs.note: Katlego Matseke's South African deep house track, remixed by Fred Everything, with vocals by Kristina Sheli; a slow-burning bittersweet dream for connoisseur parties.

songs.title: Mixed Feelings
songs.note: Described as a sugar-sweet pop vocal and vintage trance track, with a fun, fist-pumping EP around it; not named explicitly as a focus track.

songs.title: &JUST&NIGE&MARK&G (Justin Harris remix)
songs.note: Pure acid house remix from Bournemouth producer, praised as the pick of its remix bunch for its euphoric piano riff and momentum.

songs.title: Amaskengman (Ikonika remix)
songs.note: Dutch grime producer's track on DRMTRK, given an ebullient, pitch-bend-happy remix by Ikonika that closes the release.

songs.title: Red Hots (Splurt Diablo remix)
songs.note: A super-trippy, seasick, techno-adjacent remake of Red Hots by Splurt Diablo, the alias of UK grime MC Merky Ace.

songs.title: Azabache
songs.note: Gothic-electronic album from an Asturias-born, London-based multimedia artist, moving from inhuman landscapes to tentative human voices.

songs.title: Grind – Slow Mix
songs.note: Slow, sleazy Toronto electro track from the Grind EP, with muttered vocals and detuned tones, feeling like an endless weird party.

songs.title: Duck & Cover
songs.note: Chunky big beat and p-funk track with cheeky spoken samples cut and scratched through squelch; described as party central.

songs.title: Don't Go to the Disco
songs.note: Companion track with fun voiceovers, more repetition and vocoder, on the same two-track release.

songs.title: Do You Worst
songs.note: Ethereal pop-imbued track about realizing a friendship or relationship needs to end; one of the writer's favorites.

songs.title: Far Far Away
songs.note: A Pete Shelley tribute singled out as a standout where the band leans into the rapturous purity of a great pop song.

songs.title: Greatest Hits Radio
songs.note: Singled out with "Far Far Away" as a sticky pop song where the band really shines.

songs.title: Markin' It Down
songs.note: Satirizes algorithm-driven music taste, contrasting it with a record store clerk recommending Fall, Can, and Kleenex.

songs.title: Infirmary
songs.note: A-side of a 12-inch split with Burial, opening with jazzy piano that gives way to delicate footwork drums and a stutter-y bass drop.

songs.title: Unknown Summer
songs.note: A 10-minute split track built on staticky four-on-the-floor percussion and a humming vocal sample, with a teenage voice appearing.

songs.title: cycli infini
songs.note: An almost 40-minute piece built on tape loops and a circle-of-fifths progression, featuring flute, saxophone, and pedal steel.

songs.title: You're Never Useless
songs.note: Described as deconstructed calypso, with recognizable rhythms sped up and set whirling against a grainy textural layer. Reviewer calls it pure fun that rewards close listening.

songs.title: Now Go Out
songs.note: Balances a gleeful cascade of synths and bubble-pop percussion with moments of lovely repose.

songs.title: Chop
songs.note: Rhythmic notes hang in the air, sparkling like the finale of a planetarium light show.

songs.title: Obedience to Authority Figures
songs.note: The reviewer's listening notes describe it as feeling like auditory poppers.

songs.title: Wake Up To Your House
songs.note: A softer, slower reimagining of a song originally on Pantheon of Me, opening The Mystery School.

songs.title: They Start The Dance
songs.note: A slow-burning rendition from The Mystery School, followed by the haunting track "Cherry".

songs.title: Hard to Please
songs.note: Mazy Fly's song taken to grand, atmospheric heights, with synths replaced by shimmering piano and strings.

songs.title: Oh The Glamour
songs.note: A sparkling ode to Black and queer communities creating celebration and luxury even when times are hard.

songs.title: Running Blind
songs.note: A classic house track about the soul-fortifying qualities of the dancefloor, reaching big ecstatic heights.

songs.title: Mine O Mine
songs.note: A collab where Aluna explores her self-worth, offering a refreshingly honest take on resilience and independence.

songs.title: Hazer
songs.note: Its bloody, unsettling video nails the music's bug-eyed chaos and perverse sense of humor.

songs.title: Permanently Closed
songs.note: A gabber-style track where a breathy, cotton-candy vocal drifts to the surface of the chaos.

songs.title: Debtors Prison Click Here Disney Needs To See This
songs.note: Without its synth and drum storm, it could be a dreampop ballad, and it addresses capitalism's ravages.

songs.title: Sun Showers
songs.note: Bottom-heavy production and dynamic sleights of hand make this one of the standouts on Alchemy.

songs.title: Go The Distance
songs.note: Samples and dynamic production tie its sugar-high hooks together, setting it apart on Alchemy.

songs.title: Moon Song
songs.note: A psychedelic single carried by ethereal vocals and dreamy guitar, the album's standout track.

songs.title: Amsale Manefesha
songs.note: A lushly textured, entirely instrumental track that closes the album.

songs.title: Perfect Blue
songs.note: The title track, with fuzzy guitars and Adamu singing about changing for someone he loves.

songs.title: Cream of the Crop
songs.note: Teeter-totter guitars and a pounding rhythm section back Tika Hall's livid howl over controlled chaos.

songs.title: Punk City USA
songs.note: A catchy track whose refrain about bad energy has stuck in the writer's head for weeks.

songs.title: Constant State
songs.note: Two-song release; power-pop pace with bright hooks, and the post says The Ramones are a major influence.

songs.title: P.C.H
songs.note: Vocalist Charlotte Gigi wields an aggressive voice over urgent '80s riffs.

songs.title: Tangled in Joy
songs.note: Effervescent, jangly '80s-style pop love song from their long-awaited debut full-length.

songs.title: Eraser
songs.note: Lead single showing the band's impeccable pacing, anthemic vocals, and sticky hooks.

songs.title: Shadow Me
songs.note: Girl group-y track on their sophomore LP, showing singer Lira Mondal's versatile voice.

songs.title: Petit Four
songs.note: Raw, funky track compared to Bush Tetras, highlighting the band's wider-ranging sound.

songs.title: The Third War
songs.note: Sung in Tunisian Arabic; predicts or threatens global mayhem from ongoing violence and death.

songs.title: Lies
songs.note: Closing track described as a distorted, tense dirge and perhaps the release's standout.

songs.title: Vento Triste
songs.note: Explosive opener with machine-gun drums and shouted vocals about feeling dead inside.

songs.title: Oltre Lo Sguardo
songs.note: Guitar takes on a psychedelic, almost surf-y tone on this track.

songs.title: Canzone Della Foresta
songs.note: Soaring, ringing guitar notes make this one of the strongest tracks, a desolate ode to rain.

songs.title: Garland
songs.note: Energetic highlight with laser-like synth lines and propulsive drumming in gloomy post-punk.

songs.title: Blood Chokes
songs.note: Named the most impactful track on Be My Vengeance, a cathartic celebration of trans resilience and found family.

songs.title: NBC's Chris Angel
songs.note: Cited as an example of weary resignation on FOHDH, with wobbly bass and choral vocals over gravelly delivery.

songs.title: Rib Cage
songs.note: A persistent beat shifts into a shuddering sound, from dragonfly-wing flutter to a troubled car engine.

songs.title: Feeding Time
songs.note: Warbles, whistles, and whirrs suggest curious animals in a windy desert environment.

songs.title: Spines
songs.note: Humid feel with crackling like a late summer storm and a discordant, ominous melodic element.

songs.title: 10 Mach 11's
songs.note: Reworks Biggie's Come On over thick funk synths, with Tree praising his crew and dismissing imposters.

songs.title: Benz
songs.note: Rides a vintage Southern bounce beat, with Tree joyfully and convincingly repeating the Benz hook.
A favorite from the debut EP, turning emergency vehicle sounds into an infectious hook.

songs.title: Airforce blue
songs.note: Lead single pairing autotuned vocals with bedroom pop production; called another favorite.

songs.title: Wishing well
songs.note: Closes the EP with an unrequited-love song over glistening piano keys and an abrupt ending.

songs.title: III
songs.note: Roxanne and Piñeyro trade Dean Blunt-style verses over a trap-laced beat.

songs.title: The Veil II
songs.note: Carried by sparse acoustic guitar playing and otherworldly chimes, with nothing else.

songs.title: Natural Wonder Beauty Concept
songs.note: Its title track pairs an uptempo jungle groove with slow-motion vocal chops; called one of the year's best electronic tracks.

songs.title: Three Drums
songs.note: A blissful downtempo track that Kieran Hebden put out this year, after his dance-heavy festival run.

songs.title: Darkness, Darkness
songs.note: The A-side, built on loping drums, dry horn samples, and distorted guitar jamming.

songs.title: No Services
songs.note: The withdrawn back half, an ambient piece of resonant piano chords over faint fretboard scraping.

songs.title: Child of Venus
songs.note: Dream-pop opener with airy atmosphere and lyrics about transitions and trauma; standout tracks include "Still", "Photographs" and "Ghosts".

songs.title: Nos Habet Caramel
songs.note: Cairo DJ/producer's debut blends global club styles with Egyptian music; highlights include "Bingo", "Ghaltet Meen" and "Mesh Marshmallow".

songs.title: Kufi Conversations
songs.note: Gorgeous Jefe and Lord RA collaborate on upbeat, optimistic rap; standout tracks include "The Touch", "UNICO" and "Toy Gunz".

songs.title: DITELAN BUMI
songs.note: Singaporean punks' economical, live-sounding set of under ten minutes; highlights the title track and "Mayat".

songs.title: Hit Record
songs.note: Montreal band blends post-punk leanness with garage swagger; described as sparky, dynamic, melody-driven rock.

songs.title: Disruptive Frequencies
songs.note: Compilation of Black and South Asian experimental and electronic artists; highlights Bantu's "Dark Energy" and Poulomi Desai's "The Vichitra".

songs.title: Overtime
songs.note: A euphoric, future-forward track on Pancakes that the post says goes extremely hard.

songs.title: Tainted
songs.note: A gentler, tender piece showing the softer side of the Pancakes album.

songs.title: Presence
songs.note: Melodic bass and celestial pads interrupted by metallic effects and a half-spoken vocal, sounding songwriterly and human.

songs.title: Morning Chatter
songs.note: A blissful track that the post says still carries a core of unease and melancholy.

songs.title: Hanif Reads Toni
songs.note: Opens the album with poet Hanif Abdurraqqib reading a passage from Toni Morrison's Jazz.

songs.title: Run Run Run
songs.note: A bittersweet, energetic standout where Dixon recounts joyful and dark childhood moments.

songs.title: Beloved! Paradise! Jazz!?
songs.note: The soulful title track that closes the album, with Dixon singing about feeling fixed.

songs.artist: Abbott Jackson, Swizzy, and Red Amandala
songs.title: Love Runs for Free
songs.note: The vocals share the bounce and swing of Jackson's smoky jazz arrangement.

songs.artist: Abbott Jackson, Swizzy, and Red Amandala
songs.title: Passionate
songs.note: An album highlight where the two rappers ride a cascade of marimba and snare.

songs.title: Scars
songs.note: An upbeat synth-driven standout on Guy, with lyrics about growth and her father's hardships.

songs.title: Meant to Be
songs.note: A disco track on Guy where Jayda G declares she is Black from the start.

songs.title: When She Dance
songs.note: A tribute to her grandmother, built from archival recordings of her late father.

songs.title: Doppelgänger
songs.note: A pillowy, sophisticated arrangement that shows the band's sprawling, fluid sound on Hagata.

songs.title: Hoppe
songs.note: An unpredictable, rowdy track on Hagata that contrasts with the band's more serene side.

songs.title: Rounds
songs.note: Pianist Awadagin Pratt improvises his own cadenza on this stirring piece, a practice the post links to Beethoven and Liszt.

songs.title: Code
songs.note: Fiery glassy piano runs trade with upper strings in a soloistic-ensemble dialogue before Roomful of Teeth enter dramatically.

songs.title: Time Past, Time Future
songs.note: Left-handed piano gestures bring jazz roots and a hammering rhythm that the post compares to Horace Silver.

songs.title: Untitled Composition for Piano and Eight Voices
songs.note: Brooding piano chords are set against harrowing, wordless vocal harmonies, described as deliciously stark.

songs.title: Wolke über Bäumen
songs.note: Violinist Sarah Saviet plays gut strings, a baroque bow, and scordatura retuned 32 times over sixteen minutes.

songs.title: Farewell to Piano
songs.note: Featured among the album's equally riveting works, with the post linking to the track.

songs.title: Falter
songs.note: Named as one of the riveting works rounding out Sarah Saviet's album, with the post linking to the track.

songs.title: Apartment Sounds
songs.note: Violin part is organized around clock ticking, porch chimes, and window ambience, using scratch tones and pizzicato.

songs.title: Tooth and Nail
songs.note: Synthetic patterns trace structures that Yvonne Lam's crystalline articulation inhabits beautifully; originally written for Nadia Sirota.

songs.title: Rest These Hands
songs.note: No electronic part; Lam reads a brief poem by the composer's mother with world-weary wisdom in her intonation.

songs.title: Remote Sensing on the Beach
songs.note: Norwegian fjord recordings and sonified 3D coastal maps carry the listener from shore into the sea, with hydrophone sounds.

songs.title: Mundiglossia
songs.note: Solo soprano saxophone piece by Thomas Giles, built on extended techniques and a spiral structure over about 30 minutes.

songs.title: Quantum Suicide
songs.note: An R&B crooner built on smooth production, with lyrics that touch on depression and darker subject matter.

songs.title: Shed That Fear
songs.note: An anthemic track urging listeners to shed fear of death and live their lives the right way.

songs.title: Workers Interlude
songs.note: A soul-stirring track where Marcus Brown turns his sights on capitalism.

songs.title: Unbreak My Love
songs.note: A triumphant closer that the writer compared to early '90s Sounds of Blackness releases.

songs.title: Is This Where The Party Is?
songs.note: A sugary garage-punk rock and roll title track with pathos beneath its party vibes, likened to the Bangles meeting Ex Hex.

songs.title: Slo Pokes
songs.note: Stik Figa takes aim at MCs who are all flash and no substance, turning clichés into pithy career advice.

songs.title: Zambezi Zinger
songs.note: A jubilant track with Tanya Morgan's Donwill and Von Pea, featuring a playful tweak of Nas's "Oochie Wally."

songs.title: Yah's Shorthand
songs.note: A ruminative track where Stik Figa wrestles with his own contradictions, called the album's most devastating moment.

songs.title: CORNBALLS OF EARTH
songs.note: Filtered space jazz loop backs Vice gazing into a blunted galaxy and pondering his standing.

songs.title: Reach Out
songs.note: Described as a nostalgia-drenched throwback session on the Yacht Club Vol. 2 release.

songs.title: Key West
songs.note: Spun into a mini-travelogue, per the post, within the relaxed summer-themed album.

songs.title: Cook
songs.note: Bernz pushes the seductive nature of his culinary skills across this track.

songs.title: Sea Breeze
songs.note: Airy synth gusts carry Bernz's boast about flowing on his own reef.

songs.title: For How Much?
songs.note: Twists 80s R&B melody around crackling snares and kicks.

songs.title: Downs Got Up
songs.note: Powered by a bluesy low-end riff, per the post.

songs.title: The Black Surf
songs.note: Ventures into blissful psychedelic territory with guest vocals from Quelle Chris.

songs.title: Ain't Nobody Coming Down To Save You
songs.note: Crunching blues-rock with gospel touches delivers an end-of-days charge; a mid-album peak.

songs.title: Time
songs.note: Gentle introductory statement over a jazz-inflected backdrop and chugging mid-tempo drums.

songs.title: Guardian Angel
songs.note: Revisits going through school with an elder sibling, a personal track.

songs.title: Retrospect
songs.note: Embraces dwelling on the past to reach present-time satisfaction.

songs.title: Raised
songs.note: Explores the MC's own formative years.

songs.title: I Am Reuben
songs.note: Title track featuring archived vocals from his late brother Reuben over ominous keys.

songs.title: Gomba Slap
songs.note: Spotlights Tamás Czirják's forceful drum work.

songs.title: Mosquitoh
songs.note: A woozy showcase for Bencze Molnár's off-kilter synth patterns.

songs.title: When It Hits
songs.note: Carried by Viktor Sági's lolling basslines.

songs.title: Up In The Clouds
songs.note: Closes the album with feathery brushes and dreamy celestial synths.

songs.title: Love is Love
songs.note: Atonal, piano-spiked track featuring Sheek Louch with minimalist atmospherics.

songs.title: Masked Up
songs.note: Almost industrial-tinged experimental sortie in the Signature set.

songs.title: Uncle Chris Car
songs.note: Album-setter where hazy bass spurs Ortiz to revisit his pre-rap days.

songs.title: Dearly Departed
songs.note: Opener mixing reflective sentiments with cut-throat barbs over mid-tempo beatwork.

songs.title: Best Nonfiction
songs.note: Mid-project cut with guest support from IAMGAWD over pillowy bass and serene synths.

songs.title: Consistent
songs.note: Mystically-charged closer with a guest turn from Angelenah.

songs.title: Ease Side
songs.note: Key cut with thudding drums and swaying guitar, warning against unguided missteps.

songs.title: Human Kindness (Acoustic Mix)
songs.note: Ends the album in sonic curveball fashion, venturing into experimental folk.

songs.title: Renni Bes
songs.note: Hints at UK garage and classic Detroit techno with heavy Reese bass drone and funky drum clatter.

songs.title: Seek
songs.note: Bass-heavy track using a gospel preacher over a heavy drum track, with physical, fresh sound.

songs.title: Acid 13
songs.note: Lifts you up on warm pads while digital spirits sing; one of the two standout electro-leaning tunes.

songs.title: Flight to Mars
songs.note: Plots out a darker, more isolationist groove; a standout electro-leaning tune.

songs.title: Granulate
songs.note: Skittering stepper whose rhythm sometimes settles into four-to-the-floor before splitting into funkier patterns.

songs.title: Vector Space
songs.note: Sparse rhythm over a holding thrum, described as the real treat of the release.

songs.title: I Miss Your Love
songs.note: Loving reconstruction of 1980s Chicago house with a church-y, joyous dancefloor feel.

songs.title: Azotandote
songs.note: Listed as a standout track from this month's electronic picks.

songs.title: Never Say Never
songs.note: Melancholic electropop with a futurist twist, with Kiffie's gentle vocals and Edward Spark's production.

songs.title: Eerie Nostalgia
songs.note: Berlin trio's lush, dark punk debut full-length; highlights include the updated closer "Echoes" and "Asleep". Released as an album, so the focus track is not clearly

songs.title: Raw Liquid Power
songs.note: Glaswegian quartet's first studio EP, a fun, catchy follow-up to their 2022 demo, with the track "Stilettos" singled out.

songs.artist: Eye of the Cormorant/Eye of the Heron
songs.title: S/T
songs.note: Donna Allen's lo-fi bird-centric anarcho-punk demo, raw and energetic, with the first part named for the cormorant.

songs.title: Gelap Gempita
songs.note: Central Java duo's political electronic punk album, with the standout track "Tanam Kemandirian" praised for its soaring vocals.

songs.title: Spiral Dub
songs.note: San Francisco six-piece psych-punk act; highlights include "Top of the World", "Hang From the Line", and "Knockin' on My Head".
A tense, propulsive track where one player's spare plucks sit inside the other's rapid notes, seeming to escape time.

songs.title: Reichwaltz
songs.note: The busier track from Pozin's electronics album, twisting through fast-pulsing oscillations and shifting rhythms.

songs.title: Schlafkulture
songs.note: A higher-toned, more meditative track from Pozin's solo electronics album, balancing minimalism with glitch.

songs.title: Etude 2
songs.note: A darting, pin-prick piece that injects burning edges into the reserved, tense duo material.

songs.title: Flow
songs.note: The album closer, where both musicians explore the full range of their instruments in an original piece.

songs.title: Improvisation II
songs.note: A 17-minute improvisation where the trio loosens up more than elsewhere on the Oliveros-inspired album.

songs.artist: B L A C K I E
songs.title: still got love
songs.note: A punchy, curt MC-mode blast that opens a distilled project of motivational mantras and lyrical catharsis.

songs.artist: B L A C K I E
songs.title: born inside excrement
songs.note: The penultimate cut, driven by growling bass tones, with the MC urging listeners to forget what hurts.

songs.title: fish don't climb trees
songs.note: The opening title track, heralded by a muted horn riff, showing the MC's drifting, abstract wanderlust.

songs.title: Grey Theory
songs.note: A vital moment with craggy drums and wavering keys, where the MC sketches out blurred boundary lines.

songs.title: Mirrors
songs.note: The closer, where the host admits to old soul aspirations and claims his sound is vintage.

songs.title: Could Be
songs.note: The melancholic opener, with a pained vocal sample over crackling mid-tempo drums and subdued brass.

songs.title: Lemons
songs.note: A swaying, Latin-tinged instrumental standout from the project.

songs.title: City Rhodes
songs.note: A skewed and hazy instrumental standout described as a highlight of the album.

songs.title: Breeze
songs.note: A gently weeping instrumental standout from the album.

songs.title: Thank You Very Much
songs.note: Closer featuring Lynx 196.9 and his aqueous, ear-catching flow.

songs.title: East Hollywood
songs.note: An early moment carried by a mournful, sad-clown piano riff full of lonesome regret.

songs.title: The 6th Floor
songs.note: Described as humid, humming guitar-based violence over a noir-leaning beatscape.

songs.title: Think Pieces
songs.note: A tornado of pained atmospherics built around an incantation from Sharif referencing many odd touchstones.

songs.title: Diamond Gem
songs.note: Showcases Son Raw's sweeping orchestral strings across the album's expansive beats.

songs.title: Maintain
songs.note: Static-encrusted funk production highlighted in the album's varied beat work.

songs.title: Simple Man
songs.note: Features bluesy sax riffs over crackly boom-bap drums.

songs.title: The General
songs.note: Five Steez declares his worth as a veteran and pushes his contribution to Jamaica's underground scene.

songs.title: Dub Outro
songs.note: Closes the album in a sticky mix of sound system effects and echo-inflected sirens.

songs.title: Jazz Dreamin
songs.note: Scene-setting opener blending cushy keys and a melancholic sax refrain with a Biggie vocal snippet.

songs.title: Jazz From The Soul
songs.note: Delves into meditative, deeper territory on the album's jazz theme.

songs.title: Vibrations In Your Mind
songs.note: A woozy track that weaves in spiritual jazz influences.

songs.title: Step Into A World
songs.note: KRS-One-inspired track featuring Amber Navran of Moonchild on two installments.

songs.title: Eight Pregnancy Scares
songs.note: An early moment where a missed love is reminisced over and chided by the MC's own intentions.

songs.title: Angela Bassett
songs.note: Shows the MC's confident, amiable tone, name-checking Grand Puba and Brand Nubian.

songs.title: COACH K & PEE
songs.note: A deep funk outing with U'nik Flow guesting on verses.

songs.title: END CREDITS 2.5
songs.note: A glitchy funk track where the host brags about keeping it player.

songs.title: LOWKEY AND OUT THE WAY
songs.note: Bedded by subdued keys, with Blackchai skating over the beat.

songs.title: OSBORN WAVECAP
songs.note: S!LENCE adds to the aqueous ambiance of this track.
A key late-album song questioning where the love is, with a meditative mid-tempo feel.

songs.title: ThePlugTune
songs.note: Whistle-imbued opener that establishes the Native Tongues inspiration behind the project.

songs.title: BabyTalk
songs.note: Drifts in a woozy big band direction, showcasing Controller 7's melodic sensibilities.

songs.title: GoodBye
songs.note: Heralded by dreamy cinematic strings.

songs.title: LongTermPlans
songs.note: Treads through classic soul territory.

songs.title: PassingLane
songs.note: An 80s-tinged track featuring Dessa.

songs.title: BeesKnees
songs.note: Kooky, naturalistic funk with Iowa Rockwell on the track.

songs.title: PardonInterruptions
songs.note: MC Paul Barman teams with Open Mike Eagle, weaving in a De La Soul deep cut reference.

songs.title: Drowning Poet
songs.note: A askew, time-warping meditation where tones seem to bend like taffy, performed by the Anagram String Trio.

songs.title: Ensembletje!
songs.note: A gorgeous quartet piece named for the performing group, which includes the composer on electronics.

songs.title: this is a place where i can sit with clarity
songs.note: Title piece, a solo organ work with drone-like qualities and simple melodic shapes drifting through sustained tones.

songs.title: Les si doux redoux
songs.note: Basset horn piece evoking a slight winter thaw, casting an undulating, shimmering shadow rather than nature's violence.

songs.title: Black on Green
songs.note: A visceral piece for bassist Charlotte Testu conveying a tornado approaching, with a tightly wound sense of dread.

songs.title: Nacarat
songs.note: An epic for electric guitarist Serge Teyssot-Gay evoking a hurricane, though the review finds its structure predictable.

songs.title: Augun
songs.note: A deconstruction of an Icelandic folk tune, recast in a tangle of colliding harmony and rhythm, performed by Ashley Bathgate.

songs.title: Assemble
songs.note: Evokes a chorale, treating eight tracks as an orchestral arrangement whose parts make sense only when voiced together.

songs.title: Willow's Song
songs.note: A brief, lush piece taken from a larger work, reconfigured for cellist Ashley Bathgate as a prelude.

songs.title: Shimmer
songs.note: A cycling, minimalist work of endlessly morphing permutations of a pattern, with lines taking on a life of their own.

songs.title: Dementia
songs.note: Electro-acoustic piece where motifs become increasingly splintered and disconnected, reflecting the mental decay of the disease.

songs.title: Recovery
songs.note: Aims to sonify the halting steps of recovery, with sonic tension transforming into a drifting serenity.

songs.title: Mini-bestiaire pour la fin du monde
songs.note: Synthesizer melodies snake within abstract whooshes and crunches, suggesting elusive thematic development.

songs.title: Impromptu[e]
songs.note: Uses cello sounds from cellist Lara Laverdure, twisted and chopped up, as source material for a rigorous composition.

songs.title: Trash Trio
songs.note: A choreography-based work where timbres and rhythms shift with each performer's pace and noisemaking detritus.

songs.title: Hair Score
songs.note: A deeply personal piece made from traced hair patterns, performed as a memorial to their late mother with tin cans.

songs.title: Stones
songs.note: A brief open-ended Christian Wolff work where the crew produces shifting sonic mosaics from stones found in a cave.

songs.title: Inside the Ritual
songs.note: An ambulatory ambient piece dominated by crickets, cowbells, footsteps, vocal incantations, and hichiriki flute.

songs.title: Quilt City Blues
songs.note: Linked as a track by pianist Jon Cowherd, a familiar collaborator on Brian Blade's Kings Highway.

songs.title: La Balada dels Perduts
songs.note: Highlighted as a standout from several July releases by Barcelona label Underpool, recommended for checking out.

songs.title: 28 Tables and Tapes
songs.note: Linked as a track featuring turntablist DJ Illvibe, who adds textures to a playful jazz take on Beethoven.

songs.title: Scourged at Dawn
songs.note: Sits within Galgendood's all-consuming darkness, with scant squirming melodies that the post says extend the album's gloom.

songs.title: Bog Bodies Near the Humid Crypt
songs.note: Another track whose faint melodies the post says feel like part of the album's unsettling, shadowed atmosphere.

songs.title: Daguerreotype
songs.note: Praised for rich melodicism and stop-start rhythmic madness, showing the band's range on Conflagrations.

songs.title: EarthRecycle
songs.note: An ambient-industrial oddity that the post cites as part of Rannoch's range on Conflagrations.

songs.title: Threnody to a Dying Star
songs.note: Album-closing 17-minute epic with dense interplay and powerful riffing that the post calls elite-level.

songs.title: Blast Furnace
songs.note: A loosie from the band's new release, with a fat midtempo groove and memorable riffs the post calls eternal.

songs.title: Standoff
songs.note: The B-side loosie that the post says spends more time barreling full speed with memorable riffs and full-bodied tones.

songs.title: Moss Covered Bones on the Altar of the Moon
songs.note: A towering mid-album epic that the post says pushes the Blackbraid project to its highest peaks yet.

songs.title: A Song of Death on Winds of Dawn
songs.note: A second towering mid-album epic on Blackbraid II that the post highlights as a high point.

songs.title: Der Hafen 1
songs.note: Dark, reverberant track where Olive shapes Schiefner's prepared tapes and mixer feedback into eerie portraits.

songs.title: Der Hafen 2
songs.note: Olive uses magnetic pickups and tuning forks, prompting Schiefner to build varied, confrontational clanging noise.

songs.title: One
songs.note: Instrumental rock track with fiery energy, opening World Views from a former Pere Ubu member.

songs.title: Conversations in an Ancient Forest
songs.note: Graham turns horn bleats into a field of noise on this track from I Continue.

songs.title: You Know That I Will Never Give Up
songs.note: High-pitched dissonance bounces around like comets, filling the track with cosmic-feeling sound.

songs.title: Transform
songs.note: A ping-pong-gone-wrong piece with fast, frantic repetitions and bright, high-energy tones.

songs.title: Superconscious
songs.note: A harried, neuron-firing fusion of man and machine that the writer especially admires.

songs.title: Luna
songs.note: A skewed clip built on Scranton's idiosyncratic internal rhythm, opening Body Pillow.

songs.title: Big Glider
songs.note: A swinging lope that adds to the rhythmic momentum of Body Pillow's early tracks.

songs.title: Tricks in the Air
songs.note: Described as the Residents setting up a laboratory in Autechre's basement; the album's intoxicating culmination.

songs.title: Trash Trio
songs.note: Cacophonous opener made in a Czech cave with siblings, rattling metal and echoing physical movements.

songs.title: Hair Score
songs.note: Harrowing hums and moans that deal with the passing of Vítková's mother.

songs.title: Stones
songs.note: A Christian Wolff composition where rocks are clacked together in a downpour of rhythm.

songs.title: Inside the Ritual
songs.note: Recorded in a Slovakian church, a 23-minute closer blending reality and dreams through voice and flute.

songs.title: The Sky Over Petrograd
songs.note: A 15-minute cloud of repetition, noise, and churn that the writer calls particularly impressive.
